The chat screen currently only shows messages on initial load and manual refresh. After sending a message via WebSocket JSON-RPC, the user has to scroll or hit refresh to see the assistant's response.

- Keep the WebSocket connection open in ChatScreen instead of opening/closing per message
- Listen for streaming response events and update the message list reactively
- Use Riverpod for reactive state management of messages
- Auto-scroll to bottom as new content streams in

### Files to Change
- lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart
- lib/core/services/ws_client.dart
- Possibly add a streaming provider

title: fix: Session creation bypasses WS — opens new chat directly (closes #36)
body:
Closes #36

### Root cause
The dashboard WebSocket endpoint blocks connections from non-loopback IPs. The Android phone connects from the LAN (192.168.x.x), not 127.0.0.1, so WS calls fail with "Connection closed".

### Fix
New sessions no longer use  over WebSocket. Instead:
- Name dialog → generates UUID → navigates directly to ChatScreen
- The agent creates/persists the session implicitly on first message send
- No WS dependency, no auth token needed for session creation
- Instant navigation, no loading spinner needed

title: fix: Handle 404 for new sessions + clearer WS error
body:
### Fixes

- New sessions (fresh UUID) no longer show 'session not found 404' — empty chat state shown instead
- WebSocket 'Connection closed' error now explains the root cause: dashboard blocks WS from non-localhost IPs
- Added mounted guards before setState in async callbacks

### Server-side requirement

The dashboard WebSocket endpoint only accepts connections from localhost (127.0.0.1, ::1). From the Android phone on LAN, WS connections are rejected. To enable full chat functionality, the dashboard needs to allow LAN WebSocket connections.

title: fix: Use session.create instead of session.resume (fixes session not found)
body:
### Root cause
`session.resume` only works for sessions currently active in the gateway process. Sessions from the REST API (created via CLI or previous gateway instances) aren't known to the current gateway, so `session.resume` returns "session not found".

### Fix
Use `session.create` with the `session_id` parameter instead. This starts a new agent process for the given session, whether it's new or existing. Added `createOrResumeSession()` to WsClient for this purpose.

### Affected
- All sessions (new and existing) — both were failing with "session not found"
- Both WS streaming path and REST fallback path

title: feat: HTTPS support for remote hosting (HF Spaces, Tailscale HTTPS, etc.)
body:
## Summary

Adds HTTPS support so the Android app can connect to Hermes instances behind HTTPS reverse proxies -- specifically Hugging Face Spaces, but also Cloudflare, Nginx, Tailscale HTTPS, etc.

## Problem

The app hardcoded `http://` everywhere:
- `connection.dart`: `baseUrl` was always `http://`
- `main.dart`: validation and API key update both built URLs as `http://$host:$port`
- `DashboardClient`: hardcoded `http://$host:$port`

This blocked connecting to HF Spaces (which serves HTTPS on 443) and any other HTTPS-hosted Hermes instance.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/core/models/connection.dart` | Detect `https://` prefix, default port 443 for HTTPS, add `useHttps` bool to model |
| `lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart` | Pass `useHttps` through `saveConnection` and `updateApiKey`; `DashboardClient` accepts `useHttps` |
| `lib/main.dart` | Use `conn.baseUrl` (scheme-aware) instead of hardcoded `http://` |
| `lib/core/screens/cron_screen.dart` | Pass `useHttps` to `DashboardClient` |
| `lib/core/screens/memory_screen.dart` | Pass `useHttps` to `DashboardClient` |
| `lib/core/screens/settings_screen.dart` | Pass `useHttps` to `DashboardClient` |
| `lib/core/screens/skills_screen.dart` | Pass `useHttps` to `DashboardClient` |

## How to use with HF Spaces

Enter your Space URL with `https://` prefix:
- **Host:** `https://your-space.hf.space`
- **Port:** `443` (or leave blank, it auto-detects)
- **API Key:** your `GATEWAY_TOKEN`

The app automatically detects HTTPS, switches the scheme, and defaults to port 443.

## Backward compatibility

Existing HTTP connections continue to work unchanged. The `useHttps` field defaults to `false` in `fromMap`, so old saved connections are unaffected.

title: fix: omit default ports from baseUrl to avoid proxy issues
body:
## Problem

The merged HTTPS support (v1.0.4) generates base URLs with explicit default ports. For example, when a user enters `https://f4b404-hermes.hf.space` with port 443, the app produces `https://f4b404-hermes.hf.space:443`.

The Dart http package sends the explicit port in the Host header (e.g. `Host: f4b404-hermes.hf.space:443`). Some reverse proxies (HF Spaces / Cloudflare) do not expect the default port in the Host header and may return 401 or 404.

## Fix

Omit the port from the URL when it matches the scheme default:
- `https://host` instead of `https://host:443`
- `http://host` instead of `http://host:80`

Custom non-default ports (e.g. 8443, 8080, 9119) are still included.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/core/models/connection.dart` | `baseUrl` omits default ports |
| `lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart` | `DashboardClient._buildBaseUrl` omits default ports |

## Backward compatibility

HTTP localhost connections still work. Custom ports still work.

title: Chat messages disappear after streaming: wrong session ID in sendMessageStreaming
body:
## Bug description

Chat messages disappear from the UI within one second of a response being received. The chat history is always empty when opening any session.

## Root cause

`GatewayChatClient.sendMessageStreaming()` posts to `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a freshly generated `mob-{timestamp}-{uuid}` session ID in the `X-Hermes-Session-Id` header. The Hermes API server saves the conversation under that ephemeral ID -- not the session the user opened in the session browser.

When streaming ends, `onDone` calls `_client.getMessages(widget.session.id)`. That fetches messages for the original session (from the session list), which has none. The empty list replaces the optimistically-rendered messages in `_messages`, causing them to vanish.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect to a Hermes server with `API_SERVER_ENABLED=true`.
2. Tap any session from the session list.
3. Send a message and watch the reply stream in.
4. Within ~1 second of the stream finishing, the messages disappear and the chat appears empty.
5. Reopening the session confirms 0 messages.

## Expected behaviour

Messages persist in the UI after streaming completes, and are visible on re-open.

## Actual behaviour

Messages vanish. `GET /api/sessions/{widget.session.id}/messages` returns an empty list because the conversation was saved under a different, ephemeral ID.

## Correct fix

Switch `chat_screen.dart` from `POST /v1/chat/completions` (stateless, wrong endpoint) to `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/chat/stream` -- the purpose-built session streaming endpoint. It:

- Loads history from the correct session before the agent run
- Saves back to the same session row after
- Emits a `run.completed` SSE event with the authoritative turn messages, so `onDone` can hydrate from the event instead of a separate `GET /messages` call

This endpoint has been available since Hermes Agent v0.16.0.

## Environment

- Hermes Android: v1.0.1
- Hermes Agent API server: v0.16.0

title: fix(chat): use session API streaming endpoint to persist history
body:
chat_screen was calling POST /v1/chat/completions (stateless) with a session ID in X-Hermes-Session-Id. The server saved the conversation under that ID, but onDone then fetched GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages where id came from the session browser -- a different row. The GET returned empty, causing messages to vanish within ~1s of streaming.

Fix: switch to POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream, the purpose-built session endpoint that:
- loads history from the correct session row before the agent run
- persists the full conversation back to the same session row after
- delivers the authoritative turn messages in the run.completed SSE event, eliminating the separate GET /messages round-trip entirely

Adds GatewayChatClient.sendMessageStreamingViaSessionApi() that parses the structured session SSE event schema (assistant.delta, tool.started, tool.completed, run.completed) and a static _parseSessionSseFrame() helper for the new event format.

The existing sendMessageStreaming() is kept unchanged with a deprecation note so it can still be used when a session API is unavailable.

Closes #65

title: feat: support password-protected dashboards and configurable dashboard port
body:
## Summary

The dashboard-backed screens (Memory, Cron Jobs, Skills, Settings) previously only worked against an **open** (`--insecure`) dashboard on the default port `9119`, because `DashboardClient` authenticated by scraping the SPA session token from the dashboard homepage — which is only injected in insecure mode.

This PR adds support for **password-protected dashboards** and **non-default dashboard ports**, while keeping the existing open-dashboard behaviour unchanged.

## What changed

- **`DashboardClient` cookie auth.** When dashboard credentials are configured, the client logs in via `POST /auth/password-login` (provider `basic`) and authenticates subsequent `/api/` calls with the returned `hermes_session_at` session cookie — the same mechanism the Hermes desktop client uses. With no credentials it falls back to the existing homepage token scrape, so open dashboards keep working.
- **Configurable dashboard port.** `SavedConnection` gains optional `dashboardPortOverride`, `dashboardUsername`, and `dashboardPassword` fields (persisted; `fromMap` is backward-compatible with existing saved connections). The `dashboardPort` getter honours the override and otherwise keeps the previous default (`9119` for HTTP, the external port for HTTPS).
- **UI.** A collapsible **"Custom dashboard details"** section in the Add Connection dialog (collapsed by default) and a **"Dashboard Login"** entry on each connection's overflow menu. Both validate the dashboard before saving.
- **Robustness.** `DashboardClient` now accepts an injectable `http.Client` (for tests) and de-duplicates concurrent login/token requests so parallel drawer calls trigger a single auth round-trip (the dashboard rate-limits password logins). Updating a connection's API key no longer clears its dashboard settings.

## How dashboard auth works now

```
no credentials set ->  GET /  -> scrape window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__  (open / --insecure dashboard)
credentials set    ->  POST /auth/password-login {provider:"basic",username,password}
                       -> Set-Cookie: hermes_session_at=...  -> sent on every /api/ call
```

## Backward compatibility

- Existing saved connections load unchanged (new fields default to null → previous behaviour).
- No changes to the Gateway API (chat/sessions) path.

## Testing

Added unit tests (`test/connection_manager_test.dart`):

- `SavedConnection`: port override precedence, `toMap`/`fromMap` round-trip, backward-compatible parsing, blank-credential normalisation, `copyWith`.
- `DashboardClient` (via injected `MockClient`): password→cookie login, token-scrape fallback, 401 re-authentication, and bad-credential error.
- `ConnectionManager`: persistence of the new fields, `updateDashboardAuth` set/clear, and API-key updates preserving dashboard settings.

## CODE_QUALITY_CHECKLIST

**Analysis**
- [x] `flutter analyze` — zero errors/warnings (CI runs `--fatal-infos`)
- [x] `flutter pub outdated` — N/A, no dependency changes
- [x] `flutter test` — passes (new tests added)
- [x] `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` — clean build in CI

**Architecture**
- [x] State management consistent (`setState` dialogs, matching existing code)
- [x] No orphaned imports / dead code
- [x] Network calls have visible error-handling paths
- [x] `StatefulWidget` resources disposed (new `TextEditingController`s disposed; the Dashboard Login dialog disposes its controllers on close)
- [x] Streaming/WebSocket lifecycles — N/A, unchanged

**UX**
- [x] Error states are visible (login/validation failures surfaced in the dialogs)
- [x] Loading indicators shown during validation
- [x] Responsive — noted: changes are dialog-based; existing phone/tablet layouts unchanged
- [x] Dark mode — unchanged
- [x] Forms validate and prevent bad submissions (gateway + optional dashboard validation before save)

**Security**
- [x] No secrets committed
- [x] User-provided hosts/URLs normalised before use
- [ ] Sensitive values masked — **noted exception:** the dashboard password is stored in `SharedPreferences` in plaintext, mirroring the existing `apiKey` handling. Migrating both to `flutter_secure_storage` is suggested as a separate follow-up.

**Release**
- [x] Version bumped in `pubspec.yaml` (`1.0.7+107`)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` added/updated
- [x] CI builds a clean APK
- [x] PR links to this checklist (above)

**Manual smoke testing**
- [x] Connect to a Gateway API Server
- [x] Browse sessions
- [x] Send a message and receive a streamed response
- [x] Open Memory/Cron/Skills/Settings against a **basic-auth** dashboard (configured via Dashboard Login)
- [x] Phone layout verified — noted: tablet layout not specifically re-tested for the new dialogs

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- Dashboard password (and the existing API key) are stored unencrypted in `SharedPreferences` — a `flutter_secure_storage` migration would be a good separate PR.
- The dashboard is assumed to be on the same host as the gateway; only the port is configurable, not a separate dashboard host.

title: feat: proxy path prefix and proxied dashboard support
body:
Adds support for Hermes deployments behind a reverse proxy where the
Gateway API and Dashboard share the same host/port but sit under
different URL paths (e.g. `/profile/peter/v1/` for chat,
`/dashboard/api/` for dashboard).

### Changes

- **`SavedConnection`**: new fields `gatewayPrefix`, `dashboardPrefix`,
  and `dashboardProxied` to configure custom API paths and proxy mode.

- **`joinBaseUrl()`**: normalizes a base URL with an optional path
  prefix, used by both `ApiClient` and `DashboardClient`.

- **`ApiClient`**: accepts optional `pathPrefix` parameter so all REST
  calls (sessions, messages, health, chat completions) go through the
  correct proxy path.

- **`DashboardClient`**: accepts `pathPrefix` and `proxied` parameters.
  When `proxied` is true, skips SPA session-token auto-discovery and
  sends clean HTTP requests — the proxy injects `Authorization: Bearer`.

- **UI**: adds an "Advanced / Proxy Settings" collapsible section to
  the connection dialog with fields for gateway path prefix, dashboard
  path prefix, and a "Dashboard behind proxy" toggle.

If a specific voice is chosen, calls `setVoice()` for TTS and derives

title: fix: remember and restore scroll position per session
body:
When leaving and re-entering a chat session, the scroll position is
now restored to where the user was, instead of always jumping to the
bottom (or top, since `_scrollToBottom()` fired before the ListView
was laid out).

### Changes

**`_lastPixels`** — tracks the last known scroll position, updated in
`_onScroll()` on every scroll event. Storing in `dispose()` was
unreliable because `hasClients` is already false when the widget tree
tears down.

**`_savedPositions`** — a static map (`sessionId → pixels`) shared
across `ChatScreen` instances so returning to the same session
restores the previous scroll offset.

**`_fetchMessages()`** — if a saved position exists for the session,
uses `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` to `jumpTo()` the
saved offset after layout completes. On first visit, scrolls to the
bottom as before.

title: Feat/tool card
body:
Groups consecutive tool calls into compact emoji cards instead of
rendering individual tool-bubbles. Tool cards appear during streaming
(via SSE `hermes.tool.progress` events) and persist after the response
completes. Also filters out empty ghost bubbles left behind during
token-by-token streaming.

### Changes

**`_toolMessages`** — a separate state list populated during streaming
via SSE tool-progress events. On stream completion (`onDone`), server
messages with `role: 'tool'` are parsed to extract tool names via
`_extractToolMessages()`.

**`_extractToolMessages()`** — scans the server message list for
`role: 'tool'` entries. Extracts the tool name from the `name` field,
or parses `source="..."` from the content (e.g.
`<untrusted_tool_result source="browser_navigate">`).

**`_toolEmoji()`** — maps tool names to emojis: 🌐 browser, 📄
read_file, ✏️ write_file, 🔍 search, 💻 execute, 🧠 think, 🔧 default.

**`_ToolProgressCard`** — a compact inline widget showing `✅ 🌐 🔍 📄`
(completed) or `⏳ 🌐 🔍` with a spinner (active). Consecutive tool
calls are grouped into separate cards (e.g. `user → 🌐 📄 → assistant →
user → 🔍 → assistant`).

**Empty bubble filter** — assistant messages with empty content are
excluded from the display list, eliminating phantom bubbles during
streaming.

**Real-time streaming** — tools from SSE events that arrive during
streaming are shown immediately, before the server response is
complete. Previously they only appeared after `onDone` or on re-entry.

title: fix: render multimodal session content safely
body:
> **Agent disclosure:** This change was prepared, tested, and submitted by Metis, an AI coding agent, acting on behalf of @ruben2000de. Ruben authorized the contribution and validated the fix on his Pixel 8a.

## Bug Description

Opening a session that contains OpenAI-style multipart message content shows a blank/white chat screen instead of rendering the conversation.

ADB logcat reports:

```text
type 'List<dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'String?' in type cast
#0 _ChatScreenState._buildBody (chat_screen.dart:690)
```

## Root Cause

`ChatScreen` cast every message's `content` field directly to `String?`. Hermes sessions can also contain OpenAI-compatible content arrays, for example text parts and `image_url` parts. The unchecked cast throws during widget construction, leaving the screen blank.

## Fix

- Add `messageContentToText` to normalize both legacy string content and multipart content arrays.
- Preserve text parts and render image/file parts as safe placeholders.
- Render unknown structured parts as an explicit placeholder instead of crashing the whole chat view.
- Use the normalizer for user/assistant bubbles, filtering, and tool-message extraction.
- Add regression coverage for strings, text arrays, mixed text/image content, nulls, and unknown parts.

## How to Verify

1. Connect the Android client to a Hermes gateway.
2. Open a session containing a message whose `content` is a list with `text` and/or `image_url` parts.
3. Confirm the session renders instead of showing a blank screen.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression tests for legacy and multipart content.
- [x] `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` — no issues found.
- [x] `flutter test` — all 37 tests passed.
- [x] Manually reproduced on a Pixel 8a with the v1.0.9 APK, then verified the same session renders in the patched side-by-side build.
- [x] Checked ADB logcat after opening the affected session; no Flutter exception remains.

## Maintainer Notes

- Review scope is intentionally small: one commit, three files.
- No dependency, configuration, storage, API, or migration changes.
- Maintainer edits are enabled on the source branch.
- GitHub Actions is awaiting the standard first-time fork-contributor approval; the same analyze/test commands have already passed locally.

## Risk Assessment

Low — the change is isolated to display-time conversion of message content. Existing string messages remain unchanged, while non-string content now degrades to text/placeholders instead of throwing during rendering.

title: Literal `\n` displayed instead of newlines; raw tool results leaked to chat
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs make the app nearly unusable for sessions involving web search or extraction:

1. **Tool result messages (role: tool) appear as full message bubbles** instead of being filtered out or collapsed.
2. **JSON-escaped `\n` sequences in content are rendered literally** rather than being normalized to real newlines.

Together they produce walls of raw JSON with visible `\n` characters, raw markdown syntax (`#`, `---`), and internal server wrappers (`<untrusted_tool_result>`).

## To reproduce

1. Connect to a Hermes Gateway API server.
2. Start a new session or open an existing one that contains tool results (e.g. ask a question that triggers web_search or web_extract).
3. Observe the assistant's response.

Expected: tool results are hidden or shown as compact progress indicators; text content has real newlines and rendered markdown.

Actual: tool result messages appear as full chat bubbles containing raw JSON with literal `\n` characters and unrendered markdown syntax.

## Additional observations

- The same session renders correctly on Hermes Desktop -- tool results are hidden, content has proper newlines.
- Messages composed on Desktop and viewed back on mobile render correctly, confirming that `MarkdownBody` (from `flutter_markdown`) is functional and the issue is upstream in how content is prepared.

## Root cause analysis

### Bug 1: Tool result leakage

In `chat_screen.dart`, `_buildBody()` (line 682) filters messages with `role == 'tool'` by skipping them and instead showing a compact `_ToolProgressCard`. However, this filtering may not catch all tool-result messages if the server variant of the role string differs, or if certain messages are stored with role `assistant` but contain embedded tool output. The result is raw `<untrusted_tool_result>` wrappers and JSON appearing in the user's view.

### Bug 2: `\n` normalization

Tool result content from APIs like `web_extract` returns data that includes a JSON-encoded content field:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "content": "{\"results\": [{\"content\": \"...\\n\\n...\"}]}"
}
```

When `jsonDecode` in Dart processes the outer message, the `content` field becomes a Dart string. But that string still contains literal two-character `\n` sequences (backslash followed by n) because those were escape sequences in the inner JSON string, not real newline characters.

The string is then passed to `MarkdownBody` (line 825) which renders `\n` as text rather than line breaks, because they aren't actually newline characters.

Desktop avoids this either by filtering tool messages entirely or by normalizing `\n` before display.

### Rendering pipeline

```
API (JSON) -> jsonDecode -> messageContentToText() -> MarkdownBody
```

`messageContentToText()` (message_content.dart) is a simple identity function for string content -- it does no normalization of escape sequences.

## Suggested fix locations

1. **chat_screen.dart ~line 684**: Add broader filtering for tool result messages that may have non-standard role values, or ensure `role == 'tool'` catches all variants.

2. **message_content.dart**: Add normalization of literal `\n` to actual newlines. A narrow replacement in `messageContentToText()` would cover all rendering paths in one place:

   ```dart
   String messageContentToText(dynamic content) {
     if (content == null) return '';
     if (content is String) return content.replaceAll('\\n', '\n');
     // ...
   }
   ```

   The replacement should target the two-character `\n` sequence specifically, not all backslash escapes, to avoid over-escaping legitimate content.

3. **chat_screen.dart `_buildBody()`**: Ensure that messages with tool-like content that bypass the role filter are still prevented from appearing as full assistant bubbles.

## Environment

- App version: 1.0.10+110 (as published on GitHub)
- Device: Android (any)
- Server: Hermes Gateway API Server
- No prior issues filed for this behavior (31 closed, 1 open)

---

title: Literal `\n` displayed instead of newlines; raw tool results leaked to chat
body:
> AI-assisted by Hermes Agent, on behalf of @louquillio.

## Summary

Two related bugs make the app nearly unusable for sessions involving web search or extraction:

1. **Tool result messages (role: tool) appear as full message bubbles** instead of being filtered out or collapsed.
2. **JSON-escaped `\n` sequences in content are rendered literally** rather than being normalized to real newlines.

Together they produce walls of raw JSON with visible `\n` characters, raw markdown syntax (`#`, `---`), and internal server wrappers (`<untrusted_tool_result>`).

## To reproduce

1. Connect to a Hermes Gateway API server.
2. Start a new session or open an existing one that contains tool results (e.g. ask a question that triggers web_search or web_extract).
3. Observe the assistant's response.

Expected: tool results are hidden or shown as compact progress indicators; text content has real newlines and rendered markdown.

Actual: tool result messages appear as full chat bubbles containing raw JSON with literal `\n` characters and unrendered markdown syntax.

## Additional observations

- The same session renders correctly on Hermes Desktop -- tool results are hidden, content has proper newlines.
- Messages composed on Desktop and viewed back on mobile render correctly, confirming that `MarkdownBody` (from `flutter_markdown`) is functional and the issue is upstream in how content is prepared.

## Root cause analysis

### Bug 1: Tool result leakage

In `chat_screen.dart`, `_buildBody()` (line 682) filters messages with `role == 'tool'` by skipping them and instead showing a compact `_ToolProgressCard`. However, this filtering may not catch all tool-result messages if the server variant of the role string differs, or if certain messages are stored with role `assistant` but contain embedded tool output. The result is raw `<untrusted_tool_result>` wrappers and JSON appearing in the user's view.

### Bug 2: `\n` normalization

Tool result content from APIs like `web_extract` returns data that includes a JSON-encoded content field:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "content": "{\"results\": [{\"content\": \"...\\n\\n...\"}]}"
}
```

When `jsonDecode` in Dart processes the outer message, the `content` field becomes a Dart string. But that string still contains literal two-character `\n` sequences (backslash followed by n) because those were escape sequences in the inner JSON string, not real newline characters.

The string is then passed to `MarkdownBody` (line 825) which renders `\n` as text rather than line breaks, because they aren't actually newline characters.

Desktop avoids this either by filtering tool messages entirely or by normalizing `\n` before display.

### Rendering pipeline

```
API (JSON) -> jsonDecode -> messageContentToText() -> MarkdownBody
```

`messageContentToText()` (message_content.dart) is a simple identity function for string content -- it does no normalization of escape sequences.

## Suggested fix locations

1. **chat_screen.dart ~line 684**: Add broader filtering for tool result messages that may have non-standard role values, or ensure `role == 'tool'` catches all variants.

2. **message_content.dart**: Add normalization of literal `\n` to actual newlines. A narrow replacement in `messageContentToText()` would cover all rendering paths in one place:

   ```dart
   String messageContentToText(dynamic content) {
     if (content == null) return '';
     if (content is String) return content.replaceAll('\\n', '\n');
     // ...
   }
   ```

   The replacement should target the two-character `\n` sequence specifically, not all backslash escapes, to avoid over-escaping legitimate content.

3. **chat_screen.dart `_buildBody()`**: Ensure that messages with tool-like content that bypass the role filter are still prevented from appearing as full assistant bubbles.

## Environment

- App version: 1.0.10+110 (as published on GitHub)
- Device: Android (any)
- Server: Hermes Gateway API Server
- No prior issues filed for this behavior (31 closed, 1 open)

title: v2.0.0/v2.0.1 release APKs are unsigned — install fails with 'app not installed as package appears to be invalid'
body:
## Summary

The **v2.0.0 and v2.0.1 release APKs are unsigned** — they contain no APK Signature Scheme v1/v2/v3 signature at all. Android has refused unsigned APKs for years, so every install attempt fails with:

> App not installed as package appears to be invalid

Older releases (e.g. v1.0.13 and v1.0.8) are properly signed and install fine, so this looks like a regression in the release pipeline for the 2.x line, not a user-side problem.

## How to reproduce

1. Download `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` from the v2.0.1 (or v2.0.0) release.
2. Try to install on any Android device (sideload).
3. Observe: "App not installed as package appears to be invalid".

Workaround for users: install v1.0.13 — it is signed correctly.

## Evidence

Verified directly against the downloaded release assets (zip integrity passes, sizes match the release listing):

| Release | v2/v3 signing block ("APK Sig Block 42") present? | Zip integrity | Installable |
|---|---|---|---|
| v2.0.1 `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` (21,805,298 bytes) | **No** | OK | ❌ |
| v2.0.0 `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` (21,661,111 bytes) | **No** | OK | ❌ |
| v1.0.13 `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` (19,159,942 bytes) | **Yes** | OK | ✅ |

Checks:

- No `META-INF/*.RSA|.DSA|.EC|.SF` (no v1 signature) in any of the three APKs.
- The APK Signing Block magic `APK Sig Block 42` is absent from both 2.x APKs; present in v1.0.13.
- `python3 -c` zip `testzip()` returns OK for all three (files are not corrupt).

## Likely cause

The 2.x releases were built with `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` per the release notes, but the resulting APKs were published without the signing step, or the signing step silently failed. Worth checking:

- whether the release keystore was configured in the build environment used for the 2.0.0/2.0.1 tags,
- whether `flutter build apk --release` produced signed APKs locally (debug vs release keystore),
- whether the uploaded artifacts came from a debug/unsigned build directory.

## Suggested fix

1. Re-sign the v2.0.0/v2.0.1 APKs with the same release keystore used for ≤v1.0.13 (so existing installs can update in place — same key needed, otherwise users must uninstall first and lose saved connections).
2. Re-upload the assets or publish a v2.0.2 with the correct artifacts.
3. Add a CI step that verifies the signing block is present before uploading (e.g. `apksigner verify --print-certs app-arm64-v8a-release.apk` or a check for the `APK Sig Block 42` magic).

## Impact

- Users cannot install or update to 2.x at all; several releases' worth of fixes (background turn notifications, scroll fix, reverse-proxy path prefixes) are unreachable.
- Users who force-install by uninstalling the old app lose their saved connections/API keys.

title: Remote Gateway transport never activates against stock Hermes (turn_recovery capability doesn't exist upstream) + legacy fallback lacks resume re-sync
body:
## Summary

Two findings from running v2.0.1 (build 2131) against a stock Hermes Agent server:

1. **The v2 Remote Gateway transport can never activate against real Hermes** — the app falls back to legacy REST every time, so the "Background recovery unavailable — legacy transport" banner is permanent.
2. **In legacy fallback mode there is no resume-time re-sync**, so a turn that completes while the socket is dead (screen lock / Doze) loses its final message client-side until the chat is reopened.

## Finding 1: `turn_recovery` capability does not exist upstream

`_readyFailureAllowsLegacy` (lib/core/services/gateway_turn_coordinator.dart:1706+) requires the `gateway.ready` greeting to carry `protocol` + `capabilities.turn_recovery` for the desktop transport to engage.

The greeting emitted by Hermes (NousResearch/hermes-agent, `tui_gateway/entry.py:438-440`, latest origin/main `86b2057a1`, 2026-08-16) is:

```json
{"type": "gateway.ready", "payload": {"skin": {...}, "change_events": true}}
```

No `protocol`, no `capabilities`. A whole-tree search of origin/main for `turn_recovery` returns zero matches — the only implementation of this capability is this repo's synthetic fixture `tools/fake_gateway/turn_recovery_contract.py` ("hermes.fake_gateway.turn_recovery.v2"). As written, the app's negotiation hits `missingProtocol` → legacy allowed, so every real-Hermes connection degrades to REST. The community Remote Gateway edition was validated against a gateway contract upstream has never shipped.

Suggested direction: either (a) document that the desktop transport requires a server capability Hermes does not yet implement (and track the upstream side), or (b) negotiate against what Hermes actually emits and gate the durable-turn machinery on a capability the server really advertises.

## Finding 2: legacy mode has no resume re-sync

`didChangeAppLifecycleState` (lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:352-362) on `resumed` calls `_ensureDesktopSession()` and `_recoverPendingTurn()` — but `_recoverPendingTurn` returns immediately when `_legacyTransportFallback` is true (:689). Nothing re-fetches history on resume.

Repro: open a chat (legacy transport), submit a prompt, lock the screen mid-turn. The socket dies, the turn completes server-side, the final `message.complete` event is never delivered, and on unlock nothing re-syncs — the reply's tail (often the final assistant text) is missing until you leave and reopen the chat (which triggers `_initializeChat` → `_fetchMessages` → `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, so the message is safe server-side, just not re-rendered).

Suggested fix: when `_legacyTransportFallback` is active (or when recovery finds nothing pending), re-fetch history on resume, guarded against clobbering an active stream (`_streaming`) and with a last-message watermark to avoid full-history refetches on every unlock.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) and origin/main 86b2057a1 — both reproduce
- App v2.0.1 build 2131, Android 15, connection over Tailscale (LAN)
- Desktop Gateway URL set, dashboard basic-auth, API server 8642 for sessions

## Why it matters

The headline v2 feature (unified Desktop Gateway JSON-RPC transport with durable turn recovery, approvals replay, exactly-once submission) is effectively dead code against the ecosystem it targets, and the fallback path it actually runs on has the one failure mode (backgrounded turn settling) the durable machinery was built to prevent.

title: fix: remove hardcoded desktop gateway URL default and allow clearing optional fields
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in the connection add/edit dialog that made the Desktop
Gateway URL field effectively unmanageable. This matters because, per #84,
stock Hermes always falls back to legacy REST — reaching a clean REST setup
is the only practical path, and these bugs block it.

### 1. Hardcoded default

`_AddDialog` defaulted "Desktop Gateway URL" to a hardcoded developer IP
(`http://192.168.1.193/desktop`) instead of empty, so a fresh connection
pre-filled a bogus URL.

### 2. Un-clearable fields

`_validateAndSave` converted empty optional fields (`gatewayPrefix`,
`dashboardPrefix`, `desktopGatewayUrl`) to `null` before saving, but
`updateConnection`'s `clear*` flags (in `connection_manager.dart`) require a
**non-null empty string** to detect a clear. With `null` passed, `copyWith`'s
`null ?? oldValue` kept the previous value, so these fields silently reverted
to their last value on every edit.

## Changes

`lib/main.dart` only — pass the raw (possibly empty) value through instead of
null-coalescing it, and default the desktop gateway field text to empty.

## Verification

Built and installed locally; confirmed the "Desktop Gateway URL" field now
defaults to empty and can be cleared on an existing connection, allowing the
app to fall back to REST chat against a stock Hermes gateway.

## Related

- #84 — Remote Gateway transport never activates against stock Hermes; this
  fix makes the documented REST fallback reachable without a working Desktop
  Gateway.

title: Android app sessions are never persisted server-side (state.db has no app-path source) — history lost on reconnect/restart
body:
## Bug Description

The Android app (**remote client**) connects and authenticates to the Hermes gateway, but its
conversations are **never persisted as stored sessions**. History exists only in the live
websocket stream and evaporates on reconnect/restart — the phone loses everything, even though
the *server* is the layer that should own persistence.

This is broader than #84: #84 is about the transport falling back to legacy and dropping a *single*
final message. This issue is that **no app-path session is ever written at all**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the app on the phone (S23 Ultra, `com.hermesagent.hermes_android.dev` v2.0.1-dev) and
   connect to the gateway over Tailscale (`100.67.76.44` → `http://0.0.0.0:8642`).
2. Send a message; the reply streams back and displays fine.
3. Close / background the app (or let the socket die via Doze), then reopen.
4. The conversation history is gone (or a fresh, unpersisted session forks).

## Expected Behavior

The conversation should be persisted server-side as a stored session (via the gateway's
`api_server`/websocket path) so it survives reconnect and app restart — same as `tui`/`desktop`/
`telegram` sessions.

## Actual Behavior

- The phone authenticates and mints websocket tickets fine (verified live today):
  `login_success` / `ws_ticket_minted` for `ip=100.67.76.44`.
- But the canonical `state.db` has **zero** sessions from `ws` / `api` / `mobile` / `dashboard` /
  `android` sources. Sources present, across the whole DB: `tui`, `cron`, `telegram`, `desktop`,
  `subagent`, `cli`. An app-path session has never been stored.

## Environment

- App: `~/code/hermes-android`, branch `fix/jsonrpc-stock-hermes`, HEAD `5bc7992`
- Installed APK: `app-debug.apk` v2.0.1-dev (built Aug 20 23:37; durable-session-key fix `2cddffc`
  is in HEAD but NOT in the installed build)
- Server: Hermes gateway, `api_server` on `http://0.0.0.0:8642`, terminal backend `local`
- Phone: Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra, Tailscale IP `100.67.76.44`

## Root-cause analysis (two independent layers)

1. **Client (installed APK):** predates the durable-session-key fix `2cddffc` ("resume sessions by
   durable session key, not volatile sid"). It resumes by the volatile `sid`; the server refuses
   (4007) and a fresh, unpersisted session forks silently → "obscure jsonrpc errors" + lost history.
   Source on the branch is correct; the running binary is not.
2. **Server write path (unverified):** even a fixed client can't persist unless the gateway's
   `/api/ws` handler actually writes replies to `state.db` and assigns a durable source. This has
   NOT yet been confirmed — it is the main remaining investigation item.

## Security note (relevant to the fix)

`api_server` is network-accessible on `0.0.0.0:8642` with a **local (unsandboxed)** terminal
backend. The gateway logs a WARNING about this. Exposure is currently limited to the Tailscale
network, but any authenticated client can run code as the host user.

title: Clarify request renders empty dialog: question/choices missing when agent sends batch payload
body:
### Summary

When the Hermes agent asks a clarifying question during a chat, hermes-android shows an **empty "Hermes needs your input" dialog**: no question text, no choices, just a free-text field. The request itself arrives (the dialog opens and `Skip`/`Continue` work), but the content is missing.

Hermes Desktop renders the same prompt correctly, so the payload is arriving — the Android client is failing to parse it.

### Observed behavior (v2.1.0, build 2140)

- Dialog title: `Hermes needs your input`
- Body shows only the fallback text `Hermes needs more information to continue.` (this is the hardcoded default in `gateway_clarify.dart`)
- No choice options rendered (no radio/checkbox rows)
- Text field label is `Your answer` (it would be `Other answer` when choices are present)
- Typing a free-text answer and pressing Continue **does** resolve the request server-side — so only rendering/parsing of content is broken, transport is fine

### Root cause

Current Hermes Agent builds call the clarify tool with a **`questions` array** (batch wire format, even for a single question). The gateway then emits `clarify.request` with this payload shape:

```json
{
  "type": "clarify.request",
  "payload": {
    "request_id": "ab12cd34",
    "questions": [
      {
        "qid": "q1",
        "question": "Which product?",
        "choices": ["A", "B", "C"],
        "multi_select": false
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The Android parser `GatewayClarifyRequest.fromEventData` (`lib/core/models/gateway_clarify.dart`) only reads the **flat single-question** shape:

```json
{
  "request_id": "ab12cd34",
  "question": "Which product?",
  "choices": ["A", "B", "C"]
}
```

It never looks at `data['questions']`. Because `request_id` is present at the top level of both shapes, the dialog opens — but `question`/`choices` resolve to null, so the fallback strings render and no options appear.

A repo-wide search confirms there is no handling of the `questions` list / `qid` anywhere in the client (`lib/core/`).

### Repro

1. Connect hermes-android v2.1.0 to a stock Hermes Agent gateway (any recent release; legacy Desktop Gateway transport).
2. Start a chat and trigger any agent clarification (current Hermes agents emit the batch form even for one question).
3. Observe the empty dialog described above.

### Expected

Question text and up to 4 choices render with radio/checkbox selection and an `Other answer` field, mirroring Hermes Desktop — for both the flat single-question payload **and** the batch `questions[]` payload (either by supporting both shapes in `fromEventData`, or by mapping a 1-question batch onto the existing single-question UI).

### Environment

- hermes-android v2.1.0 (build 2140), default branch as of 2026-09-04
- Stock Hermes Agent gateway (hermes-agent, desktop/TUI gateway transport)
- Android 14, Samsung Galaxy

title: fix(clarify): parse batch questions[] payload from stock Hermes gateways
body:
Fixes #94.

Stock Hermes gateways emit `clarify.request` with a batch `questions[]` array (even for a single prompt). The client only parsed the legacy flat shape, so the dialog opened with fallback text and no choices.

## Changes

- `GatewayClarifyRequest.fromEventDataList` expands batch payloads into per-question prompts carrying their `qid`; flat payloads still parse via `fromEventData`
- `clarify.respond` now echoes `question_id` back so the gateway locks each answer independently; per-question Skip no longer cancels the whole batch
- Prompt queue de-duplication keys on `request_id` + `question_id`
- Fake gateway mirrors the stock batch shape with a `batch clarify test` fixture and per-question lock handling; contract probe covers the round trip

## Verification

- `flutter analyze`: clean
- `flutter test`: 947/947 passing (12 clarify tests, 84 connection manager tests)
- Fake gateway contract probe (`test_fake_gateway.py`): passes, including the new batch clarify section

title: ci: fail the release build when APKs lack a signing block
body:
Part of #82.

The v2.0.0/v2.0.1 release APKs shipped unsigned from a build that completed without error. The workflow already refuses tagged releases without a keystore, but nothing verified the produced APKs actually carry a signature.

## Changes

- New `Verify release APKs are signed` step after the build: runs `apksigner verify --print-certs` against every split release APK and fails the build if any APK is unsigned or carries no certificate

## Notes

- Re-signing and re-uploading the existing v2.0.0/v2.0.1 assets needs a maintainer decision (same keystore required for in-place updates), so it is not included here
- Verification runs only on the signed release path (`HAS_RELEASE_KEYSTORE == 'true'`)

title: fix(android): list and apply chat models without a Desktop Gateway
body:
The per-chat model picker is coupled to the Desktop Gateway WebSocket: `_showModelSelector` returns early unless a gateway client exists, and applying a choice pushes it over that socket via `setSessionModel` / `setSessionReasoning`. Any deployment without a reachable gateway therefore has a permanently dead picker, even though chat, sessions and history all work.

Listing needs only `api/model/info` and `api/model/options` over dashboard REST, and the API server already resolves a per-request `model` field, so the socket is not reqd for either half of the feature.

- list models through `DashboardClient` when no gateway is configured;
- keep the selection local and persisted instead of pushing it over the socket;
- carry the chosen model as the `model` field on the chat request, which `sendMessageStreaming` already accepts.

Reasoning effort remains gateway-only and is simply not applied in this mode.

Gateway turn recovery and its journal invariants are untouched: with a gateway configured every path behaves as before.

Motivation: we run Hermes headless and reverse-proxy only a handful of read-only dashboard GETs to the android client -- api/model/{info,options} for this picker, plus api/{memory,skills,cron/jobs} for the read-only tabs -- while deliberately not routing api/config, which returns provider keys and passwords. Every one of those tabs already works over REST; the model picker was the only feature that reached for the gateway socket, and only to read two endpoints we already publish.

title: fix: send the Hermes profile on the Desktop Gateway socket
body:
## Problem

When a connection has dashboard credentials (or a Desktop Gateway URL), chat moves onto the Desktop Gateway transport (`/api/ws`). On a **machine-level** `hermes dashboard` / `hermes serve` — the default when you run it without `--isolated` — that server hosts every profile on the machine and scopes each JSON-RPC call by a `profile` field in its params (`tui_gateway/server.py` `_profile_db` / `_profile_scoped`; `session.create` and `session.resume` store it on the session so later turns re-bind to that profile's home). The app never sent that field, so every chat quietly ran as the server's own (default) profile.

Observed on Hermes v0.21.0 (2026.8.31) with app v2.1.1: a connection meant for profile `sol` (gateway prefix `/p/sol`, dashboard 9119 with basic auth) produced short, generic replies from the default profile's model; the turns landed in the root session store with `source: tui` and never appeared in `sol`'s sessions. The session list looked right because it comes from the Gateway API with the `/p/sol` prefix — only the chat socket was misrouted, which makes this easy to miss.

## Fix

- New optional per-connection field **Hermes profile** (`SavedConnection.gatewayProfile`, persisted as `gateway_profile`, included in config backup/restore) under *Custom proxy and dashboard details*.
- `WsClient` merges `profile` into the params of every JSON-RPC request it sends on that socket (`send` and `sendStreaming`), the same way Hermes Desktop attaches its active profile to every scoped request. A caller that already set `profile` wins; a blank field sends nothing so the server keeps its own default.
- `DesktopGatewayClient` passes the profile to the socket client on all three construction paths (initial connect, reconnect, recovery-coordinator fresh sockets).
- Light input validation (no `/` or whitespace) so a path prefix pasted by mistake is rejected with a clear message.
- README + CHANGELOG entry.

Backward compatible: connections without the field behave exactly as before; isolated per-profile dashboards need nothing. The socket URL is unchanged.

### Revision history

The first push put the profile in the `/api/ws` query string. That was wrong: the `?profile=` reader I had cited in 0.21.0 belongs to `/api/pty`, not `/api/ws`, and the chat socket never looks at the URL. Thanks to the automation review for catching it. The current revision sends the field in the payload as described above.

## Not in this PR

The dashboard REST screens (Memory / Cron / Skills) on a machine-level dashboard also read the server's own profile. Hermes' sessions router accepts `?profile=` but the cron/skills routers (in the build I tested) do not, so I left those untouched rather than half-fix them. Happy to follow up if you'd like the sessions search to carry the profile too.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, `flutter test` green (results in the comments).
- New tests: `withProfile` merge rules (add / blank / null / caller wins); a fake gateway on a loopback `HttpServer` asserting that `session.resume`, `session.create` and an arbitrary RPC each carry `profile` in their params while the upgrade request URL stays `/api/ws?token=…`; model round-trip + `copyWith(clearGatewayProfile: true)`; config-backup round-trip.
- Not exercised on a device from this branch (no Android build environment on the machine I used). The bug itself was reproduced on a device with v2.1.1 as described above; the server contract was verified against Hermes 0.21.0 and upstream `main` (`tui_gateway/server.py`, `tui_gateway/methods_session.py`, `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: ci: pin the production APK signing certificate
body:
## Summary

Hardens the release path related to #82. The existing gate proves that each APK has a valid signature, but it would still accept an accidentally rotated or unrelated keystore and silently break future in-place upgrades.

## Findings

I downloaded and inspected the published ARM64 APKs with Android SDK `apksigner`:

- `v2.1.1` is correctly v2-signed with production certificate SHA-256 `475baf431b16d050c8f658ac838783b273f7c10bba06ed1d16bb0a4239f592fb`
- the backed-up production keystore has the same certificate fingerprint
- `v1.0.13` uses a different certificate (`0710e9dfe1eef9ab15906433878d8c3dd14e141d554fc57b66acc7e4ced302a3`), consistent with the repository's note that the old community APK used the standard Android debug certificate

Both APKs use `com.hermesagent.hermes_android`, so an existing v1.0.13 install cannot update in place to the production-signed v2.1.x line. This PR cannot repair already-published assets or recover compatibility with that old debug signer. It prevents another unintended signer change from v2.1.0 onwards.

## Changes

- pin the authorised production certificate SHA-256 in the release workflow
- parse every split APK's signer certificates from `apksigner --print-certs`
- fail unless the APK has exactly the expected production signer
- extend the release identity shape test so removal or weakening of the pin is detected

## Verification

- `flutter test --no-pub test/release_identity_test.dart` -> 2 passed
- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos test/release_identity_test.dart` -> no issues
- `git diff --check`
- verifier accepted the published v2.1.1 ARM64 APK and rejected the differently signed v1.0.13 APK as expected

## Scope

The existing v2.0.0/v2.0.1 assets remain unsigned. Current v2.1.x assets are signed and installable for fresh installs and updates within the production-signed release line.

title: Project chats permanently blocked: projects.assign_session does not exist on stock Hermes gateways
body:
# Project chats are permanently blocked: `projects.assign_session` does not exist on stock Hermes gateways

## Summary

Starting a chat inside a Project fails with "Couldn't create Project chat" against a stock Hermes Agent server, because the commit-before-open path calls the JSON-RPC method `projects.assign_session`, which upstream Hermes has never shipped. The gateway answers `-32601 unknown method`, the client treats it as fatal, and the chat never opens.

Project **creation** works (`projects.create` exists upstream) — so the user can create a project but can never start a chat in it. This is the same bug class as #84 (`turn_recovery` capability validated only against this repo's synthetic fake gateway, never against real Hermes).

## Root cause

Client path (`lib/core/screens/workspace_screen.dart`, `_finishNewChat`):

1. Draft a Project chat → `projects.assign_session(session_id, project_id)` must succeed **before** the chat opens ("commit-before-open").
2. Stock Hermes `tui_gateway/methods_projects.py` registers: `projects.list`, `projects.get`, `projects.create`, `projects.archive`, `projects.delete`, `projects.set_active`, `projects.for_cwd` — plus `projects.tree`, `projects.project_sessions`, `projects.discover_repos`, `projects.record_repos` in `methods_config.py`. **No `assign_session`.** `git log -S "assign_session"` across the entire upstream history: zero hits.
3. Gateway replies `-32601 unknown method: projects.assign_session`. In `ProjectsGatewayClient._request` this is not a "sibling missing" soft-fail (the probe method is `projects.list`, which succeeds), so it surfaces as a hard error → snackbar "Couldn't create Project chat" + Retry that can never succeed.

Meanwhile, upstream Hermes derives a session's project membership from the session's **working directory** (`projects_db.project_for_path(cwd)`), and `session.create` accepts a `cwd` parameter. There is no per-session explicit assignment row upstream — the app's contract was designed against `tools/fake_gateway/`, not against the real server.

## Reproduction

1. Hermes Agent v0.21.2 (upstream `e440bf35`), gateway running with `projects.*` support.
2. Android app v2.1.1 (build 2141), connected over LAN/Tailscale.
3. Projects pane → open a project → "New chat" (or Home → New → Project chat).
4. Expected: chat opens inside the project. Actual: "Couldn't create Project chat" with a Retry that always fails. Quick chat works (it skips the assign call).

## Proposed fix (implemented, tested)

Make the missing `assign_session` sibling non-fatal and bind the chat through the mechanism stock Hermes actually honors — the session `cwd`:

- `workspace_screen.dart`: catch `ProjectsUnsupportedException` around the assign call; show an explanatory snackbar and open the chat anyway (other errors keep the existing blocking + Retry behavior).
- `new_chat_options.dart`: `NewChatDraft` carries `projectWorkingDirectory` (project `primary_path` / first folder).
- `chat_screen.dart` / `desktop_gateway_client.dart`: thread it through `ensureSession` → `_connect` → `_resumeOrCreate`.
- `ws_client.dart`: `createOrResumeSession(sessionId, {workingDirectory})` forwards it as `cwd` on `session.create`, which upstream accepts, persists, and uses for `project_for_path` grouping — so the chat lands under the project on the next tree refresh.

On a future gateway that ships `projects.assign_session`, the explicit assignment still takes precedence; cwd binding is only the fallback.

Verification: `flutter analyze` clean; full existing suite (947 tests) passes; release APK builds and signs.

## Notes

- A project with no working directory on the gateway host has no cwd to bind to; on such gateways the chat opens Unassigned with the explanatory snackbar rather than being blocked.
- The longer-term fix is upstream: either Hermes grows a real session→project assignment RPC (needs a new association table, since membership is currently cwd-derived), or the app contract is documented as cwd-based.

---

Full patch attached (5 files, +75/−13).

## Problem

The gateway answers `-32601`, the client treats it as fatal, and the chat never opens. Full analysis in #100.

## Fix

Make the missing sibling non-fatal and bind the chat through the mechanism stock Hermes actually honors — the session `cwd`:

title: fix: open Project chats on stock Hermes gateways
body:
## Summary

Fixes #100 with the stock Hermes gateway contract.

Project chats currently require `projects.assign_session`, but stock Hermes does not ship that sibling RPC. The app therefore blocks the chat before it can open. The existing PR #101 identifies the right cwd-based fallback, but its `session.create` request still includes the unsupported `session_id` field and also contains an unrelated feature commit.

## Changes

- treat only a missing `projects.assign_session` sibling as a non-fatal compatibility fallback

- retain the runtime session ID returned by the gateway in the existing mobile-to-gateway mapping
- keep transport and genuine Project assignment failures blocking and retryable
- add widget, draft-model, and WebSocket request-shape regression coverage

A future gateway that implements `projects.assign_session` still uses the explicit assignment path. The cwd fallback is only used when that method is absent.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze --no-pub`: no issues
- `flutter test --no-pub`: 949 passed
- `git diff --check`

This is a clean, single-scope alternative to #101. The original cwd fallback was proposed by @Thaeland and is credited in the commit.

title: Tablet: message bubbles size from the full screen while the chat column is capped at 800 dp — long lines are clipped, not wrapped
body:
# Tablet: message bubbles size from the full screen while the chat column is capped at 800 dp — long lines are clipped, not wrapped

**App version:** 2.1.3 (build 2143)
**Device:** Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max (13.3", 3408 × 2272 px, density 320 dpi → DPR 2)
**Logical size:** 1704 × 1136 dp (landscape / portrait)
**Transport:** legacy REST/SSE (8642) — unrelated, but noted since #84 keeps the desktop transport off

## Symptom

On a tablet, long message lines are hard-cut around three quarters of the screen width and the
area to the right of the cut stays blank, so the text looks like it never wraps. Short messages are
fine. The reviewer's own messages (right-aligned) show the opposite: the beginning of every line is
cut off, because the bubble is wider than the viewport it is placed in.

Measured on the device above (landscape): text is laid out 1560 dp wide, only 736 dp of it is
visible (47 %); the cut lands at ~76 % of the screen width with ~416 dp of empty space beyond it.
Portrait hides less (992 dp laid out, 736 dp visible, cut at ~88 %), which is why the problem is
easy to miss when the tablet is held vertically.

## Cause

Two widths that were never reconciled:

1. The chat body caps its content column at 800 dp on tablets —
   `lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:2703`

   ```dart
   body: Center(
     child: ConstrainedBox(
       constraints: BoxConstraints(
         maxWidth: Responsive.isTablet(context) ? 800 : double.infinity,
       ),
   ```

2. Every message bubble is sized from the **whole screen** instead —
   `lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:3389`

   ```dart
   constraints: BoxConstraints(
     maxWidth: MediaQuery.of(context).size.width - 80,
   ),
   ```

3. The 800 dp cap cannot clamp the bubble, because at `lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:3468` the
   bubble is wrapped in a `Row` with a single non-flex child:

   ```dart
   return Row(
     mainAxisAlignment: isUser ? MainAxisAlignment.end : MainAxisAlignment.start,
     children: [bubble],
   );
   ```

   Flutter gives non-flex `Row` children **unbounded** main-axis constraints
   (`RenderFlex._constraintsForNonFlexChild` → `BoxConstraints(maxHeight: constraints.maxHeight)`
   for `Axis.horizontal`), so the bubble lays out at `screenWidth - 80` (1624 dp here) inside an
   800 dp viewport and the ListView clips it at its own edge.

Git history shows the gap: the bubble expression comes from the original phone-only chat screen
(#5, b05a2f4), while the 800 dp tablet cap was added the same day by the responsive-layout work
(#32, cffd071) without revisiting the bubble.

## Why the test suite misses it

`widget_test.dart` pumps `MessageBubble` as the whole `Scaffold` body (default 800 × 600 surface),
never inside a constrained column, and the layout regression tests there use small widths
(320/360 dp) with a 200 % text scale. `hermes_shell_test.dart` / `workspace_screen_test.dart` cover
the rail, not the chat content width. `CODE_QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md` asks to "verify behaviour on at
least one phone-sized layout and one wider/tablet layout" — the wide case has no coverage for chat.

## Suggested fix

Give the bubble its parent's constraints instead of the screen's — replacing the single-child `Row`
with `Align` is enough, since `Align` passes bounded loose constraints down:

```dart
return Align(
  alignment: isUser ? Alignment.centerRight : Alignment.centerLeft,
  child: bubble,
);
```

plus a regression widget test that pumps `MessageBubble` inside
`Center(ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: 800))` at a 1704 × 1136 dp surface and asserts the bubble's width
is ≤ 800 and that no `RenderFlex` overflow is reported.

Worth doing now rather than later: the roadmap's tablet design is a three-pane rail + list + detail
(`docs/ANDROID_FINAL_UI_SPEC_DRAFT.md`), which will make the chat pane *narrower* than 800 dp — the
bubble would then overflow even more.

title: Stock-gateway compatibility: 28 fixes and features verified against a stock Hermes gateway
body:
## What this is

28 commits that make the Android client work correctly against a **stock Hermes gateway** — no custom server RPCs, no fixture-only assumptions. Every feature here is built on RPCs that ship in stock Hermes (verified against the live gateway contract), mirroring how Hermes Desktop performs the same gestures.

Each commit has a plain-language summary first, then the technical detail.

## Commits (oldest → newest)

### Features

- **`82c0ff7` — Chats show the right project name.** The chat list only learned about project membership from a short "preview" list the server sent, so a filed chat that missed the preview cut was mislabeled "Unassigned". The app now reads a complete map of every filed chat's owner, so labels are correct no matter how many chats you have. (Technical: reads `session_projects` from `projects.tree` via `ownerLabelOf()`; the Home bucket `__no_project__` is not a filing and stays unlabeled.)

- **`5a2b283` — Name-only Projects get a real folder.** Creating a Project with just a name used to leave it folderless, so chats couldn't be filed into it. The app now automatically provisions a fresh folder for the new Project via the dashboard, never adopting a pre-existing one — taken names bump to `-1/-2/...` and any failure degrades to folderless rather than a wrong folder.

- **`02b89f8` — The connection survives your phone going to sleep.** Previously, phone sleep, Wi-Fi NAT eviction, or a gateway restart silently killed the chat socket and nothing worked until you restarted the app. The client now sends a heartbeat every 15 seconds and auto-reconnects with backoff when the link drops, so conversations pick up where they left off. (Mirrors the desktop's json-rpc-channel keepalive.)

- **`bd840b3` — Cron runs get their own home.** Scheduled-job runs used to flood the chat list. They now stay out of the chat/recents list entirely and appear only in the Cron screen, where tapping a job expands into its run history — same separation the desktop app uses.

- **`5b65dfc` — Move unassigned chats into a Project.** Adds the gesture: from the Unassigned list, pick a chat, pick a Project, done. Uses the stock `session.workspace.move` primitive (re-home the chat's working folder — the gateway derives project membership from the folder).

### Transport & wire fixes

- **`07f7e2c` — No more double-connect races.** Two parts of the app asking for a connection at the same time could each open a socket and fight over it. Socket creation is now single-flight with a strict closed-flag and resume binding.

- **`95227d0` — Every request has a deadline.** HTTP calls that could hang forever now carry a request timeout, and the login flow is single-flight so two racing auth attempts can't clobber each other's session.

- **`ec6e296` — A cancelled turn can never claim success.** Stream state was shared between overlapping calls, so cancelling one turn could report "completed". Each call now owns its state; token delivery is gated on the call still being current.

- **`a1b4e26` — The app launches even with a corrupt local store.** A damaged saved-connections file used to crash the app at startup. It now survives, and the session parser tolerates type variations from the server instead of throwing.

- **`e9428f5` — File attachments work on stock gateways.** The client was sending extra fields on `file.attach` that only the test fixture accepted; stock gateways rejected every attach with "Extra inputs are not permitted". Now it sends exactly the stock parameter set.

- **`0f11754` — Recovers when the server forgets your session.** The gateway garbage-collects idle sessions from memory; the client's cached handle would then fail every call. It now detects the stale binding, resumes the stored session automatically, and if a turn is still running server-side, tells you it "continues on the server" instead of going silent.

### Honest-degradation fixes

- **`118d39f` — "This gateway doesn't support that" instead of "broken".** When a feature is genuinely absent on a stock gateway, the app shows a calm capability notice rather than a permanent red failure banner.

- **`29e90f0` — Don't cry wolf on pending turns.** The "stock gateway" label was being applied to verdicts that had pending turns attached, masking real upload errors. The label now requires clean evidence of absence, and upload errors surface honestly.

- **`0b88e54` — "I don't know" renders as unknown, not "Unassigned".** When the projects lookup fails or times out, chats are no longer falsely shown as unclaimed; the archived list survives a promote, and the merged lists dedupe.

### Session list / Unassigned bucket

- **`3eda7b2` — Server-archived chats appear in the Archived chip.** Previously the Archived chip only showed device-local expirations; server-archived sessions were invisible. Now they're fetched through the dashboard transport, which honors the archived filter.

- **`751b078` + `a6df777` — The chat list actually pages.** The client only ever fetched the first page, so older chats were unreachable — not filtered out, just never loaded. Both session-list loaders now page through the full list as you scroll.

- **`f403591` — The Home bucket isn't "claimed".** The server's "claimed" set includes the synthetic Home bucket, so using it raw made the Unassigned filter permanently empty. A chat is now only claimed when a real project owns it.

- **`fdf4fa3` — Project labels from the real per-node data.** Chat→project labels are derived from each project node's actual `sessionIds` array instead of a key that doesn't exist on the wire, which previously rendered every filed chat as "Unassigned".

### Audit fixes & misc

- **`8911b9d` — No more permanent write lockout.** The turn-recovery journal could fill with entries its eviction rules could never remove, after which *every* write threw — a device-wide lockout. There's now a last-resort eviction tier for quarantined entries.

- **`8a4507c` — Stop button shows the real final state.** The interrupt response carries the authoritative final state of the turn; it was being read for a snackbar and thrown away, leaving the view showing truncated data as if complete.

- **`825472c` — Five audit LOWs.** Capability registry reset on reconnect, soft-false caching fix, batch selection leak across filters, archived-project name matching, and purging backup temp files so encrypted copies don't accumulate.

- **`325ffe6` — Snackbars dismiss themselves.** A Flutter breaking change made action snackbars stay forever; all six Undo/Retry snackbars now set `persist: false`.

- **`1fafff7` — Voice dictation works on Android 11+.** The app never declared the speech-recognition service in its manifest's `<queries>` block, so Android reported no recognizer available even when one existed.

- **`db2c3cc` — Dead code removal.** Drops the orphaned `filing.*`/`assets.*` gateway clients that targeted RPC families this build doesn't use.

### Stock-only refactor (completes the conversion)

- **`bc0907b` — Ports the stock move primitive.** Gives the move-chat UI its backing: `moveSessionWorkspace` over `session.workspace.move` with honest reason strings for impossible moves.

- **`b7be41f` — Move = cwd re-home, nothing else.** `moveSessionToProject` no longer attempts `projects.assign_session` first. That RPC never shipped in stock Hermes, so trying it was a doomed round-trip on every move.

- **`a68e86e` — `projects.assign_session` deleted entirely.** The never-shipped RPC and all its machinery (commit-before-open, draft-id reconcile) are gone. `session.workspace.move` — how Hermes Desktop files chats — is the only move primitive. New Project chats open with the Project's folder as the session cwd; folderless Projects say so honestly.

## Verification (at this branch tip)

- `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` — clean, no issues
- `flutter test` — **997/997 passed**
- `real_gateway_contract_probe.py` against a spawned stock `tui_gateway` — **PASS** (create/resume/cwd/param-rejection)

## Summary

Adds **Settings → Appearance → Chat detail cards**, with an independent choice for the **Tool activity** and **Reasoning** cards:

| Choice | Behavior |
|---|---|
