title: feat: add a compact chat density
body:
## What was wrong

Every chat bubble is laid out with a tablet's worth of air, and every bubble is captioned:

- `margin: 16/4dp`, `padding: 16/12dp`, `radius: 18`, and a 4dp gap under the body — applied even to a one-line "yes"
- a bold **You** / **Hermes** label above *every* message, plus a 6dp gap under it

The label carries no information that the layout does not: the bubble is left- or right-aligned and the user fill is gold. On a phone it costs a full line of vertical space per message, which is the scarcest thing on the screen.

## What changed

A new **Appearance → Chat density** setting with two values. *Comfortable* is the current layout, unchanged, and stays the default, so nothing moves for anyone who does not touch the setting.

| | Comfortable (default) | Compact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sender label | `You` / `Hermes` above each bubble | removed from the layout, kept for screen readers |
| Bubble padding | 16 × 12dp | 12 × 6dp |
| Bubble margin | 16 × 4dp | 12 × 2dp |
| Corner radius | 18 | 14 |
| Max-width inset | 80dp | 48dp |
| Gap under the body / under the list | 4dp / 4dp | 0 / 0 |

The wider bubble is the part that saves lines rather than pixels: 48dp of inset instead of 80dp lets prose wrap later, so a three-line message often becomes two.

Geometry lives on the `ChatDensity` enum, so the message list and the settings copy read one source of truth. The selection is written through `ChatDensityStore` *and* broadcast on a `ValueNotifier`, so a chat that is already open re-lays out the moment the setting changes instead of waiting for the route to be reopened (`_verboseMode` still needs a reopen; this does not). The new key joins `ConfigBackupService.exactPreferenceKeys`, and the copy exists in all 11 catalogues with the generated `app_localizations*.dart` committed.

### The label is a layout change, not an information change

Dropping a visible caption must not drop the speaker from the accessibility tree, so compact wraps the bubble in `Semantics(container: true, label: 'You' | 'Hermes')` instead of deleting the information. It stays a separate node rather than a `MergeSemantics` group on purpose: assistant bubbles contain their own controls (code-block copy and wrap), and merging would make those children read out as one blob. Comfortable adds no wrapper, so no message announces its speaker twice.

### Storage stays the only source of truth

The preference has two in-memory copies — the broadcast the chat list listens to, and the settings card's own copy, taken in `initState` (a Settings rebuild does not rerun it). Both now follow storage:

- a configuration restore re-reads the preference through `ChatDensityStore` once the write loop finishes, and the settings card subscribes to the broadcast, so an import cannot leave the card showing one density while the chat uses another;
- the picker resolves its own `Navigator` and `ModalRoute` *before* awaiting the write and only pops if that route is still current, so a sheet dismissed mid-write can no longer take Settings down with it.

### Screenshots

Same six-message conversation, 411dp wide, Roboto, rendered from the real `MessageBubble` in a widget-test harness:

**Comfortable → Compact**

![Comfortable and Compact side by side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_compare.png)

**Dark theme**

![Comfortable and Compact in dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_compare_dark.png)

**Compact at 130% Android text scale** (no clipping, wrapping absorbs the extra size)

![Compact at 1.3x text scale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_compact_large_text.png)

Full size: [Comfortable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_comfortable.png) · [Compact](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_compact.png) · [Comfortable dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_comfortable_dark.png) · [Compact dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/compact-density-screenshots/screenshots/density_compact_dark.png)

Measured, those six messages occupy **720dp** of list in Comfortable and **468dp** in Compact — about a third less scrolling for identical content. (The images live on an `assets/compact-density-screenshots` branch of my fork so this diff stays image-free.)

## Tests

**Unit / widget** — `test/chat_density_preference_test.dart`, `test/chat_density_bubble_test.dart`, `test/chat_density_settings_card_test.dart`: the storage fallback, every inset being strictly tighter, the store round-trip plus the broadcast, the label appearing/disappearing, the insets actually reaching the `Container`, compact being wider for the same unwrapped line, the same conversation fitting in less vertical space, and the settings card persisting a selection.

**Screen level** — `test/chat_density_chat_screen_test.dart` pumps a real `ChatScreen` over a fixture gateway rather than a lone `MessageBubble`, because the interesting failures are in the wiring, not in the bubble:

- `a launch with compact stored renders unlabelled bubbles` — the preference is actually read on mount
- `a launch with no stored value keeps the sender labels` — the default is untouched
- `stored preferences win over a stale density broadcast` — a leftover broadcast value cannot outlive the mount; the persisted value is the truth
- `changing the density re-lays out an already open chat` — save → labels vanish → save back → labels return, with no remount
- `compact still announces the speaker to screen readers` / `comfortable does not duplicate the speaker` — the `Semantics` label appears exactly where it should

**Settings and restore** — `test/chat_density_settings_card_test.dart` and `test/config_backup_service_test.dart`: `a restored preference reaches the mounted card`, `import re-broadcasts a restored chat density`, and `a picker dismissed mid-write does not close Settings`.

Proven to bite by reverting only the implementation (`_loadChatDensity()` + the notifier listener removed, `Semantics` wrapper removed) and re-running the screen test:

```
Expected: no matching candidates
  Actual: _DescendantWidgetFinder:<Found 1 widget with text "You" descending from widget with key
  a launch with compact stored renders unlabelled bubbles [E]

Expected: exactly one matching candidate
  Actual: _DescendantWidgetFinder:<Found 0 widgets with text "You" descending from widgets with key
  stored preferences win over a stale density broadcast [E]

Expected: no matching candidates
  Actual: _DescendantWidgetFinder:<Found 1 widget with text "You" descending from widget with key
  changing the density re-lays out an already open chat [E]

Expected: no matching candidates
  Actual: _DescendantWidgetFinder:<Found 1 widget with text "You" descending from widget with key
  compact still announces the speaker to screen readers [E]
```

and by reverting the label guard and the padding/margin constants for the bubble tests:

```
Expected: no matching candidates
  Actual: _TextWidgetFinder:<Found 1 widget with text "You": [
  compact removes the You and Hermes labels [E]

Expected: EdgeInsets:<EdgeInsets(12.0, 6.0, 12.0, 6.0)>
  Actual: EdgeInsets:<EdgeInsets(16.0, 12.0, 16.0, 12.0)>
  compact uses the density insets on the bubble [E]
```

and by reverting each of the three review fixes on its own:

```
Expected: ChatDensity:<ChatDensity.compact>
  Actual: ChatDensity:<ChatDensity.comfortable>
  import re-broadcasts a restored chat density [E]

Expected: exactly one matching candidate
  Actual: _TextContainingWidgetFinder:<Found 0 widgets with text containing Compact: []>
  a restored preference reaches the mounted card [E]

Expected: exactly one matching candidate
  Actual: _TextWidgetFinder:<Found 0 widgets with text "Chat density": []>
  a picker dismissed mid-write does not close Settings [E]
```

## Gates

```
$ flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos
No issues found!

$ flutter test --no-pub
+1293: All tests passed!
```

No `CHANGELOG.md` entry and no `CODE_QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md` boxes: recent merged PRs let the release commit compile the notes, and the checklist is scoped to release PRs.

title: fix: keep a collapsed tool-activity card collapsed while tools run
body:
## What was wrong

While the agent is working, the activity card opens itself — that part is intended. But collapsing it only sticks until the *next* tool call arrives, at which point it springs back open, and it only stays shut once the turn is over. So the one moment you want it closed (a long run of terminal calls scrolling past) is the one moment it refuses.

Cause: the `ExpansionTile` was keyed on the activity list itself —

```dart
key: PageStorageKey<String>(
  'gateway-activity-${activities.map((item) => item.toolId ?? item.name).join('-')}',
),
initiallyExpanded: active || widget.verbose,
```

Every new activity changes that key, so Flutter throws the tile away and builds a fresh one, whose `initiallyExpanded` is `active == true` — i.e. open, exactly when the user asked for closed. When the turn finishes the same expression goes false, which is why the card appeared to remember the collapse only at the end.

## What changed

Expansion state now belongs to the card's `State`, not to a widget key that is recomputed from the data:

- the tile is driven by an `ExpansibleController` the `State` owns, so a rebuilt card is still the same card;
- **a tap pins the user's choice.** `_userExpanded` records it and the card stops following the turn: further tool calls arriving do not reopen it, and the end of the turn does not close it either;
- **until it is tapped, nothing changes.** The card still opens while anything is running (or in verbose mode) and closes once the turn settles, so anyone who never touches it sees today's behaviour;
- the programmatic `expand()`/`collapse()` is flagged, so the card opening on its own is not mistaken for a tap and does not pin itself.

`PageStorageKey` is dropped rather than made stable: it existed to key the tile on its contents, and its restoration would fight the pin.

## The collapsed header still reports progress

This was already in the header, and it is the reason a pinned card is still useful — so it is covered by tests now instead of being incidental:

| State | Collapsed header shows |
| --- | --- |
| Tools running | spinner + `Hermes is using N tools`, card tinted with the running accent |
| All finished | check icon + `N completed` |
| Some failed | error icon + `N failed • M total` |

**Step by step** — 2 tools running, you collapse it, a third tool call lands, the turn finishes:

![Tool activity card: collapsed while running and staying collapsed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/tool-group-collapse/screenshots/tool_group_pin_grid.png)

[Same thing animated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/tool-group-collapse/screenshots/tool_group_pin.gif) (the card is collapsed at step 2 and never reopens itself):

![Animated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igitur/hermes-android/assets/tool-group-collapse/screenshots/tool_group_pin.gif)

Rendered from the real `GatewayActivityCard` at 411dp wide with the real Roboto in a widget-test harness, so the images are the widget's own output.

## The pin follows the group, not the row

Pinning in the card's own `State` is not enough either: `chat_screen.dart` renders the projection through a `ListView.builder`, and while a turn streams the assistant bubble is inserted **ahead** of the trailing activity card, so the card is rebuilt at a lower index and its `State` is discarded (rows scrolled out of the viewport are evicted the same way). The card would reopen mid-run.

So the projection now hands out identity: consecutive tool activities become a `ChatToolActivityGroup({id, activities})`, and `id` is derived from the group's *first* activity — the one element that never changes while the group grows — disambiguated by occurrence for the seedless case. The same group gets the same id whether it was flushed from stored tool results or is still the trailing streamed group.

`ToolActivityGroupPins` (new, `lib/core/services/`) holds the choices keyed by that id. `ChatScreen` owns one, passes `pinnedExpansion` into the card and records `onPinChanged`; the card carries `key: ValueKey('tool-activity-<id>')`, and `initiallyExpanded` follows the remembered choice first and only falls back to the running/verbose default. A card that is rebuilt at another index, or evicted and recreated, therefore opens the way the user left it.

## Tests

New `test/gateway_activity_card_collapse_pin_test.dart` (6 tests):

- `a card the user collapsed stays collapsed as tools arrive` — collapse, then a second tool call appears: still closed, and the header still reads `Hermes is using 2 tools` with one spinner
- `a collapsed card reports the turn finishing` — spinner and running copy give way to a check icon and `1 completed`, still closed
- `an untouched card still opens and closes with the turn` — the default path is unchanged, including a later tool keeping it open
- `a card the user expanded stays expanded when tools settle` — the pin works in both directions
- `verbose opens the card without counting as a tap` — turning verbose off closes the card, proving a programmatic open does not pin
- `the user can reopen a card that auto-collapsed`

`test/gateway_activity_card_projection_pin_test.dart` (6 tests) drives the real projection through a list that mirrors the item builder, because that is where the bug lives:

- `the group keeps its id when the projection moves it down the list` — asserts the card sits at index 1 before the assistant text and index 2 after, with the same id
- `the id is stable while the group grows`
- `a collapsed card stays collapsed when text moves it down the list` — the reported scenario end to end
- `a card pinned open stays open when it moves and the turn settles`
- `the pin survives the row being evicted and rebuilt` — unmounts the card entirely, then rebuilds it
- `each group keeps its own choice` — two groups in one projection, only one collapsed

Proven to bite by reverting only `lib/core/widgets/gateway_activity_card.dart` to its current upstream implementation and re-running the fixed-position file — 5 of 6 fail, the headline one with the reported symptom:

```
Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  a card the user collapsed stays collapsed as tools arrive [E]

Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  an untouched card still opens and closes with the turn [E]

Expected: true
  Actual: <false>
  a card the user expanded stays expanded when tools settle [E]

Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  verbose opens the card without counting as a tap [E]

Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  the user can reopen a card that auto-collapsed [E]
```

and by reverting `initiallyExpanded` to the running/verbose default, i.e. not honouring a pin restored after a remount:

```
Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  a collapsed card stays collapsed when text moves it down the list [E]

Expected: true
  Actual: <false>
  a card pinned open stays open when it moves and the turn settles [E]

Expected: false
  Actual: <true>
  the pin survives the row being evicted and rebuilt [E]
```

## Gates

```
$ flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos
No issues found!

$ flutter test --no-pub
+1285: All tests passed!
```

Six files: `gateway_activity_card.dart`, `chat_screen.dart`, `chat_display_items.dart`, the new `tool_activity_group_pins.dart`, and two test files. No new copy, so no ARB/`gen-l10n` churn; no `CHANGELOG.md` and no checklist boxes, consistent with recent merged PRs (release commits compile the notes).

title: perf: full session-list resync every foreground, per-turn transcript refetch, and no durable /v1/runs in API-server mode
body:
## Environment

- App 2.1.19 (versionCode 21592), Android, targetSdk 36, Samsung Galaxy Fold6 over Tailscale
- Server A: Hermes 0.21.4, `api_server` on :8642 (OpenAI-compatible) — used as an "API server" connection
- Server B: Hermes 0.22.2, dashboard :9119 + `/api/ws` — used as a "Dashboard" connection
- Data: server-side `aiohttp.access` logs matched by client IP, window 2026-10-18 15:29 → 2026-10-19 03:08

## 1. Full session-list resync on every foreground

`GET /api/sessions?limit=100&offset={0,100,200}` — 112 complete syncs (offset=0 → offset=100 → offset=200 until a short page) in that window. Hourly counts of the offset=0 leg: 15h: 2, 16h: 8, 18h: 33, 01h: 36, 02h: 33.

Each sync is ~88 KB uncompressed (81,633 B for the first page alone). Two full syncs fired 2 s apart on a single resume (02:46:52 and 02:46:54), which suggests both `resumed` and an in-flight initial load trigger a full sync.

Suggestion: incremental fetch keyed on an `updated_at` / newest-id cursor, keep the first page cached for instant paint, and coalesce concurrent syncs into one.

## 2. Whole transcript tail refetched after every turn

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?limit=50&order=latest` — 50 calls in the window; median 167 KB, p90 287 KB, max 310 KB (uncompressed JSON). One call per completed turn.

Suggestion: append-only fetch with a since/message-id cursor, or let the turn stream deliver the new messages so no refetch is needed.

## 3. API-server mode never uses durable runs

In API-server mode the client only uses `POST /v1/chat/completions` (20 calls in the window, responses 438 KB – 4.29 MB). Both servers advertise durable run submission in `/v1/capabilities` — `runs.submit`, 24 h retention, `/v1/runs/{id}/events` SSE, idempotency keys.

Switching this mode to `/v1/runs` would (a) give it real resume-after-background instead of "chat runs live", and (b) replace the 4 MB single responses with incremental event consumption.

## 4. Minor: two ws tickets and two sockets per connect

`dashboard-auth.log` logs two `ws_ticket_minted` events per connect (~3 ms apart); the server accepts two `/api/ws` sockets within 3 ms, and one is closed ~20 ms later while its `client.capabilities` reply is still pending, producing `Unexpected ASGI message 'websocket.send', after sending 'websocket.close'` on the server.

Probably the legacy-probe socket from #84, so low priority — but it makes every connect noisy server-side and throws away the capability probe result.

## 5. Server-side note: responses are not compressed

Hermes returns the session list as 81,633 B with no `Content-Encoding` even when the request sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br`; gzip -9 produces 14,176 B (5.8x). Worth a server-side response-compression middleware, excluding `text/event-stream` so token streaming is unaffected.

Happy to test patches against either server.

title: Keep the gateway socket alive while the app is backgrounded
body:
## The problem

My Hermes Android app kept dropping the desktop gateway connection every time I minimized it. The reconnect-on-resume logic already existed, but the drop itself was the bug: when Android freezes or kills a cached process, the Dart `gateway.ping` heartbeat timer stops with it, and the gateway tears the socket down at its 45-second silence deadline. By the time I came back to the app, the connection was already gone.

## What I did

I added a client-side keep-alive that keeps the process alive while the app is backgrounded, so the heartbeat timers keep ticking and every socket stays under the silence deadline. The gateway itself is untouched — this rides entirely on stock behavior.

On the Android side there's a new `ConnectionKeepAliveService`, a `specialUse` foreground service (with the subtype property required on targetSdk 34+) started and stopped over a small `keepalive` MethodChannel on `MainActivity`. It uses `START_NOT_STICKY` and a quiet `IMPORTANCE_LOW` notification channel, and a refused start (Android 12+ background-start limits) returns `false` so Dart treats it as a silent no-op rather than an error.

On the Dart side `ConnectionKeepAliveService` owns the whole policy in one testable method, `onAppLifecycleState(state, hasLiveSocket:)`, which the app-root lifecycle observer delegates to. The gate is `DesktopGatewayClient.hasLiveSocket` — a static check over live clients for an open or reconnecting socket. Gating on live sockets rather than constructed clients matters: the turn application controller holds one client per connection for the whole app lifetime, so a client-count gate would arm the service on every backgrounding even with zero traffic. The service starts only when I background with a live or reconnecting socket, and stops on resume, on `detached` (after detach no Dart isolate survives to stop it, so an orphaned service would pin the process forever), and in `dispose()`. `stop()` is unconditional so no state divergence can wedge it, and a cycle counter handles a stop landing while a start is still in flight.

This works for any number of concurrent sessions: one service pins the process, every session's heartbeat is its own timer inside its own `WsClient`, and the gate is an `any` over live clients.

## How I verified it

I ran a deep audit of the feature with an independent reviewer pass alongside my own, and every finding is fixed in the second commit: a back-exit path that orphaned the service with a permanent notification, a missed-stop race that could strand the notification, an unrecoverable stop guard, and the client-count gate described above. Each fix had a failing test written first, and I mutation-checked the key ones (reverting the detached handling turns the suite red). The full suite is 1337/1337 green and `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean. I also built and installed the release APK and confirmed in real use that minimizing no longer drops the connection.

title: fix: avoid duplicate assistant bubbles for previewed completions
body:
## Problem

When the gateway emits the final answer as `message.interim` and then sends `message.complete` with `response_previewed: true`, the chat displays the same answer twice. For example, a `3+4` request ends with two identical `7` bubbles.

## Changes

- Settle previewed/transformed completions onto the sealed interim message from the current user turn. Reused completions require an exact text match.
- Respect explicit `message.start` boundaries, keeping separate messages and repeated user turns distinct.
- Preserve late reasoning updates, including append/replace semantics and the latest verbose/collapsed state.
- Add widget regressions covering these event sequences.

## Validation

- All 20 tests in `test/chat_history_scroll_test.dart` passed.
- Static analysis of the changed files passed.
- Full analysis and test CI passed for the exact head commit: https://github.com/krotname/hermes-android/actions/runs/39232710402

body:

## Audit and release update (28 October 2026)

I completed the [historical contribution audit](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/aa0e2d78d070290d2fe4efd5ab6323024d4aee58/docs/licensing/README.md). For PR #88, the common base and all 56 source commits contain the same README blob with MIT. The merge keeps the MIT declaration in an updated README. The dossier documents the applicable GitHub D.6 contribution terms and their separate-agreement exception. I found no contrary public agreement in the reviewed discussions. I shipped the notice corrections in [signed v3.0.4](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/releases/tag/v3.0.4) at `aa0e2d78d070290d2fe4efd5ab6323024d4aee58`: the complete application MIT text, contributor attribution, and scoped Graphify, Hermes fixture, Flutter and Gradle notices. The Cinzel OFL and embedded Library LGPL terms, source and relink materials remain intact. I verified the three published ABI APKs, their production signer and 22 packaged source/notice assets per split, plus release hashes and the exact-commit source/relink bundle.

- [x] Document existing contribution-time licence evidence and scoped component terms.
- [x] Deliver complete MIT/attribution and third-party notices.
- [x] Publish a new immutable signed release and update the F-Droid MR.
- [x] Verify the exact-head F-Droid source-build and binary-comparison pipeline.

I verified that [F-Droid pipeline 2997044065](https://gitlab.com/samrussellmobile/fdroiddata-hermes/-/pipelines/2997044065) on `defaa46155e5fd07585a859ce22e295e15e4c706` passed all 9 jobs, including source building and signed-binary verification. I am closing the audit/release issue as completed. F-Droid maintainers retain the inclusion and network-review decision.

I updated [MR !45384](https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/merge_requests/45384) with the evidence, release pin and narrow source-scan adjustments. I also [clarified the old PR #88 confirmation request](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/88#issuecomment-6107817804). This audit does not certify original authorship of all third-party code or replace a legal opinion.

<details>
<summary>Original report, retained as historical context; the update above supersedes its waiting status</summary>

The F-Droid submission currently declares `License: MIT`, and the README says MIT, but the published app source has no top-level `LICENSE`. `NOTICE.md`, imported with the Community Remote Gateway edition, also says that the repository does not grant a licence for upstream code. These cannot be reconciled by adding an MIT file on behalf of contributors without checking their rights.

**Scope and evidence**

- @CristianGCiocoi has [explicitly confirmed MIT distribution of the code he authored in the Community Remote Gateway edition merged as `2d4bcd5`](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/issues/81#issuecomment-6108110695), while retaining his copyright. His confirmation expressly excludes third-party contributions.
- @CarlosReyesPena: [request for confirmation covering PR #88](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/88#issuecomment-6107817804) is still awaiting a response. This is a substantial 56-commit contribution.
- Other substantial merged contributions also require an explicit grant or documented pre-existing outbound licence: @Thaeland ([PR #106](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/106), [PR #137](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/137)); @maebahesioru ([PR #115](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/115), [PR #128](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/128)); @igitur ([PR #143](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/143), [PR #147](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/147), [PR #148](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/pull/148)). The remaining contributors and imported `Codex <codex@local>` commits also need provenance/attribution review before claiming an all-tree grant.

**Request to the named authors:** If you agree, please comment here (or on your linked PR): “I confirm that the code and other original material I authored and contributed to rusty4444/hermes-android may be distributed under the MIT License. Copyright in my contributions remains with me. This confirmation does not cover third-party material.” If any part cannot be licensed this way, please identify that part so we can resolve it separately. No response will be treated as consent.

**Completion criteria**

1. Record public, attributable confirmations or existing licence evidence for every material contribution; resolve any unlicensed third-party material without silently relicensing it.
2. Add a canonical MIT `LICENSE` with accurate copyright attribution, and replace the obsolete/contradictory `NOTICE.md` wording while preserving contributor credits and the unofficial-project disclaimer.
3. Publish a **new immutable signed release** containing both files, then update the F-Droid MR to that release and verify its reproducible-build pipeline. Do not repoint an existing tag or update fdroiddata to an incompletely licensed source tree.

Tracking this openly so contributors and F-Droid reviewers have one auditable place for the evidence.

title: Add resumable voice recordings with server-side transcription
body:
Continued in #164 after resolving conflicts against current `main`.
GitHub rejected reopening this closed PR through GraphQL and REST (HTTP422
without detailed errors). The updated commits remain on the same branch;
#164 is a draft and still documents outstanding physical-device testing.

Users can record a voice message in several parts, pause to think, preview the
combined clip and send one recognized message. A local draft survives leaving
the chat; backgrounding stops the microphone. The existing system-dictation
button and ordinary composer remain available.

During active recording, Android keeps the chat screen awake using its Activity
window flag. Pause, Stop, leaving the chat or manual locking releases the flag;
Continue enables it again. The device screen-timeout setting is unchanged, and
no wake-lock permission, microphone foreground service or new dependency is added.

The chat actions menu adds **Record voice message**. Send uploads M4A to the
configured Hermes Dashboard's existing authenticated `/api/audio/transcribe`
route in the selected profile, then submits the recognized text through the
existing REST, legacy Gateway or recovery transport. No new server endpoint,
client-side model or direct provider credentials are introduced. Dashboard
access and configured server STT are required; unsupported connections retain
the recording and show an actionable failure.

## Example: commenting on a long assistant reply

When reading a long assistant reply, a user may want to comment on several
separate points. They read one section, record a short comment, pause the
recording while reading the next section, then continue with another comment.
At the end, they can preview the combined recording and send all their feedback
as one message.

This keeps reading and thinking gaps out of the recording. It also lets the
assistant respond to the complete set of comments together, instead of starting
separate turns after each short fragment.

Draft safety:

- An unrelated typed draft and selected files are preserved.
- Transcription errors, prompt failures and uncertain acknowledgements retain
  the audio. Socket writes and HTTP headers alone do not discard it.
- Positive reply/tool activity, an authoritative recovery ACK or a new canonical
  user row can establish acceptance. There is no automatic prompt resubmission.
- Android joins local AAC/M4A fragments with its platform media APIs; journaled
  hashes protect recovery after an interrupted join. No FFmpeg is required.

Dependencies: pinned `record` 7.1.1 and `audioplayers` 6.8.1, plus their federated
packages. Existing locked dependencies are unchanged. New strings use
AppLocalizations; English is provided and other locales initially use its
generated fallback.

Validation: **1527 full Flutter tests**, static analysis and Android development
compilation pass. Ten added screen-awake cases cover pause/resume, draft safety,
permission/start/stop failures, background/start races, disposal ownership,
pending native replies, timer updates and unsupported platforms. Existing tests
cover interrupted joins, upload bounds, profile routing and acceptance/failure
boundaries across chat transports. Device testing of this isolated contribution's
microphone, real codec concatenation, playback and screen timeout is still required;
synthetic tests and compilation are not hardware acceptance.

The branch includes current `main` (v2.1.30, `63670ab3`) through a merge commit.
Conflict resolution preserves upstream's editable composer, Return/newline
behavior, unsent-prompt recovery and chat rename action. Voice transcription
uses the new submission boundary without clearing a separate typed/photo draft.
A regression test edits the composer while transcription is pending.

Details: `docs/VOICE_MESSAGE_DRAFTS.md`.

title: Support client certificates (mTLS) for gateway and dashboard connections
body:
## Summary

Add optional client-certificate (mTLS) authentication per connection, so the app can talk to a Hermes gateway/dashboard that sits behind a reverse proxy requiring a client cert.

## Why

Exposing the gateway API server (8642) and dashboard (9119) beyond the LAN is commonly done with nginx/Caddy in front, and TLS client certificates are the usual way to authenticate the phone there instead of putting a shared bearer key in front of an internet-facing port. Today the app cannot connect to such a deployment at all.

## Current behaviour

Against an nginx vhost with `ssl_verify_client on`, the TLS handshake is refused before anything reaches Hermes. The app shows a connection error and the server logs an HTTP 400 with nginx's short "No required SSL certificate was sent" body:

```
"GET /api/status HTTP/2.0" 400 237 "-" "ktor-client"
```

Verified independently: `curl https://host/` → 400, and the same request with a valid client cert → 302/200. So the proxy is healthy; the app simply never presents a certificate. Native Android HTTP stacks do not use user-installed KeyChain certificates unless the app explicitly asks for one — only browsers/WebViews prompt — so there is no user-side workaround today, and `ssl_verify_client` cannot reasonably be disabled on the server.

Also worth noting: a 400 with an opaque body is indistinguishable from "wrong URL / server down" in the UI. Surfacing the handshake failure or the upstream body would make this diagnosable without server logs.

## Prior art in this repo

PR #91 ("Add configurable Android mTLS transport", branch `giorgioughini-gateway-mtls`, sha `40863fea`) already proposed this:

- per-connection mTLS config in the Add/Edit Connection flow
- Android certificate picker, KeyChain alias remembered in secure storage
- native client for Gateway REST/SSE, dashboard REST and Desktop Gateway WebSocket when enabled
- separate dashboard URL/port reusing the selected certificate

It was closed by automation as not mergeable (branch conflicting, no update after changes requested), never merged — and `main` has no client-certificate plumbing today (no `SecurityContext`/OkHttp mTLS code under `lib/`). If the branch can be rebased, landing that work as-is would resolve this; otherwise a fresh implementation with the same shape is fine.

## Requested behaviour

- per-connection opt-in, disabled by default (existing deployments unaffected)
- certificate selected through the Android certificate picker; private key stays in KeyChain, app stores only the alias (matches the design of #91)
- applied consistently to gateway REST (`/api/sessions`, `/api/sessions/{id}/messages`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`), dashboard REST (Memory/Cron/Skills/Settings) and the Desktop Gateway WebSocket — a cert that authenticates REST but not the WS is worse than no support
- compose correctly with the existing custom-CA trust added in #108 (private CA for the server cert + client cert for the app is the normal pairing)
- fail closed and legibly: if mTLS is configured and the cert is missing/expired/rejected, show the TLS/short proxy body rather than a generic connection failure

## Acceptance

- with an nginx (or Caddy) vhost enforcing `ssl_verify_client on`, a connection configured with a client cert can list sessions and stream a chat turn
- without a certificate, the same endpoint still fails closed and the error names the cause
- HTTP-only LAN connections behave exactly as they do now

Happy to test a build against a real mTLS-proxied Hermes instance (nginx, client cert from a private CA) and report back with logs.

title: Support client certificates (mTLS) for gateway and dashboard connections
body:
## What this does

Adds optional, per-connection client-certificate (mTLS) authentication so the app can talk to a Hermes gateway/dashboard published behind a reverse proxy that enforces `ssl_verify_client on`.

Fixes #165.

## Why

Without this the feature described in #165 cannot work: the native TLS handshake sends no client certificate, so the proxy answers HTTP 400 ("No required SSL certificate was sent") before anything reaches Hermes (verified: no cert → 400, with a valid cert → 302/200). Android user-installed certificates are only used by browsers/WebViews, so there is no user-side workaround.

## Design (Dart only — no native code)

This is a fresh implementation, not a reopen of #91. #91 proposed OkHttp + Android KeyChain + platform channels; that branch closed unmergeable and conflicts with main, and none of it is needed here: the app's HTTP stack is already `dart:io` (`IOClient`, `IOWebSocketChannel`), and `SecurityContext` loads a cert + key pair directly. So this adds zero native code, zero platform channels, and zero new permissions.

## Changes

- **`lib/core/models/client_certificate.dart`** (new): immutable `ClientCertificateConfig` (label, cert/key paths in app-private storage, nullable key password), with `==`, `copyWith`, JSON.
- **`lib/core/services/client_certificate_service.dart`** (new): imports `.p12`/`.pfx` via `pkcs12_parser` (^1.1.0 — pure Dart; `Pkcs12.load` → `certificatePem`/`privateKeyPem`/`caChainPem`, chain concatenated leaf-first for `useCertificateChain`) or a PEM pair into a fresh `<appSupport>/client-certs/` dir. Typed user-facing errors for wrong-password vs unreadable-file; key material stays out of SharedPreferences and logs.
- **`lib/core/services/tls_client_factory.dart`** (new): `securityContextFor` (null → platform default), `createHttpClient` (keeps `idleTimeout = Duration.zero`, no `badCertificateCallback` — server trust stays platform-default), `createRestClient`. Unloadable cert → throw, never silently fall back.
- **Wiring**: `SavedConnection.clientCertificate` (+ `copyWith`/JSON/persistence); `ConnectionManager` API client, `DashboardClient`, `WsClient` (`customClient:`) and every construction site under `lib/` pass it through.
- **UI**: mTLS section in Add/Edit connection (HTTPS only): P12 picker (`file_picker`) + obscured password, or PEM cert/key pickers; shows the loaded label, Remove, and blocks saving a certificate-gated connection with nothing loaded.
- **l10n**: new keys in `app_en.arb` + regenerated localisations.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos` → **No issues found**
- `flutter test --no-pub` → **all 1509+21 tests pass** (incl. 4 new files: config round-trip, PEM + P12 import happy/wrong-password paths against a throwaway committed fixture, factory default/failure behaviour, end-to-end wiring through manager → REST → WS)
- `test/fixtures/` are throwaway OpenSSL certs (never real secrets), flagged in README + `pubspec.yaml` `false_secrets`

Debug-signed APK for testing: attached to the PR thread once the `release.yml` debug artifacts are available, or build locally with `flutter build apk --debug`.

## Screenshot / test notes welcome

Happy to test against a real mTLS-proxied Hermes (nginx, private CA) and report back. Keychain import (Android certificate picker) is deliberately out of scope for this PR — P12/PEM file import covers the flow with no permissions or native code; a picker could layer on top later reusing the same factory.

title: feat: inspect delegated task timelines above the parent chat
body:
## Summary

Tap a delegated task in the parent chat timeline to inspect its own read-only timeline in a phone sheet or wide-screen dialog. The parent chat remains mounted, including its composer, scroll and stream.

- Retain durable child-session references separately from subagent/delegation identity, including terminal failure/interruption status.
- Read bounded 50-row raw history pages through the authenticated Dashboard origin and selected Gateway profile; refresh active tasks in the foreground and offer explicit older-history loading.
- Render selectable Markdown, exposed reasoning and actual tool arguments/results, with stable collapsible sections.
- Recover retained structured references on reopening; explain when an older server did not persist a usable child reference.
- Keep parent-provided live previews clearly separate from recorded rows.

### Read-only safety

The viewer never opens a child socket or calls watch, resume, create, close, prompt, approval or task-control RPCs. Stock lazy watch attachment can affect runtime lifecycle, so it is deliberately not used. The API-server history fallback is not used because it omits richer reasoning metadata.

This shows reasoning the server exposes, not hidden/provider-private reasoning. Recorded history may lag a running task until it flushes. Missing historical child identities cannot be reconstructed. The viewer verifies newer live child references through bounded compression-lineage reads. Some stock servers cannot expose all compressed task segments; the viewer retains known content and labels that coverage **Partial history** instead of implying it is complete.

## Validation

- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos`: no issues.

title: feat(push): automatic background notifications without manual setup
body:
## Summary

Makes Android background push a one-toggle flow: enable **Background notifications**, then accept Android's permission prompt. On devices with working Google Play Services, users need no separate distributor app, push URLs, keys or chat IDs.

- Embed the open-source UnifiedPush FCM distributor (3.1.0), preserving existing external UnifiedPush choices and optional advanced transport selection. No Firebase/GMS client SDK, Firebase project or Google credentials are bundled/required.
- Subscribe to current and future durable chats allowed by the authenticated principal's live server policy. Old explicit-session consent is never silently broadened.
- Negotiate dynamic scope before permission/enrolment; bind authenticated event pages to installation/generation/scope; preserve encrypted challenge confirmation, monotonic revisions, revocation and selected-profile isolation.
- Carry the reviewed push registration/account-mutation hardening needed for safe automatic enrolment. Serialize saved-list transactions across managers, fence actual per-page notification lookups and capture event-specific observer-time ACL targets so later grants cannot authorise previously denied inbox events.
- Update Android/server setup and privacy documentation; retain adverse-order regressions, an actual Dart→Python TCP contract smoke test and recorded-command sealed-native replay.

## Server compatibility / migration

The paired `server/mobile-push` companion must be installed/enabled by the operator, with verified dashboard authentication and an explicit principal grant. This PR does not install or reconfigure a running server. `owner_all_sessions: true` is an operator decision for a personal owner—not a grant the app creates. Restricted accounts stay restricted.

Automatic enrolment requires advertised `session_scope_modes: ["explicit", "authorized"]`. Deploy the paired fenced client/server together. Missing/outdated/unauthorised servers fail visibly before permission or registration. Existing explicit subscriptions stay explicit until the user disables and opts in again.

## Verification

Locally executed against the repaired production candidate:

- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos`: clean.
- Full Flutter suite: **1,914 passed**, zero skipped; successful terminal JSON `done` event verified.
- Native Robolectric push/account tests, including the retained independent replay: **48 passed**, zero failures/errors/skips.
- Full Python suite with real-host tests and opt-in Dart TCP smoke: **240 passed**, zero skipped, on **Python 3.11.15** and **3.14.7**. One upstream Starlette/httpx deprecation warning.
- Actual `flutter build apk --debug`: passed.
- Resolved Android runtime dependency graph: no `com.google.firebase` or `com.google.android.gms` SDK artifacts.
- README release-window checks and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent SPEC review: PASS after reproducing/fixing three adverse schedules. Recorded Dart commands were replayed through real AES-GCM native persistence: preserved accounts deliver headlessly; removed accounts do not, without foreground repair.
- Independent code-quality review: **APPROVED**, 8.5/10, no critical/important findings. A nonblocking follow-up remains: Store construction can acquire a migration write lock for an event read, causing a transient safe 503 under concurrent-send contention; separating initialization from read-only access would improve availability.

The TCP smoke uses production Dart API serialization and Python router/models/store/runtime, genuine TLS Web Push/subscriber decryption/VAPID checks, future-chat events across two pages, corrupted later-page authority echoes, bounded 401 retries, rotation and revocation. Cookie verification, the disposable fixed profile and proof handoff are test-owned seams; separate real-host tests cover vetted profile mounting. Native tests inject key acquisition and distributor IPC; they are not physical-device results.

## Before release

- **Physical-device Google/UnifiedPush delivery, Doze/reboot/renewal and killed-process acceptance remain unverified.** No claim is made that emulator/JVM fixtures establish those behaviours. Android Force stop and OEM restrictions still apply.
- **Upstream licensing review remains a release gate:** embedded distributor 3.1.0's POM declares Apache-2.0 while its tagged LICENSE contains LGPL-2.1. The exact LGPL text and source/rebuild notice are retained. No dual-licence assumption, legal clearance or F-Droid approval is claimed.

title: fix: pick certificate files unfiltered on Android/iOS
body:
Fixes the client-certificate import flow in the connection dialog.

## Problem

Three separate issues made a client certificate nearly impossible to import on Android:

1. **PEM/CRT files were unpickable.** The picker used `FileType.custom` with
   `allowedExtensions`. Android's Storage Access Framework filters on MIME type,
   and `pem`/`key` have no `MimeTypeMap` entry while content providers hand back
   `application/octet-stream` — so SAF greyed out the exact files the user was
   trying to select.
2. **Three buttons for two import paths.** The UI mirrored the service
   (`importPemPair` vs `importPkcs12`) instead of what the user has in hand.
3. **The password had to be typed before picking.** The import ran with whatever
   the password field already held (usually nothing). A password-protected
   `.p12`/`.pfx` then failed, and the save gate reported "load a client
   certificate or turn off the client certificate option" — which reads as
   though the pick itself was lost.

## Changes

- **One picker.** A single `Choose certificate` button sniffs the picked bytes:
  PKCS#12 container, a single PEM document holding cert + key, or a lone half
  that is staged until its counterpart arrives (either order).
- **Unfiltered on Android/iOS.** Those platforms pick with `FileType.any` and
  let the service reject non-certificate bytes; desktop keeps the extension
  filter, where it works. A 1 MiB guard rejects mis-picks before reading.
- **Pick first, password after.** `ClientCertificateImportException` now carries
  `passwordRelated`, set for MAC and bad-password failures. On such a failure
  the dialog keeps the picked bytes, says the file needs its password, and
  retries the import (debounced) when the password field changes — so one pick
  plus a typed password succeeds without a second trip to the picker.
- An empty password on a protected container reports *needs a password*; a
  supplied-but-wrong password still reports *incorrect password*.

## Tests

`flutter analyze` clean; 110 tests pass across the certificate/mTLS suites,
including new coverage for the empty-password prompt, the wrong-password
classification, and a non-certificate file not being treated as password-related.

## Follow-up: password field visibility and loaded-certificate layout

Reported after on-device testing, both fixed here:

- **The password field was shown before any file was chosen**, implying a
  password had to be typed first. It now appears only once a pick reports that
  it is password-protected, autofocuses, and carries a one-line explanation.
- **Saving with an unopened pick said the wrong thing.** "Load a client
  certificate or turn off the client certificate option" reads as though no
  file had been chosen; that case now asks for the certificate password
  specifically.
- **The loaded-certificate row was cramped.** The file label sat beside
  *Remove certificate*, squeezing a long name into a sliver. The label and the
  button are stacked instead.

title: fix(chat): quiet conversation and collapsed verbose details
body:
## Chat behaviour

- With Verbose Mode off, show user messages and assistant replies with source-local successful completion evidence. Hide tools, reasoning, delegated tasks, reports, commentary, partial replies and source diagnostics.
- With Verbose Mode on, expose retained detail with expandable sections collapsed on entry. Preserve manual expansion during the visit, including lazy scrolling, and reset it after a genuine close/reopen.
- Show one current-activity bar above the composer in either mode. Keep failure and uncertain-outcome notices readable without a typing spinner, and keep approvals/input requests accessible.

## Completion and recovery safeguards

Preserve the RC's independent saved/received projections and existing admission/recovery authority. Do not match replies by text, order or an admission floor.

Reject unowned late completions before changing a newer response. Require successful SSE protocol completion rather than ordinary EOF, and keep error/partial receipts from becoming final through a later success bookend. Retain completed REST/SSE output against lagging history until an exact, authoritative response ID permits handover.

Revoke failed response presentation before settlement storage completes, preserve retained terminal authority across older resume/history results, and let recovery backoff handle repeated storage rejection without starving the UI. Keep parent scrolling stable beneath task inspection while allowing authorised end-follow to converge after collapsed rows change lazy-layout estimates.

## Saved-history compatibility

Metadata-free saved assistant rows do not establish finality. Quiet mode hides those rows, including older answers from gateways that omit completion metadata; Verbose Mode keeps them available. Current REST/SSE responses have no durable message ID and remain local to the chat visit. See [Chat presentation](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/45e61394197b4ec69d30bdea3aee722234c3487f/docs/chat-presentation.md).

title: Sending into an existing Desktop session fails silently (server refuses with `permission_denied`, app renders nothing)
body:
> _AI-assisted issue — written by @louquillio and Hermes Agent (Nous Research)._

### What happens

Opening an existing session that was created by the Hermes desktop app and sending a message produces no reply and no error. The message never arrives on the desktop either. Reading the same conversation works normally, so the app looks connected and the chat looks healthy.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a session created by the desktop app (source `local`, id `local-<hash>`).
2. Open it in the app from the chat list.
3. Send any message.

### Expected

Either the message is delivered, or the app says why it cannot be.

### Actual

The app POSTs `/v1/chat/completions` with `X-Hermes-Session-Id: local-<hash>`; the gateway refuses the turn and delivers the refusal in-band inside **HTTP 200**, which the app does not surface:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions -> 200, 1,027 bytes

data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant"},"finish_reason":null}], ...}
data: {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"error"}],
       "error":{"message":"permission_denied","type":"RuntimeStoreError"},
       "hermes":{"completed":true,"partial":false,"failed":true,
                 "error":"permission_denied","error_code":"agent_error"}}
data: [DONE]
```

Server side the same failure logs as `Agent task chatcmpl-… failed during SSE streaming: permission_denied`, with no `inbound message` line — the turn never dispatches.

Same client, same server, session created by the app itself (`mob-…`): HTTP 200 with the actual answer (~62 KB in my test). Reads are unaffected in both cases — `GET /api/sessions/<local-id>/messages` returns 200 with the full history, which is why the conversation looks fine right up until you send.

### Cause

The gateway does not accept a turn submitted through the `api_server` platform into a session whose source is `local`, and returns that refusal as a completion error rather than an HTTP failure. The app lists such sessions without distinguishing them, offers them as chats, and then discards the error event.

### Why this is a bug rather than a request for a new capability

- The chat list is fully selectable, and selecting an existing session presents the composer. A UI that hands you a composer for a chat is asserting that the chat is writable.
- If resuming existing threads were not supported, the composer would not be presented for them. If either surface is the secondary one, it is the `+` new-chat control, not the existing-session list.
- It also worked previously. The refresh behaviour is a separate matter and is not part of this report: a phone must pull before it can even list a session started on the desktop, and after a desktop turn the phone needs a manual refresh to show it. Switching a conversation between desktop and mobile is not well served by either interface today — but on the path that matters here, the turn itself went through.

So the app offers a writable chat and then discards the server's refusal, leaving a message that appears sent and a conversation that never receives it.

### Suggested fixes — either one removes the silent failure

- Surface `finish_reason: "error"` / `hermes.failed: true` as a visible error in the chat and keep the draft, rather than ending the turn silently.
- Label or filter sessions the app cannot post into. `/api/sessions` returns a `source` field per session (`local`, `api_server`, `cron`, `subagent`, `tool`, …), verified against this server, so read-only sessions can be marked in the list.

### Environment

- App 2.1.33 (build 2176, versionCode 21762, arm64-v8a)
- Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 17
- Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24), gateway API server on :8642
- Reproduced first on 1.0.8 and again after a clean install of 2.1.33

title: Full fork audit at 24c7d07 (3.0.0): 1 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 9 LOW — AI-generated, owner validation needed
body:
I ran a full audit of this fork at `24c7d07` (the 3.0.0 release merge) and I'm posting the results here for review.

> **Important:** This report was completed entirely by AI (me, acting as the auditing agent, with AI review subagents and an independent AI code-hunt pass). It may be incomplete or inaccurate. Several plausible-sounding findings were already caught and rejected during verification, but the owner will need to validate the accuracy of everything below before acting on it. Nothing here was changed in the code — this is a read-only audit.

*** Because this is a freshly released versio, I didn't want to try and fix anything as I was afraid I would be getting in the way of you implementing other features.  This version is definitely a better release than 2.0.  ***

## Toolchain and versions used

The red/green verification process ran on Linux (CachyOS) with:

- **Flutter 3.44.0** (stable, framework revision `559ffa3f75`) / **Dart 3.12.0** — `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` and the full `flutter test` suite
- **omp 18.12.6** — `omp cleanse -a` (checker sweep) and `omp -p --no-session` (independent fresh-context bug hunt)
- **Python 3.14.9** — `scripts/real_gateway_contract_probe.py` against a live stock `tui_gateway` in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`
- **Hermes Agent** with three scoped review subagents plus one independent hunt agent, all on model **Qwen3.8 Flash Next**

## Gates (all green)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` | clean, exit 0 |
| `flutter test` | **4366/4366 passed** (1m26s) |
| `real_gateway_contract_probe.py` (live stock gateway) | **PASS 5/5** |
| `omp cleanse -a` | dart analyze clean (ruff/gradle weren't on PATH, so `server/` and `android/` weren't machine-swept) |
| Independent OMP hunt on `desktop_gateway_client.dart` | 8 candidates; I verified 3 real and rejected 4 as false positives |
| 3 scoped review agents (transport / turn-lifecycle / app-shell) | 15 findings, each re-verified against the cited lines |

## HIGH

**H1. Stop during a recovery-v2 wind-down permanently re-locks the composer.**
`chat_screen.dart:5244` bumps `_responseGeneration` *before* calling `interrupt()`. The coordinator's `interrupt()` returns `_reconcile(uncertain)` (`gateway_turn_coordinator.dart:924`), which legitimately yields a **non-terminal** state when the server accepted the interrupt but the turn is still winding down. `_applyGatewayTurnState` then hits the `projection.isActive` branch and re-sets `_sending = _streaming = true` (`chat_screen.dart:2608-2612`). Every subsequent coordinator state — including the real terminal one — is fenced out by the generation bump in the submit's `onState` (`chat_screen.dart:4021`), and `_onTurnSettled` is background-only. The composer stays locked with a stale pending scaffold until a second Stop tap or screen re-entry. I found no test covering the non-terminal-interrupt screen path.

## MEDIUM

**M1. SSE body stream has no stall timeout.** `connection_manager.dart:1834-1888` — `GatewayChatClient.sendMessageStreaming` puts `.timeout(requestTimeout)` on every non-streaming HTTP call, but the SSE body subscription is unbounded and `await completion.future` never times out. A server (or a half-open TCP path after phone sleep / NAT drop) that sends 200 headers then stops emitting hangs the send in "generating" forever; `whenStreamSettled()` blocks indefinitely. No test covers a stalled body.

**M2. `getSessionById` trusts the `has_more` stop signal the codebase itself documents as lying.** `connection_manager.dart:1187` early-returns on `!hasMore && short page` *before* its own zero-new/pinBound exhaustion logic runs. `session_list_screen.dart:985-995` documents that stock "can report has_more=false while rows still exist past the offset" when a pin back-fills a page. A notification deep-link resolving a compression root can stop early and return a stale root row instead of the current continuation tip.

**M3. Stop tapped during the v2 submit window falls to the legacy interrupt.** `chat_screen.dart:5267` — if the first state callback hasn't fired yet (`_activeClientTurnId == null`), Stop takes the else branch and calls the legacy `_desktopGateway.interruptPrompt` instead of the coordinator interrupt. The coordinator turn is never interrupted through its own route, and the generation bump permanently discards the turn's state/content. (The client-side mechanism is verified; whether stock's session-level interrupt happens to catch the v2 turn server-side is untested.)

**M4. `PlatformException` from the share-intent bridge hangs startup on the splash forever.** `android_share_intent_service.dart:81-87` catches only `MissingPluginException`; a `PlatformException` from `getInitialShare` rejects the `Future.wait` in `_StartupAppState._initialize` (`main.dart:101`, no try/catch), so `setState` never runs and `build` never leaves the splash. The sibling launch service explicitly catches `PlatformException` ("A launcher failure must never prevent the app from opening normally") — the asymmetry looks unintended.

**M5. Unsupported `projects.tree` makes the Unassigned filter claim every chat.** `projects_repository.dart:334-337` returns `ProjectsTreeOverview.empty` *without throwing* when the method is unsupported; `readProjects` (`workspace_screen.dart:1570-1585`) then sets `claimed = {}` and `projectsKnown = true`, so `projectsKnown && !claimed.contains(id)` marks **every** chat unassigned — including cwd-filed ones. This contradicts the repo's own docstring ("degrades only the extra metadata") and the screen's contract that an empty claimed set must mean "unknown". The fix shape already exists: the catch path sets `projectsKnown = false` — the unsupported return should do the same.

## LOW

- **L1.** `close()` leaves `_sessionBoundListener`/`_sessionCreatedListener` set (`desktop_gateway_client.dart:1268-1297`), and the `_connect` path lacks the `_closed` re-check that `resumeSubmittedSession` has — a `session.resume` completing after close fires callbacks into a torn-down owner and repopulates maps `close()` cleared.
- **L2.** `getArchivedSessions` terminates on server-reported `total` (`connection_manager.dart:2466-2471`) when present, contradicting its own docstring's "never trust total" rule; silent truncation if total under-reports. An inline comment argues stock is safe — flagged as a policy contradiction.
- **L3.** `getMessages` interpolates `sessionId` raw into the URL (`connection_manager.dart:1298-1299`) while every sibling method uses `Uri.encodeComponent`.
- **L4.** `respondToClarify` fallback sends the client-namespaced local key as the wire `request_id` after the request was forgotten on socket drop (`desktop_gateway_client.dart:1190-1194`), instead of the explicit local rejection `respondToApproval` uses for the same situation.
- **L5.** `_stopResponseInFlight` is cleared without `setState` in the transport-branch `finally` (`chat_screen.dart:5329`); the normal branch at 5232 does it correctly. Send stays gated until an unrelated rebuild.
- **L6.** Send with empty text + staged attachments while streaming silently no-ops (`chat_screen.dart:3482`): `if (_streaming) { if (text.isNotEmpty) await _sendWhileWorking(text); return; }` — attachments never considered.
- **L7.** `resetConnections()` orphans every credential bundle (`connection_manager.dart:670-697`): it collects connection ids for native push revocation but deletes only the `saved_connections` metadata key; each `connection_credentials_v1.<id>` bundle (API keys, dashboard passwords, PEM passwords) stays in the secure store with no code path that will ever remove it.
- **L8.** `ChatSpaceStore._save` ignores the `setString` bool (`chat_space_store.dart:210-218`): a rejected write reports success and the change vanishes on restart; both sibling stores (`QuickChatStore`, `LocalChatPinStore`) throw on `!saved`.
- **L9.** `bindStoredSession` adds to `_resumeOnlySessions` before validating (`desktop_gateway_client.dart:606-612`): a rejected re-bind (StateError) leaves the id permanently resume-only.

## Rejected after verification (kept here so nobody re-fixes them)

- **Rebind-guard race** — claimed the `Timer(0)` guard in `_rebindStoredSessions` sees a stale `_ws`. Wrong: `connect()` returns synchronously after firing the connected callback, so the `_ws = client` assignment runs as a microtask *before* the `Timer(0)` hop; the guard passes by design.
- **"No timeout on ticket mint / handshake"** — the handshake has `channel.ready.timeout(15s)` (`ws_client.dart:354`) and the ticket mint has `.timeout(ApiClient.requestTimeout)` (`connection_manager.dart:2226`).
- **Stale `_bindingInFlight` across sockets** — `_handleClosedConnection` rejects every pending call when the socket dies, so in-flight futures fail and self-remove; no stale-success path found.
- **`_serverRequestClientOrdinals` leak** — failed connects still run `_handleClosedConnection` (`wasConnected` is true whenever `_channel` was set), which fires `onConnectionClosed` and forgets ordinals. Only leaks if URL construction itself throws.
- **Spurious reconnect on intentional close** — real that the old client's `close()` fires `onConnectionChanged(false)` → transient disconnected event + reconnect timer, but the timer is cancelled and `_reconnectAttempts` reset when the new socket connects. Cosmetic blip only.

## Regression sweep

All previously-fixed bug classes from the earlier audit round verified still holding: single-flight `_ensureSocket`/`_resumeOrCreateSingle`, credential rollback reading stored values, auth single-flight with generation check, stale-binding recovery guard, reattach resync by stored key with durable-id watermarks, both session-list pagers terminating client-side (zero-new + pinBound, never `has_more`), page caps throwing, prune per-ID 404 confirmation with accumulator clearing, claims from placement map excluding `__no_project__`, `projects.list`-only family disowning, archived-excluded name matching, temp-export purge, PBKDF2+AES-GCM config backup, and the corrupt-store startup recovery screen. I also checked `SECURITY.md` claims against the code and found no contradictions.

## Notes

- The audit tree was one commit behind `origin/main` at the time of the run; re-running the gates after pulling is advised.
- `omp cleanse` could not sweep `server/` (no ruff) or `android/` (no gradle on PATH) — those corners were covered only by the review agents' manual reads.

Again — this report is AI-generated and may be incomplete or inaccurate; please validate each finding against the current code before acting on it.

title: feat(chat): attach long pastes as paste.txt
body:
## Summary

- Convert committed paste-sized insertions **over 3,000 UTF-16 code units** into `paste.txt` attachments in Remote Gateway chats, matching the Desktop character threshold. Subsequent names are collision-safe (`paste-2.txt`, etc.). Short pastes and legacy REST remain inline.
- Keep surrounding instructions and preserve the exact pasted UTF-8 content, including Unicode, whitespace and CRLF. Reuse the existing file-backed cache, attachment limits, ordered `file.attach` uploads and gateway-returned references; nothing uploads before **Send**.
- Fence asynchronous preparation against edits, clearing, replacement draft writers, disposal and voice startup. Keep text inline on preparation/limit failure. Carry complete paste recovery into the app owner so a detached pre-wire rejection cannot lose it; mounted recovery does not duplicate the paste as both inline text and an attachment.
- Preserve unsent paste content through existing text-draft checkpoints and restore it inline on reopen. Attachment removal commits its draft intent before asynchronous cleanup. Nonempty whitespace is now literal draft content; only an explicit empty string clears a draft.
- Add user documentation, README coverage and translated fallback copy in all 11 shipped locale ARBs, with regenerated localisations.

title: feat: add opt-in foreground hands-free voice (#142)
body:
Refs #142.

**Ready for review.** Independent SPEC and integrated QUALITY reviews approved `a33ba81c1deb44e589878307cb1e30373557f5ac`. Full Flutter/native tests, debug and unsigned R8 builds, default-off emulator startup and both GitHub CI workflows passed. Physical voice acceptance remains open.

## Foreground hands-free mode

Add an Android **“Hey Hermes”** loop in the open foreground chat, off by default. Start requires user confirmation; the app does not restore running consent.

1. Run local English keyword spotting, then release its recorder before Android recognition.
2. Admit one prompt through the normal send path after a nonempty recognizer final and native teardown. Keep partial speech and the manual draft separate.
3. Speak that admitted turn's successful public final reply through the existing FlutterTts instance and selected voice/rate.
4. Keep capture off until the owned playback result and 300 ms echo guard finish. Follow-up accepts 0–30 seconds, default 10; zero requires a new wake phrase.

Stop stays accessible during capture, waiting, playback and errors. Route coverage, account/session changes, background/lock, permission loss and manual interaction revoke consent before asynchronous work continues. Resume and permission grants do not restart capture. Manual dictation remains draft-only; voice Stop does not interrupt a submitted chat turn.

## Native ownership and inputs

- Wake and speech recognition share one joinable native audio owner with generation/request/sequence fences. Decode and worker joins stay off the UI thread. Native Activity/engine teardown also stops capture.
- Use pinned sherpa-onnx **2.0.1** and the GigaSpeech **3.3M int8** model. Build preparation verifies artifact/model hashes and packages licences/notices; the app does not download models at runtime.
- Keep FlutterTts **4.2.5** hosted Dart and non-Android source unchanged. The Android source patch owns results by utterance/epoch, rejects stale queued callbacks and revokes pending starts on Stop. Build guards check upstream/patch hashes, native source inventory and exact compiler inputs. Retain the upstream MIT licence.
- The Android speaker consumes owned native terminal results rather than uncorrelated global completion/cancel/error callbacks. Local cancellation/deadline guards remain, along with the legacy non-Android callback path.
- No wake PCM storage/upload, speech transcript logging, enrollment or API key. **Offline wake does not make the conversation offline:** Android recognition, the selected reply voice and the gateway may use networks.

## Verification on the frozen head

- **4,546 full-suite Flutter cases passed**, zero skips, errors or unfinished cases. Offline dependency resolution and strict analysis passed.
- Forced tests on CI-pinned **Gradle 9.1.0** passed **93 app-native tests**, **10 actual-plugin TTS regression tests** and **16 preparation/CI Python tests** with real pinned cached inputs and zero skips. The downloaded CI JUnit reports contain the same native case identities as the local run.
- SPEC and QUALITY: **APPROVED**. Reviewers reproduced the original native Stop A → speak B → late A completion defect, checked queued/init/error/focus siblings and replayed the real Dart speaker/controller. B stays pending with capture off until its own result and the full echo guard. `Q142-TTS-01` is resolved.
- The debug APK installed on the owned API 35 ARM64 emulator. Installed bytes matched the host SHA-256; the app rendered onboarding with microphone permission denied and no voice session started.
- The **unsigned** all-ABI release assembled with R8. Model/notices/hashes, JNI keep rules, all 24 native libraries and static 16 KB ELF/ZIP alignment passed inspection for ARMv7, ARM64 and x86_64. No production key used; no physical 16 KB-page launch claim.
- The pinned engine detected six labelled synthetic positives and rejected seven negatives on Mac CPU and Android ARM64 AAR/JNI, with fresh-process replays and no tuning. This measures synthetic engine compatibility, not human microphone accuracy or field false accepts.
- GitHub CI passed: [PR Quality Checks](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/actions/runs/40510846333), [Native Android and Push Server](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/actions/runs/40510846324). CI runs both native test modules and retains their HTML/XML reports.

## Limits and known follow-up

Physical microphone → STT → gateway → TTS testing, Android 14–16 permission/privacy/lock/provider scenarios, human accents/noise, Bluetooth/car mode, battery/thermal/latency measurements, source-built AAR/F-Droid acceptance and physical 16 KB-page launch remain unverified. No background microphone service, always-on hardware hotword or same-breath pre-roll guarantee. Say the phrase, wait for Ready, then speak.

**Low-priority `N142-TTS-01`:** an unused direct Android plugin call with `awaitSpeakCompletion(false)` can leave its result pending after an immediate platform ERROR. Current Android hands-free and Read aloud callers enable awaited completion; reviewers tested that error path and observed owned result `0`, capture off. Add a regression and settle the direct result before introducing a non-awaited Android caller. This does not block the current app-used path.

#214 (#207) and #215 (#84) share chat/coordinator paths. A separate local reconciliation at `587a14f8bad1672300681bdd461f108de2ec3580` preserves all three intents and passed strict analysis and **4,700 full-suite Flutter cases**, with zero skips, errors or unfinished cases and all 948 tracked source files unchanged. Coordinate the chat/changelog merge hunks rather than concatenating callbacks. This local combined result does not replace the individual PR heads, their CI or physical-device acceptance.

[Setup, disclosures, implementation and primary sources](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/a33ba81c1deb44e589878307cb1e30373557f5ac/docs/HANDS_FREE_VOICE.md).

No version bump, dependency/model/gateway upgrade, production signing, main merge or release. Leave #142 open for physical-device/release acceptance. Thanks @mannok for the proposal. Existing contributor history and credits remain. Hermes Agent assisted with research, implementation, independent review, documentation and tests.
