title: fix(approvals): keep dismissal on the route that opened the dialog
body:
## What

When a gateway approval dialog is dismissed, the dismissal resolves against
whatever route is current at that moment. Navigate to another chat while the
dialog is up and the dismissal lands on the wrong chat, or the pending
approval is left orphaned.

## Fix

Capture the originating route (connection + session) when the dialog is
raised. Dismissal always goes back to that route.

## Testing

- new `test/chat_approval_route_ownership_test.dart`: dismissal across
  navigation, competing surfaces, and duplicate routes
- test files here pass in full, `flutter analyze` clean; the two failing
  tests on base `main` are pre-existing and in unrelated files

title: fix(chat): settle stock idle turns only on owned successful completion receipts
body:
## What

An interrupted turn can settle as successful on evidence that doesn't prove
it: an idle status, an empty or loosely-matched completion, or a receipt from
before the response scope moved on. Seen as completed-looking turns after
reconnects where the response was actually partial or foreign, and as
"outcome could not be confirmed" banners on turns that had a legitimate
receipt.

## Fix

A stock idle turn now settles success only on an owned successful completion
receipt that matches the response scope actually observed for the current
turn:

- completion text must be nonempty and match exactly (no empty-payload or
  generic suffix shortcuts)
- later body activity, or steering accepted in the same generation, revokes
  an earlier receipt; a later matching completion can re-establish it
- receipt evidence is captured from the response row the completion actually
  selected, before that row is overwritten
- idle alone releases admission without inventing success or failure

Known limit: the gateway doesn't put turn ids on these completions, so an
identical-text replay is still indistinguishable. This narrows the authority
surface but isn't replay-proof identity.

## Testing

- new `test/normal_gateway_stock_idle_settlement_test.dart`: interrupted
  turns stay unknown without a valid final receipt
- extended `test/normal_gateway_response_presentation_test.dart`: reused
  previews, transformed output, steering revocation, empty-payload rejection,
  global-ingress ID-less deliveries, foreign/mismatched payloads staying
  unknown
- test files here pass in full, `flutter analyze` clean; the two failing
  tests on base `main` are pre-existing and in unrelated files

title: Prompt submissions over WS carry no idempotency key
body:
Submitting the same prompt twice over the websocket results in two full
turns: two durable user rows, two assistant replies, two model calls.

There doesn't appear to be any idempotency key on the submit path
(`runs_idempotency.db` stays empty), so nothing client- or server-side
dedupes a repeated submission. Any retry, replay, or double-send at the
transport level becomes a duplicate turn, and with an allowlisted command
saved via "Always allow" a duplicate submission would run the command again.

Suggestion: carry a client-generated idempotency key on the prompt submit
RPC and treat a repeat key as a fetch of the existing run rather than a new
one. Not reporting a specific duplicate-submission bug here — just the
missing dedupe surface that would make any such bug harmless.

title: Accepted prompt re-delivered into the running turn on client reconnect/interface switch (stored once, executed once, agent saw it 6 times).
body:
I usually run in verbose mode as I like to watch the processing and thinking as it happens. I started to see this a few days ago so I had Hermes check my last 7 days of chats session and this is what it found.


## Summary

An already-accepted prompt is re-delivered into the **running** agent turn when the client reconnects or switches interfaces. The gateway accepts, stores, and executes the message exactly once, but the agent sees the same user message several times and restarts work each time, which looks to the user like their input was submitted twice.

This is AI-generated analysis (log and database evidence below is verbatim); owner validation needed.

## Environment

- App: Hermes Android 3.0.5 (versionCode 30092), production APK
- Gateway: stock Hermes Agent v0.22.5+794.g7a39461 (local 7a3946184153)
- Session: `20261028_045019_1deef1` (source `desktop` — the Android app records as `desktop`), 2026-10-28, phone peer `100.106.66.93`
- The user switched between webui, desktop, and the Android app during the window

## Symptom

The user sent one message ("Review chat sessions from the last 7 days…", 494 chars incl. the Android client-context block). The agent received that same message **six times** over roughly 40 minutes and resumed work on each arrival. The user never re-sent it.

## Layer-by-layer evidence

Counting the same message text at each layer:

| Layer | Source | Count | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | `gui.log` | **1** | `10:43:17,375 tui prompt accepted: ui_session=1370dd62 session_key=202610...eef1 agent_session_id=20261028_045019_1deef1 kind=user chars=494` |
| Storage | `state.db` `messages` | **1** | `id=126348, active=1, 10:43:17.373` — `select count(*) … where content like '%inputs were being submitted twice%'` returns 1 |
| Execution | `agent.log` | **1** | `10:43:17,383 conversation turn: session=20261028_045019_1deef1 … msg='Review chat sessions from the last 7 days…'` — the only `conversation turn` line containing that text |
| Agent context | live conversation | **6** | the same user text re-entered the running turn six times, each triggering new tool work |

Transport correlation from `gui.log` (tui_gateway log):

```
10:40:14,827 ws accepted peer=100.106.66.93:38018
10:40:14,897 ws accepted peer=100.106.66.93:38030
10:43:17,375 tui prompt accepted: … chars=494
10:59:53,887 ws closed peer=…:38030 reason=client_disconnect(code=1005) detached_sessions=0
10:59:53,902 ws closed peer=…:38018 reason=client_disconnect(code=1005) detached_sessions=1
10:59:56,920 ws accepted peer=100.106.66.93:58258
10:59:56,988 ws accepted peer=100.106.66.93:58272
```

The re-deliveries line up with the detach/reattach cycles and interface switches. The next genuinely new user message ("Yes", 11:03:49) was accepted and stored normally, so the session itself stayed healthy.

## Why this is distinct from #222

#222 reports the missing idempotency key on the submit path, where a double submission produces two durable rows and two turns. Here the opposite signature holds: **one acceptance, one row, one execution** — the duplication happens *after* admission, when the already-accepted prompt is replayed into the running turn on reattach. A client-generated idempotency key on the submit RPC would not catch this, because no second submit is accepted. The two issues are complementary: #222 hardens the submit surface; this one is in the reattach/delivery path.

## Suggested investigation

- What replays the last accepted prompt into a live turn when a WS client reattaches to a detached session (`detached_sessions=1` → fresh `ws accepted` pair)?
- Does the interface-switch path (same session key claimed by a different client) re-inject the pending prompt as a fresh user message into the running turn?
- The re-injected copies should be deduped against the already-admitted prompt (e.g. by admission/request id) before re-entering the agent loop.

## Notes on method (for validation)

- `gui.log` is the tui_gateway log; `gateway.log` is the platform log.
- Exact-duplicate rows in `messages` with identical timestamps and `active=0` (visible around Oct 21–22) are history-rewrite artifacts, not re-runs, and were excluded.
- Near-duplicate text scans must strip the `[Hermes Android client context v1]` wrapper first, or every app message pair looks similar.

title: Make mobile notifications clearer and more private
body:
Makes the mobile push notification experience easier to read and stops it from leaking command details to the lock screen.

What changes:

- Notifications say which connection they belong to and what state that connection is in, instead of a generic label that could mean anything. Bound-elsewhere is spelled out.
- Approval and input notifications use generic body text, so command/request details never appear in the notification surface. The full request is waiting in the app when you open it. Session titles stay visible so you still know which conversation wants you.
- Status, errors and recovery actions sit next to the control they affect instead of being buried further down settings.
- Turning local notifications off explains plainly what it does and does not change: background consent is untouched, ordinary hints are just muted until you turn it back on.
- The silent verification step says what it is: pending encrypted challenge, waiting for the server's check.
- The background notifications switch exposes a stable accessibility id and a complete label for screen readers.
- Connection state cues don't rely on color alone, and the layout holds up with long connection names and large text sizes.

One behavior note so expectations are right: when the app is in the background the gateway connection is closed on purpose, so background events surface as the generic server-activity push hint. The approve/deny prompts and full request details live in the app. That split is intentional.

Testing: flutter analyze is clean on the seven changed files and the full project on top of main at 0ee46af, and the focused test files pass (28 + 4 + 20).

title: Switching apps mid-turn destroys the turn on API-server (REST SSE) chats — foreground keep-alive never engages, beginLegacyTurn has no production caller
body:
## Summary

On a **stock Hermes gateway (API-server mode, REST `POST /v1/chat/completions` + SSE)**, switching to another app mid-turn destroys the turn. The server reads the dropped socket as an interrupt (`Interrupt requested (hard): sse client disconnected`) and the tool work is gone. The app surfaces it as `Send failed: ClientException: Connection closed while receiving data`.

Settings → Background work → **Keep chats active in the background** does not protect these chats: on this transport the foreground keep-alive can never start. As far as I can trace it, that is because the only writer of stock-turn activity (`beginLegacyTurn`/`endLegacyTurn`) has no production caller at HEAD, and REST sends never register as turn activity.

## What happens

Server side, stock Hermes Agent 0.22.2, this phone, one session on 2026-10-28 (7 `SSE client disconnected` events in that session, 5 of them while an approval prompt was pending):

```
21:01:20,571 INFO [session] agent.conversation_loop: API call #11: ...          <- model returned a tool call needing approval
21:01:32,357 INFO run_agent: Interrupt requested (hard): sse client disconnected
21:01:32,358 INFO gateway.platforms.api_server: SSE client disconnected; interrupted agent task chatcmpl-edcdc31d712341f19d614db2c5833
21:01:33,319 INFO tools.approval: Approval wait interrupted — returning deny for session chatcmpl-edcdc31d712341f19d614db2c5833
21:01:34,048 INFO [session] agent.conversation_loop: Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_system(sse_client_disconnected) ... response_len=0
```

Two more in the same session, same shape:

```
21:17:27,673 API call #2  ->  21:17:37,767 Interrupt requested (hard): sse client disconnected
21:17:43,867 API call #1  ->  21:17:53,968 Interrupt requested (hard): sse client disconnected
```

The drops land ~10–11 s after the approval request is emitted and coincide with my switching to another app. That timing is consistent with the process being frozen shortly after it leaves the foreground on this device (Samsung cached-app handling), **not** with the client's own silence bound (see below).

App side, on return:

```
Send failed: ClientException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri=https://<host>:8642/v1/chat/completions
```

That is `send_failed` (`lib/l10n/app_en.arb`), raised from the REST `onError` path (`lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:3917`, `_handleSendError(..., removePendingUserMessage: true)`). So the prompt had already been accepted and tools had already run, but the app reports a failed send and drops the pending user message — losing the work and the prompt together.

## Why the keep-alive does not engage (trace at `0ee46af`)

- The foreground service is gated on turn activity: `lib/main.dart:398-400` and `:497-499` pass `hasActiveTurn: _turnApplicationController.hasActiveTurn` into `ConnectionKeepAliveService.onAppLifecycleState()`.
- [`ConnectionKeepAliveService`](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/0ee46af36828be42913b91b5c8630ec7d010b04a/lib/core/services/connection_keepalive_service.dart#L114-L121) starts only when `_enabled && _hasActiveTurn`.
- [`hasActiveTurn`](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/0ee46af36828be42913b91b5c8630ec7d010b04a/lib/core/services/gateway_turn_application_controller.dart#L306-L309) is `_legacyTurns.isNotEmpty || <recovery-v2 sessions>`. Recovery-v2 sessions never exist on a stock gateway (#84).
- `_legacyTurns` is written **only** by `beginLegacyTurn()`/`endLegacyTurn()` (`:317`, `:328`). At `0ee46af` neither has a caller under `lib/` — `grep -rn 'beginLegacyTurn\|endLegacyTurn' lib/` returns the definitions and the doc comments only (tests do call them).
- The REST send never touches turn activity: `lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:3747` sets `_activeResponseTransport = _ResponseTransport.rest`, then `:3788` calls `GatewayChatClient.sendMessageStreaming()` → [`connection_manager.dart:1834`](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/0ee46af36828be42913b91b5c8630ec7d010b04a/lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart#L1834) `POST /v1/chat/completions`.

Net effect: on API-server chats `hasActiveTurn` stays `false`, `ConnectionKeepAliveService.start()` is never invoked, no foreground service exists, and the process is free to be frozen the moment another app comes forward. The setting in Settings → Background work is a no-op for these chats even though it defaults to enabled (`background_work_prefs.dart:6`).

Please correct me if `beginLegacyTurn` is wired somewhere I missed — I grepped the sparse `lib/` tree at `0ee46af`, not a built APK.

## This is not #112 and not the 60 s silence bound

- #112 was the screen-dispose case, fixed in `24ccbdf` by detaching the stream instead of closing the client. This is process suspension, not `dispose()`.
- [`streamInactivityTimeout`](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/0ee46af36828be42913b91b5c8630ec7d010b04a/lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart#L1567-L1571) is 60 s and raw bytes renew it. I verified stock Hermes emits `: keepalive` every 10 s during a silent tool run (a 25 s `sleep` produced two keepalive frames and the stream finished cleanly), and a plain `curl` client over the same Tailscale HTTPS URL survives such a run. So the socket is not dying of starvation — the process holding it is being frozen.

## Reproduction

1. Stock Hermes Agent (0.22.2 here), API-server mode over Tailscale HTTPS (`:8642` → `127.0.0.1:8642`).
2. Send a prompt that runs tools for more than ~30 s, or one that raises an approval prompt.
3. Switch to another app for ~15 s, then return.
4. Server logs `Interrupt requested (hard): sse client disconnected`; the app shows `Send failed: ClientException: Connection closed while receiving data`; the tool work is lost and the transcript keeps the server's interrupted placeholder.

## Options

1. **Register REST sends as turn activity** so the shipped foreground service engages — wrap the `sendMessageStreaming` call (or have `GatewayChatClient` expose it) with `beginLegacyTurn()`/`endLegacyTurn()`. Smallest change, reuses existing code and tests. Honest caveat: a foreground service raises process priority; it does not survive force-stop or Doze kill, and after a real process death there is still no durable run to reattach to (that remains #149's `/v1/runs` work).
2. **Durable `/v1/runs` for API-server chats** (separate transport project per #149). Worth recording that this genuinely decouples the turn from the device: I started a run with `POST /v1/runs`, held no connection at all, and 40 s later `GET /v1/runs/{id}` returned `status: completed` with the expected output. Nothing to freeze, nothing to lose.
3. **On resume, reconcile instead of reporting a failed send.** The prompt was accepted and the turn ran; treating a mid-turn socket death as a rejected send (`removePendingUserMessage: true`) discards both the prompt and the evidence, and is what makes this feel like data loss rather than an interruption.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **0.22.2** (stock, `d923a5eb`, Linux), API server on `127.0.0.1:8642` behind `tailscale serve` (tailnet-only, `API_SERVER_KEY` auth, TLS verifies).
- Phone: Samsung Galaxy A56, Android, Tailscale direct path to the host.
- App version: unknown from the server side — on this transport the only client identification reaching the server is `Dart/3.12 (dart:io)`; `_headers` sends `Authorization` and `Content-Type` only (`connection_manager.dart:1167`), and no query/body field carries the build. A version header (or UA suffix) on API-server requests would make reports like this one self-identifying.

Happy to capture wire-level traces or a screen recording of the freeze if useful; I can also instrument `hasActiveTurn` in a local build to confirm the gate.

title: fix(chat): register API-server sends as app-wide turn activity (#225)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #225: on the stock Hermes gateway's API-server transport (REST `POST /v1/chat/completions` + SSE), a send never registered as app-wide turn activity, so **Settings → Background work → Keep chats active in the background** could not engage the foreground service. Backgrounding the phone mid-turn froze the process; the server read the dropped socket as an interrupt (`sse client disconnected`) and the app reported a failed send, discarding the pending prompt and the already-run tool work.

## Fix

Wrap the API-server send in `beginLegacyTurn()`/`endLegacyTurn()` on the injected app-wide turn-application controller:

- The registration lives for the whole streaming lifetime and is released in `finally` when the stream settles — terminal, error, superseded or cancelled — so a mid-turn disconnect cannot leak it.
- The desktop/WS path already reports turn activity through normal-session registration; the recovery-v2 path reports through its coordinator. This closes the gap on the remaining transport.

## Tests

New `test/rest_legacy_turn_keepalive_test.dart`:

- `REST send registers app-wide turn activity until the stream settles` — asserts `hasActiveTurn` is true while the SSE stream is in flight and false after terminal completion.
- `mid-turn SSE disconnect releases the REST turn registration` — reproduces the issue's exact failure (socket drop mid-stream → `Connection closed while receiving data`), asserts the registration is released and the draft is restored.

Local verification on main `0ee46af` (Flutter 3.44.0): `flutter analyze` clean on changed files; the new suite and the related `gateway_turn_legacy_turn_keepalive_test.dart` / `chat_sse_retention_test.dart` suites pass.

## Docs

`docs/android-background-work.md` now states that API-server sends register as active turns so protection engages while the turn is in flight, with the honest caveat that protection does not survive force-stop/Doze/OEM killers, and that durable `/v1/runs` reattach on this transport remains tracked in #149.

## Risk

Low. The controller token release is a no-op on unknown/double-ended tokens; a superseded concurrent send releases its own token via its own `finally`. The foreground service is still gated on the existing Background work policy; nothing here starts it without the user's stored choice.

title: REST/API-server transport has no approval path: `event: approval.request` is rejected as "malformed SSE choices" and no /v1/runs/{id}/approval responder exists
body:
## Summary

On the **REST / API-server transport** (`POST /v1/chat/completions` + SSE) there is no approval path at all. Any turn that needs a command approval dies immediately with:

```
Send failed: Gateway sent malformed SSE choices.
```

The approval frame itself is unparseable, there is no dialog to answer it, and the app never calls the REST endpoint that resolves it. Approvals work only on the dashboard JSON-RPC transport.

This is the next failure in the same flow as #225 / #226: v3.0.6 keeps the REST send alive in the background, so the stream now survives long enough to *receive* the approval frame — and the decoder rejects it.

## Client side: why the frame is fatal

`_decodeSseFrame` (`lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart:1666`) special-cases only three event types before treating every payload as an OpenAI completion chunk:

- `event: error` — `:1681`
- `event: hermes.tool.progress` — `:1715`
- `event: hermes.status` — `:1718`

Everything else reaches the chunk validator, and `:1727` rejects a payload whose `choices` is a non-empty list of non-objects:

```dart
if (choices is! List || choices.first is! Map) {
  return const _SseFrame(error: 'Gateway sent malformed SSE choices.');
}
```

`acceptFrame` (`:1879`) treats any frame error as terminal — `finishBody(error)` at `:1882` — so the send aborts on the approval frame and the user sees it as a failed send.

I diffed `_decodeSseFrame` between **v3.0.6** and **v3.1.0**: byte-identical. The decoder did not regress; the difference is that the send now survives to the frame.

## Server side: what the frame contains

- `gateway/platforms/api_server.py:107` `_approval_event_choices()` returns the button ids: `["once", "session", "always", "deny"]` (or the shorter variants when `session`/`always` are not allowed).
- `api_server.py:113` `_approval_request_event()` puts them on the event payload as `choices`, next to the redacted `command`, `reason`, `session_id`, and the `_run_event` envelope (`event`, `run_id`, `timestamp`).
- `gateway/platforms/api_server_openai_routes.py:918` writes that payload on the same chat-completions stream: `_sse_frame(delta[1], event="approval.request")`.

So the frame carries a field named `choices` whose values are approval *scopes*, not completion choices. That name collision is what trips the validator.

## Why nothing rescues it: approvals are WS-only in the app

The app's approval subsystem is complete, and entirely wired to the dashboard transport:

- **Dispatch**: `ws_client.dart:570-578` routes server→client JSON-RPC requests (string ids `srq-…`) into `_deliverServerRequest` (`:635`); the answer goes back as `approval.respond {session_id, choice}` (`:1106-1132`), validated against `once|session|always|deny`.
- **Model**: `lib/core/models/gateway_approval.dart:39` `GatewayApprovalRequest.fromEventData` already parses exactly this payload shape — `choices` as strings, plus `smart_denied` / `allow_permanent` pruning.
- **UI**: `_showGatewayApproval` (`lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart:5534`) + `GatewayApprovalDialog`, with the prompt queues for clarify/sudo/secret so only one prompt is open and Back = deny.
- **Not the REST path**: `_showGatewayApproval` bails at `chat_screen.dart:5574` when `_desktopGateway == null && _turnApplicationSession == null` — exactly a REST-only connection, so even a decoded frame would not raise a dialog.
- **No REST responder**: `git grep -n 'v1/runs' lib/` returns **no hits**. The app never calls `POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval`.

The server side of that channel already exists: `api_server_openai_routes.py:568` `_register_stream_approval()` registers each streaming completion as a run specifically so an approval can be resolved over REST, and the id is available to the client as `run_id` on the frame and as `id` on every chunk. `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approval` takes `{"choice": "once"|"session"|"always"|"deny"}` (plus optional `request_id`, `all`) and returns `{"object": "hermes.run.approval_response", …}` (`api_server_runs.py:1169-1215`).

## Reproduction

1. Stock Hermes Agent 0.22.2, API-server mode over Tailscale HTTPS (`:8642` → `127.0.0.1:8642`).
2. Send a prompt that makes the agent run a command requiring approval (e.g. `rm -rf` on a non-existent `/tmp` path).
3. Result: `Send failed: Gateway sent malformed SSE choices.` Server side shows the client disconnect and then `Approval wait interrupted — returning deny`; the command never runs and the turn is lost.

## Suggested fix

1. Add an `approval.request` branch in `_decodeSseFrame` beside `hermes.tool.progress`, returning an `_SseFrame` carrying the approval payload instead of treating it as a chunk.
2. Feed that into the existing `GatewayApprovalRequest.fromEventData` + `GatewayApprovalDialog`, through the same prompt queue/dedup used for clarify/sudo/secret, and relax the `:5574` bail so a REST-only connection can raise it.
3. Answer on REST with `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approval` `{"choice": …}` rather than `approval.respond`; keep the notification-approval path pointing at the same responder.
4. Independently of approvals: consider ignoring unknown *event types* rather than falling through to the chunk validator, so a future `hermes.*` event degrades to "not understood" instead of killing the send. This bug is a name collision (`choices`) plus a fail-closed decoder.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **0.22.2** (stock, `d923a5eb`), API server on `127.0.0.1:8642` behind `tailscale serve` (tailnet-only, `API_SERVER_KEY` auth).
- App **3.1.0**; the relevant decoder is identical in **v3.0.6**, so both are affected.
- Phone: Samsung Galaxy A56, Android, Tailscale direct path.

Cross-refs: #116 (server→client clarify/approval/secret on the WS transport), #225 / #226 / v3.0.6 (REST send now registered as turn activity — this is the next failure in that flow), #84 (stock-gateway transport).

title: Support a separate dashboard host (subdomain) for all dashboard features
body:
**Problem**

Many self-hosted setups put the Hermes API server and the dashboard behind a reverse proxy on separate subdomains, for example:

- API: `https://agent-api.example.com` → `:8642`
- Dashboard: `https://agent.example.com` → `:9119`

Because both run on port 443 behind the proxy, the app's per-port split (`port` and `dashboardPort`) cannot reach them. The **Desktop Gateway URL** field looks like the way to point the app at a different dashboard host, but only some features use it.

**Current behaviour (from source)**

When `desktopGatewayUrl` has a different host, `normalizedGatewayBaseUrl()` uses it, so these work:

- chat over the Desktop Gateway WebSocket (`/api/auth/ws-ticket`, `/api/ws`)
- dashboard login
- memory, remote files, chat assets, delegated task history
- archived sessions and Projects

These build their URL from `connection.host` + `dashboardPort` + `dashboardPrefix` and ignore `desktopGatewayUrl`:

- `skills_screen`
- `cron_screen`
- `settings_screen` (`/api/model/info`, `/api/model/set`)
- the session search client in `session_list_screen`
- `mobile_push_service`
- the dashboard validation in `main.dart`

With a subdomain setup, those requests go to the API host and get 404, so Skills, Cron, Settings, search and push don't work.

**Workaround**

Route the dashboard under a path prefix on the API host and set **Dashboard prefix** to `/dashboard`:

```caddy
agent-api.example.com {
    handle_path /dashboard/* {
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:9119
    }
    handle {
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8642
    }
}
```

This works, but it means changing the proxy config for every instance just to suit the app.

**Request**

Allow a separate dashboard base URL (host, port and path) and use it for all dashboard calls. Options:

1. Make every dashboard client (Skills, Cron, Settings, search, push, validation) use `normalizedGatewayBaseUrl()`, so `desktopGatewayUrl` covers them too.
2. Or add an explicit **Dashboard URL** field that overrides `host` + `dashboardPort` + `dashboardPrefix` everywhere.

Option 1 looks like the smaller change, since the resolution logic already exists.

**Environment**

- hermes-agent `v0.22.3` (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable`)
- Behind a Caddy reverse proxy and Cloudflare Tunnel, one subdomain per service

title: Chat list layout breaks at 320dp width with font scale 2.0 (title invisible, FAB overlaps search, chips clipped)
body:
Testing the app at the smallest width with the largest text size, the chat list screen falls apart in a few ways.

Setup: emulator, smallest width set to 320dp (wm size 320x640), font scale 2.0, connection label long enough to not fit on one line (~100 chars). The chat list inside that connection:

- The title in the app bar is squeezed out entirely — zero visible characters, not even an ellipsis. The 2.0-scaled notification badge ends up sitting where the title should be.
- The "New" FAB grows to almost full width and overlaps down over the search field, so the search field is only partially visible.
- The filter chips row (All / Recent / Unassigned / Archived) is clipped out of the viewport completely.
- The bottom navigation labels wrap mid-word ("Chat/s", "Cro/ns") and the second line is cut off against the gesture bar.

At font scale 2.0 with the normal viewport everything degrades fine — the title ellipsizes to "Emulator-R4-Qua…" and nothing overlaps. It's specifically the 320dp + 2.0 combination that breaks. Can't attach the screenshot from a fork account, but the frame looks roughly like this::

```
[<-] [badge(1)] [search]
+-------------------------+
| + New                   |
|     (overlaps the       |
|      search field)      |
+-------------------------+
Chats   Crons   Projects   Activity   More
Chat/   Cro/    Proj/      Acti/       Mor/
s       ns      ects       vity        e
```

For anyone with a small phone using the largest text size this screen is effectively unusable — you can't see which connection you're in and the chips are gone.

Repro:
1. Set smallest width to 320dp (or `adb shell wm size 320x640`) and font scale to 2.0
2. Rename a connection to something ~100 chars
3. Open the connection and look at the chat list

Expected: title ellipsized to at least a few characters, search field and chips visible, nav labels not clipped.

title: REST/API-server approval fails with HTTP 400: POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval omits execution_generation (canonical run authority)
body:
## Summary

On an **API-server (REST/SSE) connection**, tapping Approve on a native approval prompt fails with:

> Could not send the approval: Exception: HTTP 400

The run stays parked (fails closed), so the gated tool never runs.

## Environment

- Hermes Android **3.1.7** (build 3020, `app-arm64-v8a-release.apk`), Samsung S24 Ultra
- Hermes Agent **v0.22.5** (stable, git install) on macOS, API server bound to a Tailscale IP, port 8642, `API_SERVER_KEY` auth
- No dashboard configured on the connection, so the app takes the REST approval fallback

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a connection to the Gateway API Server only (host, port 8642, API key; no dashboard).
2. In a chat, ask Hermes for something gated by an approval rule (e.g. a `git push` that `approvals` escalates).
3. The approval prompt appears in the app. Tap **Approve once**.
4. A snackbar shows `Could not send the approval: Exception: HTTP 400`.

## Root cause

The REST fallback in `_respondToApproval` posts only `choice` and an optional `request_id`:

https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/blob/810a4f9c9795876556292fb65934422e551e4e95/lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart#L5340-L5346

```dart
final result = await _client.apiPost(
  'v1/runs/$runId/approval',
  body: {
    'choice': choice,
    ...?(requestId == null ? null : {'request_id': requestId}),
  },
);
```

When the gateway runs the **canonical session authority**, `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/approval` is routed to `respond_run`, which requires the body to contain **exactly** `request_id`, `execution_generation`, and `choice`. Anything else raises `invalid_params`, which maps to HTTP 400:

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f30105a0b4b3d0c1baa6c464189755ccdbc1ac7f/gateway/platforms/api_server_authority_runs.py#L119-L125

```python
generation = body.get('execution_generation')
prompt_id = body.get('request_id')
field = 'choice' if kind == 'approval' else 'answer'
if set(body) != {'request_id', 'execution_generation', field}:
    raise RuntimeStoreError('invalid_params')   # -> 400
if row['status'] != 'started' or type(generation) is not int or generation != row['generation']:
    raise RuntimeStoreError('stale_generation')  # -> 409
```

The Hermes API server docs describe the same contract: with the canonical owner, `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` exposes `pending_controls` with `prompt_id` and `execution_generation`, and the response must be `{"request_id": "<prompt_id>", "execution_generation": N, "choice": "once"}`. Identityless or bulk responses are not accepted.

## Suggested fix

In the REST fallback, before posting:

1. `GET v1/runs/$runId` and read `pending_controls`. Find the entry whose `prompt_id` matches `requestId` (or the single pending approval when `requestId` is null) and take its `execution_generation`. Alternatively, carry `execution_generation` from the `approval.request` SSE event if the gateway includes it there.
2. Post `{'request_id': promptId, 'execution_generation': generation, 'choice': choice}`, with no other keys.
3. Keep the current `{choice, request_id}` body only for legacy (non-canonical) gateways. These can be detected by the absence of `pending_controls` / `run_unknown_resolution` in `/v1/capabilities`.
4. Surface a 409 `stale_generation` as "this approval is no longer pending" rather than a generic error.

A clarify response over REST (`/v1/runs/{id}/clarify`) has the same `request_id` + `execution_generation` + `answer` requirement, if the app adds that path.

## Workaround

Configure the dashboard on the connection (Dashboard / Proxy Settings) so approvals go through the Desktop Gateway JSON-RPC transport instead of the REST fallback.

body:
## Summary

The per-chat **Model and thinking for this chat** sheet (opened from the model button above the composer) now has a search field. It filters the model list by model ID or provider name as you type. Clearing the search restores the full list.

Filtering never changes the selection. A selected model that the current search hides stays selected, and nothing is applied until **Apply to this chat** is tapped. When the same model ID is served by more than one provider, each provider's row remains separate.

- The sheet body moved into a small private stateful widget, `_ChatModelPickerSheet`, which owns the search controller. The previous `StatefulBuilder` closure could not hold a controller with a clean lifetime.

title: Feature request: first-class Android Auto support
body:
## Feature description

Would it be possible to make the Hermes Android app a first-class citizen on Android Auto? I use Hermes from the car a lot and would love to interact with it through the Android Auto head unit rather than only on the phone screen.

## What Android Auto support could look like

- A Hermes launcher icon in Android Auto.
- Voice-initiated conversations (tap-to-talk / reply-to-message) through the car's microphone.
- Assistant answers delivered as car-compatible messaging notifications so the car can read them aloud and offer a follow-up reply.
- Continuity: the same configured connections, settings and session state that exist in the phone app should be available during an Android Auto session.

## Motivation

I run Hermes via the Android app while driving and currently have to fall back to the phone screen for anything beyond the basics. Native Android Auto integration would make the assistant usable in a hands-free, eyes-free way, which is exactly where voice-first agents shine.

## Context

I am opening this on behalf of a user who actively uses Hermes Android Auto as part of their daily workflow and is willing to test builds or provide logs from real car head units if that helps move this forward.

## Alternatives considered

- Using the phone screen while driving (distracting and sometimes illegal).
- Relying on Google Assistant as a bridge (loses the Hermes context and configured tools).

Thank you for considering this!

title: 3.1.7/3.2.x: "Send failed: permission_denied" on chats against stock gateway v0.22.5 (browsing works; stock fallback deviates)
body:
## Summary

On a gateway running stock **Hermes Agent v0.22.5**, the v3.x app browses existing chats fine but **every send fails with `Send failed: permission_denied`**. Per the README's transport-compatibility section, the app is supposed to fall back to the stock Desktop Gateway transport against gateways that don't advertise `capabilities.turn_recovery` — the raw stock protocol works against this exact gateway, so the fallback path appears to deviate from it.

## Environment

- App: **3.1.7** (published stable at time of testing; the send path is byte-identical in 3.2.0/3.2.1 — see "Code evidence")
- Gateway: Hermes Agent **v0.22.5** (current published release; nothing newer exists to "update" to), Dashboard + Desktop Gateway on :9119 with password auth
- Transport: Tailscale, HTTP (no reverse proxy), API-server transport (:8642) also healthy and reachable
- Phone: Pixel 10 Pro, over tailnet

## Symptom

- Chat list + opening existing chats (read): ✅ works
- Sending in any existing chat: ❌ `Send failed: permission_denied`
- Not chat-specific — fails across several chats.

## Gateway-side protocol evidence

I ran the app's wire flow manually (login → `/api/auth/ws-ticket` → `GET /api/ws?ticket=` → JSON-RPC) against this gateway. Results:

1. **`gateway.ready` advertises no recovery capabilities** — payload keys are exactly `[change_events, heartbeat, replay_epoch, skin]`. So (per docs) the app should use the stock transport.
2. `session.open` → `-32601 unknown method: session.open — the client and the Hermes backend are out of sync; run hermes update and restart both`. (v0.22.5 *is* the latest release; `session.open` appears only in unreleased backends, so that hint is a dead end.)
3. `prompt.submit` with recovery-v2 params (`version: 2`, `client_turn_id`) → `4000 invalid params … version: Extra inputs are not permitted`.
4. **The stock contract works end-to-end over the same path**: `session.create {source: "desktop"}` → ok; `prompt.submit {session_id, text}` → `{"status": "streaming"}`. For an existing chat: `session.resume {session_id}` → fresh runtime binding + history, then `prompt.submit {session_id: <binding>, text}` → `{"status": "streaming"}` (turn executed).
5. `prompt.submit` directly against an *unresumed* stored session id → `4001 session not found` (runtime sessions unload after ~2 min idle via scale-to-zero). Note `session.resume` returns a **different id** than the stored one.

The `permission_denied` string matches none of the raw responses above, which suggests the app's stock fallback is sending something else (or using the stored id where the resumed runtime binding is expected, or attempting a recovery method and surfacing a mapped error).

## Code evidence (why 3.2.x is expected to reproduce)

`git diff v3.1.7..main(3.2.1)` touches none of the send path:

- `lib/core/models/gateway_turn_contract.dart` — unchanged
- `lib/core/services/gateway_turn_coordinator.dart` — unchanged
- `lib/core/services/ws_client.dart` — unchanged
- `lib/core/services/desktop_gateway_client.dart` — 9 lines (URL-building cleanup, profile scoping, read-only analytics/portal methods)

## Expected behavior

Against a gateway whose `gateway.ready` carries no `turn_recovery` capability, sends should behave exactly as 2.1.32: `session.resume` (existing) / `session.create` (new), then legacy `prompt.submit` with the **returned runtime binding id**.

## Questions

1. Is the v3.x stock fallback intended to cover v0.22.5, or is there a minimum gateway build for 3.x?
2. Is there a per-connection knob to force the legacy transport (2.1.32-style)?
3. If useful, I can capture the exact frames the 3.1.7 client sends (recording proxy / logcat) to pin down the offending request — the gateway-side responses above are fully reproducible.

## Not yet tested

- Sending a brand-new chat from the phone app (raw-protocol create+submit works, so suspected to work).
- Whether `turn.reconcile`-adjacent reconnect paths fire before the visible failure.

title: test(chat): pin API versus Dashboard principal routing (#253)
body:
## Summary

Related to #253; **does not close it or claim a production fix**.

The reporter's new capture identifies API-versus-Dashboard principal routing, not a broken low-level stock WS contract. However current main `b7cd9e2` (and the v3.1.7 tag) already attaches the normal Dashboard session when both username/password are supplied, irrespective of API key. Real application-path tests pass without changing production code. Changing the gate to merely detect a password would not establish Dashboard password authentication: the HTTP client requires username too.

- Add ten `ChatScreen` widget tests using actual loopback HTTP/SSE and password-login/ticket/WebSocket transports, without injected submit/resume/history callbacks.
- Cover API-only versus dual credentials without explicit Desktop URL or proxy mode, on default and named profiles.
- Pin stored-ID resume/runtime-ID submit, selected profile, cookie auth, no principal-switch fallback or replacement chat on refusals, and no prompt resend after uncertain socket delivery.
- Record source/history and remaining reproduction boundary in `docs/reviews/issue253-principal-routing.md`. Thanks to @hnnacgov for the capture and fork fix direction. No matching contributor PR exists; no contributor commit was rewritten or copied.

## Validation

- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos`: no issues.
- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed test/chat_principal_routing_test.dart`: unchanged.
- `flutter test --no-pub --reporter expanded`: **5,189 passed**, including ten new routing cases.
- Mutation test: synthetically prioritizing a configured API key over the Dashboard attach guard makes both dual-credential cases fail on an unexpected Bearer completion POST. Restoring the original guard restores passing full-suite behavior. This is **not** an old-behavior failure: unchanged main already passes.

## Remaining blocker / limits

title: Proposal: show upcoming scheduled jobs alongside run history
body:
# Proposal: show upcoming scheduled jobs alongside run history

Suggested destination: a feature issue in rusty4444/hermes-android; coordinate a server API change with NousResearch/hermes-agent only if the existing public Dashboard/native interfaces cannot provide the required data.

Users expect a tab named Crons or Schedules to show jobs that will run in the future. A history-only view can appear empty or contain only past jobs even though an agent has successfully scheduled a reminder.

The current public app already has a CronScreen reachable through Dashboard/settings. Prefer exposing that existing manager in the main navigation, with clearly separated Upcoming and History views, before adding another cron implementation.

Upcoming should show enabled/disabled definitions, next run, timezone and target conversation where supported. History should show completed/failed runs and their result. Refresh while visible and on app resume; distinguish an unsupported connection from an empty schedule list.

Acceptance checks: a future weekly job appears before its first run, next-run time uses an explicit timezone, finished one-off runs do not hide future jobs, switching connections cannot reuse stale rows, and an API-only connection gets an accurate capability message.

Our deployment-specific API bridge is not a portable public patch. Agree the public connection capability and authorization contract first; do not add fixed profile names or silently expose new server routes.

title: Proposal: optional encrypted message previews and API-only push compatibility
body:
# Proposal: optional encrypted message previews and API-only push compatibility

Suggested destination: a feature issue in rusty4444/hermes-android, with the server-side companion/interface owner included before implementation.

The public Android app already supports an optional mobile-push companion. Extend that contract rather than adding a second independent push system.

An activity-only notification is private but cannot tell a user what a reminder says, particularly on a watch. Offer an explicit preview setting and, when enabled, deliver an encrypted bounded preview with a stable message identifier and conversation target. Android can then show useful text and open the correct saved chat. The UI must accurately explain whether chat content is included; an activity-only privacy statement must not remain after enabling previews.

For API-only connections, first agree how the companion authenticates registration, resolves the authorized profile/chat scope, rotates keys and revokes installations. Our local API-only adapter is custom integration code, not an existing public Core interface. It should not be copied as though it were a stock-server fix.

Keep ordinary reply completion and scheduled/background messages on one deduplicated notification policy. Fetch/reconcile canonical state on open; notifications do not become an alternative chat database. Avoid provider SDK or transport changes unless required by the agreed contract.

Acceptance checks: previews off/on, lock-screen policy, ordinary and scheduled messages, logout/revocation, key rotation, duplicate events, disconnected device, cold/warm tap routing and denied notification permission. Maintainers should decide the privacy default before a code PR.

title: Resume, preview and send voice drafts as one message
body:
Replacement for closed #164: after updating its source branch, GitHub rejected reopening through both GraphQL and REST (HTTP422). The original remains closed; this PR carries its preserved history and the current-main adaptation. This branch merges current main while preserving the original contribution commits, and adapts voice drafts to the current prompt transports, lifecycle fencing and hands-free behavior.

Use case: while reading a long reply, record one short comment, pause to read the next section, then continue recording another comment. Preview the combined draft and send it as one message rather than several fragmented prompts. Pausing and returning to the chat preserve the draft. Active recording keeps the screen awake; stopping, leaving or backgrounding releases that flag.

Send uses the configured Hermes Dashboard transcription endpoint, with existing authentication and profile selection, then submits the recognized text through the existing chat transport. It does not contact a Whisper endpoint directly or add another recognition service. Unrelated typed text and selected attachments remain intact. A correlated admission acknowledgement, response activity on the active request, or authoritative receipt is required before discarding audio; a socket write alone is insufficient. Ambiguous delivery retains the draft for manual review, with no automatic prompt resubmission.

Validation at the recorded base: flutter analyze --no-pub passes; 75 focused tests pass, including recovery, lifecycle, hands-free interoperation and real loopback WebSocket admission acknowledgements. The full Flutter suite passes 5222 tests. Android compileDebugKotlin passes. The exact tested source tree is recorded in verification.json.

Limits: recordings are capped at ten minutes and 6 MiB. The server must expose the existing authenticated Dashboard transcription route and have STT configured; API-only connections without that route retain the recording on failure. The recorded audio itself is not archived as a playable attachment in chat history. Real microphone permission, codec joining, preview playback and screen-timeout behavior still require device QA on this public build. Dependencies record 7.1.1 and audioplayers 6.8.1 are pinned; Android joining uses native media APIs.

The existing PR is closed; no reopening, CI success or maintainer acceptance is claimed by this local refresh. Please re-evaluate the current head, not the closed PR's frozen head.
