title: fix: explain API-only permission_denied without changing send routing (#253)
body:
Closes the remaining UX scope of #253.

## What this does

An API-key-only connection (API-server bearer key, no Dashboard username/password, no Desktop Gateway URL) can browse a Dashboard-owned chat but every send is refused by the gateway's canonical session authority with an in-band HTTP-200 SSE error `permission_denied`. The refusal was shown as a bare `Send failed: permission_denied`, which gives the user nothing to act on.

This adds **one extra localised string** that keeps the server's refusal verbatim and appends conditional guidance, selected by a small pure predicate.

English copy:

> Send failed: {error}. The server refused this write for the API key principal. If this chat is owned by the Dashboard, adding the Dashboard username and password for this connection may let it send; the server may also be refusing deliberately.

## Explicit non-changes

- **No routing or principal change.** `hasDashboardAuth`, the `_attachNormalSession()` gate and every transport decision are untouched. The failing send still goes out as the API-server key principal over `POST /v1/chat/completions`, exactly as before.
- **No resend, retry, principal switch, session-id change or thread fork.** The only edit inside `_handleSendError` is which of two strings is assigned to the existing `_terminalTurnNotice`; no request is issued from that path. The widget test asserts the fixture sees exactly one completion POST before and after further settling.
- **Original refusal preserved.** The richer string is strictly additive: `send_failed(error)` is a verbatim prefix of `send_failed_api_only_permission_denied(error)`, and this prefix invariant is asserted for all 12 shipped locales.
- **Guidance is conditional, not a diagnosis.** The copy says adding Dashboard credentials *may* let it send and explicitly states the server *may also be refusing deliberately*. It never claims that an ACL denial implies missing credentials — an intentional server policy refusal reads correctly under this wording.
- **No new error-presentation architecture.** It reuses the existing persistent terminal-notice channel (`ChatActivityBar(isTerminalNotice: true)`) that already owned terminal send failures.

## When the guidance appears

`shouldExplainApiOnlyPermissionDenial(connection, error)` (a `@visibleForTesting` top-level pure function, matching the existing `shouldUseRecoveryV2ForSession` convention in the same file) returns true only when **all** hold:

1. no `dashboardProxied`, and not both a non-blank `dashboardUsername` and `dashboardPassword`;
2. no non-blank `desktopGatewayUrl`;
3. the error string contains `permission_denied`.

Any other case renders the pre-existing plain `send_failed` unchanged. The predicate mirrors the attach gate's own condition rather than redefining it.

## Localisation

The key was inserted into all 12 shipped ARB catalogues with a real translation each (de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, pt_BR, ru, uk, zh, zh_Hans) using exact-line minimal insertion, so each ARB diff is a single added line. `lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart` is regenerated build output from `flutter gen-l10n`, not hand-edited. A test asserts every locale's generated getter is non-empty, contains the reported error, keeps the plain message as a prefix, and differs from English.

## Tests

New `test/api_only_permission_guidance_test.dart` — 23 tests:

- predicate: API-only + `permission_denied` → true; non-ACL failures (HTTP 500, timeout, socket, 429) → false; Dashboard username+password → false; `dashboardProxied` → false; explicit Desktop Gateway URL → false; blank/half credentials treated as absent; repeated calls are effect-free.
- copy: guidance keeps the refusal as a prefix, is longer, and uses conditional phrasing.
- l10n coverage: all 12 ARBs define a non-empty value containing the placeholder; all 12 generated locales stay additive and are not English fallbacks.
- widget end-to-end against a loopback fixture replaying stock gateway v0.22.5 API-only behaviour: reads succeed, the write returns the in-band SSE `permission_denied`, the rendered terminal notice carries both the verbatim refusal and the guidance, no password-login or ws-ticket is attempted, and exactly one completion POST is issued with no replay.

## Verification limitation

No live gateway ACL reproduction is claimed. The widget test replays the reporter's observed wire contract (HTTP-200 SSE error frame from `POST /v1/chat/completions`) against a local fixture server; it does not exercise a real Hermes gateway's authorisation engine, and this change asserts nothing about why the server refuses. The server-side policy refusal remains intentional and unmodified.

title: perf: stop the periodic pane refresh from re-paging archives (#149)
body:
Closes the remaining measured defect in #149: the ordinary launcher's 10-second visible-pane refresh re-paged the **archived** session list on every tick even while the user was on a non-archived filter.

## The traced call chain (before this PR)

1. `lib/main.dart` (`_navigateToWorkspace`) passes `sessionsRefreshInterval: const Duration(seconds: 10)` into `WorkspaceScreen`.
2. `WorkspaceSessionsScreenState._syncRefreshTimer()` starts `Timer.periodic(interval, ...)`, whose callback called `_load()`.
3. `_load()` routed to `_loadOnce()`, which called `widget.loadProgressively`.
4. In `workspace_screen.dart`, `loadProgressively` was wired for the embedded **Chats** pane, the embedded **Crons** pane and the **classic standalone** views as `_loadWorkspaceSessionsData(onProgress: onProgress)` — i.e. with `includeArchives` left at its default of `true` (`var archiveLoading = includeArchives && _dashboardReachable;`).
5. Only `reloadActive` ever passed `includeArchives: false`.

Result: every tick on a visible Chats or Crons pane performed the full archived-session paging against the dashboard router (`GET /api/sessions?archived=only&order=recent…`, `limit=5&offset=0` → `limit=100&offset=5` → `limit=100&offset=105` …), even though `WorkspaceChatsFilter.all`, `.recent` and `.unassigned` all match on `!session.archived` and can never render one of those rows.

## What changed

`WorkspaceSessionsScreen` gains an optional `loadWithoutArchives` loader: `loadProgressively` minus the archive authority.

* **Passive tick only.** `Timer.periodic` now calls `_tick()` → `_load(includeArchives: _isArchivedSurface, passive: true)`. A non-archived filter reads without archives; the Archived surfaces keep the full-scope tick they have today.
* **No forced fresh I/O.** `loadWithoutArchives` is wired *without* `freshActive`, so a tick still coalesces with an in-flight scan. Using `reloadActive` here would have called `SharedSessionScan.invalidate()` and *added* active scans — the opposite of the goal, and a regression of PR #156.
* **Archive authority is carried, not overwritten.** `_loadWorkspaceSessionsData(includeArchives: false)` returns an empty `archivedSessions` which the `WorkspaceSessionsData` constructor would default to `archivesKnown: true`. A scoped read therefore publishes `current.withActive(data)` — the same carry an explicit active-only refresh already uses — preserving `archivedSessions`, `archivedIsPartial`, `archiveError`, `archivesKnown` **and** the carried collection's own mutation/title epoch (`_archivedArchiveRevision` / `_archiveTitleRevision`).
* **A scoped read never satisfies a wider demand.** `_loadInFlightIncludesArchives` tracks the in-flight aggregate read's scope; an explicit full demand waiting behind a scoped tick queues its own read (`_queuedFullLoad`) instead of inheriting one that will never page archives. A `passive` tick still shares whatever is in flight.
* **Selecting Archived catches up.** Because no tick will ask for archives while another chip is selected, `_selectFilter` fires `_ensureArchives()` when switching into Archived *and only after a tick actually skipped them* (`_archivesSkippedByTick`). A pane whose archives were never skipped issues no extra request, so existing chip-tap request counts are unchanged.
* **Scope applied to all three paths**: embedded Chats, embedded Crons, and the classic standalone views (`_openWorkspaceSessionView`). Nothing excluded.

No behaviour change to the first load, pull-to-refresh, `refresh()`, becoming visible, chat-route return, the refresh interval value, any server/API contract, any endpoint, or the transcript fetch path. No new user-visible strings, so no ARB changes.

## Red-on-base evidence

`test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart` compiles against the unmodified base. Observed red at `b31f56376e5d408de55c80919001be239a534a8d` with the implementation stashed:

```
$ git stash push lib/core/screens/workspace_sessions_screen.dart lib/core/screens/workspace_screen.dart
$ git rev-parse --short HEAD        # b31f5637
$ flutter test --no-pub test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart
```

```
The following TestFailure was thrown running a test:
Expected: <2>
  Actual: <8>
a visible non-archived pane must not re-page archived=only on every tick (#149)
  …test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart line 146
The test description was:
  Chats periodic ticks stop re-paging archives on a non-archived filter
```

7 of the 10 tests in that file failed on base; 10/10 pass on this branch.

**Archive-router requests observed over 3 ticks with a non-archived filter selected** (one archived row in the fixture, so 2 pages per archive scan):

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Chats, All chip, initial load + 3 ticks | 8 (2 initial + 2 per tick) | 2 (initial only) |
| Crons pane, initial loads + 3 ticks | 10 | 4 |
| Archived chip, initial + 2 ticks | 6 | 6 (unchanged by design) |

## Preserved invariants and the test that pins each

| Invariant | Test |
|---|---|
| Archived rows survive active-only ticks; `archivesKnown` / partial / error state is not reset | `periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart` → *active-only ticks preserve archived rows, pins and Quick Chat expiry* (asserts the retained row while the catch-up archive read is **held**, and again after it fails 503 with Retry shown); `workspace_sessions_progressive_test.dart` → *a scoped tick carries the archive authority forward* |
| Absence is never deletion: device-local Quick Chat expiry and local pins are not pruned | same test — `pins.load()` still `['human']`, `quick.load().archivedAt(now)` still `{'quick'}`, "Pinned on this device" still rendered after 3 scoped ticks |
| No empty-state verdict for a partial list | same test — `expect(find.byType(EmptyState), findsNothing)` while the archive catch-up is held |
| In-flight coalescing (PR #156) is intact | `workspace_sessions_progressive_test.dart` → *overlapping scoped ticks share one scan and a newer page wins* — 3 ticks during one held scoped scan invoke the loader exactly once |
| A newer first page survives an older shared scan | same test — the refreshed read's `newer` page survives late progress from the old scoped flight |
| An explicit refresh is not discarded or downgraded by a tick | *an explicit refresh is never satisfied by a scoped tick* (the refresh future stays pending when the scoped tick completes, and the full loader runs) and *a scoped tick reads without archives while refresh keeps the full read* |
| Archived filter still refreshes archives on every tick | *Archived chip ticks keep refreshing the archive authority* — request count grows per tick **and** a title changed server-side appears after a tick |
| Explicit gestures keep their current scope | *pull-to-refresh after scoped ticks keeps its own scope* — one fresh active scan, zero extra archive pages (Chats pull-to-refresh was already archive-free through `reloadActive`) |
| Hidden pane issues nothing | *a hidden pane issues no requests at all* |
| Switching into Archived loads promptly | *switching to Archived loads archives without waiting a tick*, plus the inverse: All → Archived with nothing skipped issues no extra request |
| Chats, Crons and the classic path are all scoped | *Chats/Crons periodic ticks stop re-paging archives on a non-archived filter* (parameterised over both panes); the classic standalone views share the same `_load()`/`_tick()` code path and the same wiring |

## Validation

Run in order, all green:

```
flutter pub get
dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed <each changed .dart file>
git diff --check
flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos     # No issues found!
flutter test --no-pub                      # All tests passed! (5392 tests)
```

The same full suite on clean base `b31f5637` reports **5378 passed**, so the delta is exactly the 14 tests added here and no pre-existing failure is involved. (The `~5,189` figure quoted in the issue thread is stale against this base.)

## Explicit limitation

**No device or server transfer measurement is claimed.** Every number in this PR is a count of HTTP requests observed through `MockClient` in widget tests. Nothing here measures bytes on the wire, battery, latency or real-device behaviour.

Other limitations, stated plainly:

* The tick still reads `projects.tree` and the device Quick Chat store on every cadence. That is out of scope for this change and unchanged.
* While a non-archived filter is selected, the `ChatAttentionSection` sees the union of active and (now staler) archived rows. Archived rows are not running turns, so no attention/running signal is expected to depend on them, but their metadata can lag by more than one tick until the user selects Archived or refreshes.
* The Archived catch-up on chip selection uses `reloadArchives` (`fresh: true`), which the embedded panes wire. The classic standalone views do not wire `reloadArchives`; their only archived surface is `WorkspaceSessionView.archivedQuick`, which is permanently an archived surface and therefore keeps the full-scope tick, so it never needs the catch-up.

title: feat: split Crons into Upcoming schedules and run History (#259)
body:
Closes #259.

## Summary

Crons now opens on **Upcoming** scheduled job definitions, with a **History** chip for the existing cron run conversations. The chips follow the Chats browser's existing `ChoiceChip` pattern.

- Upcoming reuses `DashboardClient.getCronJobs()` and the existing manager's field parsing, extracted into `cron_schedule.dart`. It shows scheduled/paused/completed state, schedule, next run with an explicit zone, prompt preview, and the delivery target when supplied.
- Definitions with a next run are shown earliest-first. Paused jobs and finished one-offs remain visible under **No next run scheduled**, after future jobs.
- History retains its search, All / Recent / Archived filters, navigation and reconciliation.
- `CronScreen` remains the sole CRUD manager, reachable from More, the Crons app-bar action, and Upcoming rows/empty state. Its Last/Next labels use the shared timezone formatting too.
- Upcoming refreshes while visible and on resume/return. Held pre-resume reads receive a trailing fresh read; hidden connection replacements cannot start requests under the old visibility state. Generation fencing clears old rows immediately and rejects late old responses.
- Missing cron capability, missing Dashboard authentication, unreachable Dashboard, empty schedules and retryable server faults have distinct states. Later failures retain the previous snapshot behind an explicit stale-data notice.
- All new copy is translated in all 12 shipped ARBs using minimal line insertions; localization Dart files were generated, not hand-edited.

## Existing endpoints only

Upcoming's sole resource read is **`GET /api/cron/jobs`**, through `DashboardClient.fromConnection(...).getCronJobs()`, preserving the existing origin/prefix/authentication/TLS/selected-profile path. Existing Dashboard authentication may first read the SPA homepage or perform password login.

`CronScreen` continues to own the already-existing `GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}`, `GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}/runs`, and create/update/pause/resume/trigger/delete operations. History uses the unchanged session-list/archive routes. No new server endpoint, fixed profile name, or server-side change was added.

## Timezone evidence and labels

Inspected host source: `cron/jobs.py` and `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py` at local host-source revision `08903d4a`. Its job record has **no dedicated IANA timezone field**; next/last-run ISO timestamps carry numeric UTC offsets.

- `2026-11-09T09:00:00+11:00` → **Next: 2026-11-09 09:00 (UTC+11:00)**.
- `Z` / `+00:00` → **(UTC)**.
- A timestamp with no offset and no named zone → **(timezone unknown)**.
- Optional `timezone` / `tz` fields, top-level or in `schedule`, are retained defensively. With an offset-bearing timestamp, the named schedule zone is separate metadata, e.g. **Next: 2026-11-09 09:00 (UTC) · Schedule timezone: Australia/Sydney**. A UTC clock is never merely relabelled as Sydney time. For a zone-less timestamp with a supplied schedule zone, that zone is shown beside the server's wall clock.

There is no device-local conversion or IANA timezone conversion. The displayed instant/offset is the value returned by the server, not a prediction made by the client.

## Five acceptance checks

All widget cases below are in `test/crons_upcoming_history_test.dart`.

| Check | Tests and evidence |
|---|---|
| **a. Weekly job visible before its first run** | `a future weekly job appears in Upcoming before it has ever run`: a weekly definition with null last run and empty history appears in Upcoming, not History. |
| **b. Explicit timezone** | `the next-run time always states which timezone it is in`: offset and unknown-zone labels; rejects bare Next labels. `UTC timestamps are not relabelled as the named schedule zone`: UTC clock and named schedule zone stay distinct. `cron_schedule_test.dart` also covers Z, negative half-hour offset, nested named zone, missing/legacy values and ordering. |
| **c. Finished one-offs do not hide future jobs** | `finished one-off runs do not hide future jobs`: completed definition and finished history row coexist with a future weekly definition. Partition/sorting unit coverage verifies future definitions come first. |
| **d. No stale cross-connection jobs** | `switching the saved connection never reuses its rows`: held old-server response lands after the new server and is ignored. `loaded rows clear before a replacement connection answers`: old rows disappear immediately and stay absent if the replacement fails. |
| **e. Honest API-only capability message** | `an API-only connection is told it needs a Dashboard` (SPA homepage 404), `a dashboard without the cron route is a capability gap` (cron route 404), and `an empty schedule reads as empty, not as unsupported` prove capability and empty states cannot be confused. Typed classifier tests cover auth, transport and other failures separately. |

Additional tests cover visible/hidden polling, hidden connection replacement, app resume with a held read, stale-data feedback, working Retry, delivery targets, navigation and localization catalogs/accessors.

## Preserving #265 / #149's periodic-refresh contract

Rebased onto `eba4ee1b`, including #263, #264 and #265. The conflict was resolved by retaining `loadWithoutArchives` on the existing history browser, with **no `freshActive`** on passive ticks.

**`test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart` is byte-unchanged from main.**

`git diff origin/main -- test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart` produces no output.

- The retained history browser keeps the destination-level active cadence even while Upcoming is selected, as #265 requires.
- `WorkspaceSessionsScreen` retains #265's `withActive` archive carry-forward, in-flight scope/coalescing and `_archivesSkippedByTick` / `_ensureArchives()` catch-up.
- The only extension is an `archiveSurfaceVisible` flag (default true). A hidden retained Archived filter cannot re-enable archive paging behind Upcoming; returning to that filter invokes the existing `_ensureArchives()`. Ordinary All/Recent History ticks remain archive-free.
- Upcoming uses its own visibility-gated cron loader, never the archive router. It stops cron polling when History, another destination, another route, or the background is selected.

Request-level probe using the frozen test's fixtures, 10-second cadence, three ticks:

| Selected view | Active preview scans | Archive-router pages | Cron-list reads |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Immediately after opening Crons | 2 | **4** | 1 |
| Upcoming after 3 ticks | 5 | **4** | 4 |
| History after 3 ticks | 5 | **4** | 1 |

Thus **4 archive pages total (initial scan only), not 10**, and zero added archive requests over three ticks. The additional `a retained Archived filter does not poll behind Upcoming` regression proves the hidden-Archived case and catch-up on return.

Both `test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart` and `test/active_scope_refresh_test.dart` pass, including all held physical refresh, active Retry and overlapping scoped-refresh cases. Older navigation tests now explicitly select History; relevant mocks distinguish cron requests from archive requests without weakening their assertions.

## Validation

On head **`f48319a6fd31e9d3a11853de993ca185742c39bc`**, in this order:

1. `flutter pub get` — exit 0.
2. `flutter gen-l10n` — exit 0.
3. `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed <29 changed Dart files>` — 0 changed.
4. `git diff --check` — clean.
5. `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos` — **No issues found**.
6. `flutter test --no-pub` — **5467 passed, 0 failed**.

The earlier clean `b31f5637` baseline returned 5378 passing tests; the final branch also includes tests added by intervening main merges. No workflow files were changed.

## Limitations

- **No live multi-timezone server acceptance is claimed.** Fixtures were constructed from the inspected source contract, not recorded from a live production response. No user's real scheduled jobs were mutated.
- A missing route does not prove the connection is API-only: an older host or incorrect Dashboard prefix can answer similarly. The message therefore says the address does not expose the cron schedule and asks users to check the Dashboard address/support, rather than asserting an unproven service identity.
- Named timezone fields are defensive compatibility inputs; the inspected producer supplies numeric offsets, not IANA names. No timezone-database conversion is claimed.
- Both views stay mounted. The existing initial history/archive load and destination-level active refresh remain; only archive paging is suppressed for non-visible archived content. Upcoming polling is separately view-gated.
- The existing short Crons destination label and unrelated translation gaps remain unchanged. New Upcoming/History strings have translations in every shipped ARB.

title: feat: configurable server-side Projects root and existing-folder adoption (#232)
body:
Closes #232.

The reporter runs Hermes with every TUI/other-channel Project under
`/root/.hermes/projects`, but Projects the Android app created landed in
`/root/Projects`. Two separate problems, both fixed here:

1. **The app chose the root itself.** `DashboardFolderProvisioner` used the
   dashboard's `locked_root` when the server supplied one, else
   `<server home>/Projects`, with no way to say otherwise.
2. **Folders created outside the app can never appear.** The Projects list
   comes from the gateway's `projects.list` RPC, not a filesystem scan, so an
   unregistered directory is invisible no matter how many times you refresh.
   That is why Hermes "saw" the app's folders but wrote its documents into a
   duplicate folder of the same name under `.hermes/projects`.

## What this adds

### Configurable server-side Projects root

A per-saved-connection, persisted absolute path used when the app creates a new
Project. Reached from the **More pane → "Projects folder on the server"**
(`ProjectsRootScreen`). The preference is keyed by **saved-connection ID**, so
connections sharing an endpoint remain independent. Provisioning and discovery
read the current preference per operation: Save and Reset take effect on the
next create/scan without reconnecting.

Precedence is fixed in `ProjectsRootResolver` and never negotiable:

1. the dashboard's `locked_root` — **a server lock always wins**; the path is
   shown read-only with an explanation and no editor is rendered, so the UI
   cannot imply an override that would be ignored;
2. the per-connection root the user configured;
3. `<server home>/Projects` — the previous behaviour, so **nothing changes
   until the user opts in**.

If the dashboard cannot be read, no root is produced at all. The local
preference is deliberately *not* used as a fallback there: without the
dashboard answer the app cannot know whether the server is locked, and a local
preference must never outrank a lock it failed to read.

Validation is syntactic and conservative, because this app has no server
interface that proves a directory exists without writing to it: absolute POSIX
paths only; empty, whitespace-only, relative, `.`/`..`-bearing, control-char
and bare-`/` inputs are refused with a reason. Duplicate and trailing slashes
are normalised. A stored value that no longer validates (hand-edited prefs, an
old backup) is ignored on read rather than repaired.

### Adoption of existing server folders

The **Projects** tab now has an "Add an existing folder" action that lists the
directories under the effective root, marks the ones a Project already claims,
and registers the chosen one. Also reachable from the empty Projects state —
which is exactly where the reporter was stuck.

Registration uses only the existing creation contract: `projects.create` with
`primary_path`/`folders`, falling back to `projects.add_folder` when a gateway
accepts `primary_path` without echoing a folder row back. Nothing provisions a
directory on this path.

## Server interfaces used — all pre-existing in this repo

| Purpose | Call | Existing call site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read `locked_root` + browse home | `GET /api/files` | `lib/core/services/project_folder_provisioner.dart:220` (pre-change), now `lib/core/services/projects_root_resolver.dart:81` |
| **Enumerate** directories under the root | `GET /api/fs/list` | `lib/core/services/remote_files_client.dart:152-156` (`RemoteFilesClient.listDirectory`, route string at line 154), reused as-is |
| Register an existing folder | `projects.create` (`primary_path`, `folders`) | `lib/core/services/projects_gateway_client.dart:126-151` |
| Bind the folder when create does not echo it | `projects.add_folder` | `lib/core/services/projects_gateway_client.dart:185-203` |
| Existing registrations to diff against | `projects.list` | `lib/core/services/projects_gateway_client.dart:79-82` |

No RPC or REST route was invented.

**Server-folder enumeration was possible.** `GET /api/fs/list` already existed
for the remote-files browser, so this ships the real picker rather than the
manual-only fallback. The typed-path field remains as the documented fallback
for connections whose dashboard refuses to list.

## Honest capability messaging

* No dashboard route on the connection → the More entry is disabled with the
  standard "needs a reachable Hermes Dashboard" reason, and the screen shows
  "Not supported on this connection". Never a silent empty list.
* `fs/list` answering 401/403/404/405/501 → "This connection cannot list
  server folders", with the typed-path fallback still usable. An HTTP 404 here
  means the route is absent, because the stock route answers `200` with an
  `error` field for a path it cannot read; that `200`-with-`error` case is
  reported separately as a failure with the server's own message.
* A Project that gets registered but ends up with no folder raises
  `ProjectFolderAdoptionException` instead of reporting success — stock Project
  membership follows the working folder, so a folderless destination would not
  hold the chats the user expected. The created record is still shown, because
  it really exists.

## Placement: Settings stays clean

The control is a **More destination**, not a Settings card.
`test/model_management_screen_test.dart` pins a deliberate invariant — the
Settings screen must build no dashboard-backed editors and perform no server
discovery (model management moved to More in #238/#250/#262). An earlier draft
of this branch put the card in Settings and broke that test; the control was
moved to its own More destination, which is where Model, Skills and Memory
already live. `lib/core/screens/settings_screen.dart` is unchanged on this
branch, and `test/model_management_screen_test.dart` passes with its
assertions byte-identical to `main`. `test/projects_root_screen_test.dart`
re-asserts the invariant from the Projects-root side, so a future move back
into Settings fails loudly.

## One existing test touched (navigation hardening, no assertion changed)

Adding a row to the More menu shifts its scroll geometry, which made two
`test/workspace_screen_test.dart` cases tap a clipped row:
`scrollUntilVisible` stops as soon as a row is *mounted*, which can still leave
it partially off-screen. Both now call `tester.ensureVisible(...)` before the
tap. Every assertion in those tests is unchanged — only the navigation step is
made independent of how many rows sit above the target.

`test/more_pane_test.dart`'s destination inventory gained `'projects-root'`,
which is that test's purpose: a new More destination must be declared there.

## Concurrency

The root editor fences connection replacement and disposal with a generation
counter. The adoption sheet fences disposal; discovery objects belong to their
connection. Tests hold old reads across these boundaries.

## Tests

Coverage across eight new test files:

* `test/projects_root_preference_test.dart` — default equals current
  behaviour, persistence round-trip, per-connection isolation, validation
  table, corrupt/wrong-typed storage keeps the default and never throws.
* `test/projects_root_resolver_test.dart` — precedence including
  `locked_root` beating a configured root, unreadable dashboard, and
  provisioner integration proving a new folder is really created under the
  configured root (and under the lock when locked).
* `test/project_folder_discovery_test.dart` — registered vs unregistered
  diffing over real `fs/list` responses, unsupported vs failed, trailing-slash
  matching, held-read isolation.
* `test/project_folder_adoption_test.dart` — registration through
  `projects.create`, the `add_folder` fallback, folderless destination
  reported, failure keeps prior state and surfaces the server error, path
  rejection before any gateway call, and that an ordinary name-only create is
  unchanged.
* `test/projects_root_settings_card_test.dart` — editable/locked/unsupported/
  unavailable states, validation messages, and the connection-replacement
  fence.
* `test/adopt_project_folder_sheet_test.dart` — listing, adoption, disabled
  registered rows, error and folderless paths, typed-path fallback, and the
  end-to-end pane flow.
* `test/projects_root_screen_test.dart` — explicit More navigation, dashboard
  capability messaging and unchanged Settings traffic invariants.
* `test/projects_root_l10n_test.dart` — every new key exists in all 12 shipped
  ARBs, renders with placeholders substituted, and differs from English in
  every non-English catalogue.

26 new strings translated in all 12 shipped locales (en, de, es, fr, ja, ko,
pt, pt_BR, ru, uk, zh, zh_Hans).

## Integrated validation

Merged current `origin/main` (`eba4ee1b05441173531b560d85815626542945d6`)
with an ordinary merge commit, `f7b8fa5dd08108cd47fc9d09ad4d01a8926094f0`.
Final follow-up `4afea58526632438d8f7ef633f1eec97b9a337b1` closes the saved-ID
isolation and retained-workspace preference-read gaps, with new regressions.

On that exact final head, the ordered gate passed:

1. `flutter pub get`
2. `flutter gen-l10n`
3. `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` — 32 changed Dart files,
   zero formatting changes
4. `git diff --check`
5. `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos` — no issues
6. `flutter test --no-pub` — **5,496 tests passed**, no failures

The three `WorkspaceSessionsScreen` sites retain `loadWithoutArchives`.
All three CI checks passed on `4afea58526632438d8f7ef633f1eec97b9a337b1`:

- **Analyze & Test** — SUCCESS, 13m30s
  ([run 41837568398](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/actions/runs/41837568398))
- **Android native regressions** — SUCCESS, 3m30s
  ([run 41837568367](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android/actions/runs/41837568367))
- **Push companion and Dart TCP contract** — SUCCESS, 1m35s
  (same native/push run)

The four protected test files were also rerun together: **91 tests passed**.
All 11 generated localisation Dart files contain both the Projects keys and
`send_failed_api_only_permission_denied`. The following diffs against
`origin/main` are empty:

- `test/periodic_refresh_scope_test.dart`
- `test/workspace_sessions_progressive_test.dart`
- `test/api_only_permission_guidance_test.dart`
- `test/model_management_screen_test.dart`
- `README.md`

## Not claimed

* **No live multi-root server acceptance.** Everything here is verified against
  MockClient-backed fakes of the real routes and the unit/widget suite. No run
  against a live Hermes host with a non-default Projects root was performed.
* Path validation is syntactic, not proof of server-side existence or
  writability. Manual entries are sent to the existing gateway registration
  contract; the app does not independently verify that directory.
* Path comparison for "already a Project" is textual after trailing-slash
  normalisation. Server-side symlinks are not resolved, so two paths naming the
  same directory by different routes are treated as different; worst case the
  picker offers a folder that is already a Project under another path.
* Enumeration covers direct, non-hidden child directories, not a recursive
  search. Hidden or nested folders can be entered manually.
* Changing the root does not move or re-home existing Projects. It only affects
  folders created after the change, plus what the picker lists.

title: Sync chat pins with Hermes Desktop through the server pinned flag
body:
## Summary

Chat pins now use the same server-side `pinned` flag as Hermes Desktop, so a pin syncs both ways between the phone, Desktop and any other client of the host.

Previously Android pins were device-only (`SharedPreferences`) and never wrote the gateway flag, so Desktop pins showed only as an outline marker and phone pins never reached Desktop.

## How it works

- **Push:** Pin/Unpin sends `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with only `{"pinned": bool}` (the Desktop `session-pin-sync` contract), then requires an exact-id `GET` read-back with the same boolean before showing success. Failures keep the row unchanged and offer **Retry**.
- **Pull:** every list read adopts the server's `pinned` value, so pins made on Desktop or another device appear on the next refresh. The gateway already back-fills every pinned row onto each page, so old pinned chats need no extra reads.
- **Fencing:** confirmed writes go into a revision-fenced ledger (`ConfirmedChatPins`). A list, page, progress or search read that started *before* the write can't undo it; reads that start later stay authoritative. Lineage-aware for compressed chats.
- **Archive:** archiving a pinned chat sends `{"archived": true, "pinned": false}` in one request, as Desktop does. `pinned` is only sent for rows the server reported pinned, so gateways without the field still archive normally. Archived and unsaved draft rows don't offer Pin.
- **Migration:** device-only pins from 3.2.4 and earlier move to the server once (`migrateLegacyChatPins`). An id is dropped only after the server confirms the pin, already has it, reports `session_not_found`, or the chat is archived/hidden/internal. title: feat(chat): slash-command autocomplete backed by commands.catalog
body:
## What

Slash-command awareness in the composer, matching Desktop / hermes-webui:

- Typing a leading `/` opens a dropdown above the composer listing the commands available on the connected profile — fetched from the gateway's `commands.catalog` (cached per connection, invalidated on socket/state change), filtered locally per keystroke. Selecting an entry replaces the leading token with `/name `; the draft is never cleared.
- Sending a supported command executes it server-side via `slash.exec`: `exec` output renders as a **local notice card** (local context only, never enters request history); a `skill` directive is submitted as a normal prompt; `unsupported_command`, transport errors, or REST/SSE-only connections fall back to today's plain text send.
- New client wrappers in the `steerSession` style: `commandsCatalog` / `completeSlash` / `slashExec` on the WS client, surfaced through `desktop_gateway_client` and the application session as `slashCommandsSupported` / `fetchSlashCommands()` / `runSlashCommand()`.
- Catalog parsing is defensive (list or `commands`/`entries`/`items` envelope; executable set from the catalog, else a static fallback of the reviewed canonical commands).

## Busy-path behaviour

Slash execution runs on the **idle path only**. While a turn is live, `/cmd` still goes through `_sendWhileWorking` (the #191 steer contract) unchanged. `_dispatchSlashCommand` claims `_preparingSend` before its first await, so a double tap cannot both execute the command and submit the same text.

## Deliberate deviations

- Command output uses a dedicated local notice card rather than `GatewayNotice`, because `GatewayNotice` renders only in verbose mode — command output would be invisible by default.
- No `skills_changed` listener: the app has no such handling today; the catalog cache is per connection/session and invalidated on gateway bind and connection-state change.
- `complete.slash` is wired as a client wrapper but the v1 dropdown is a single-leading-token trigger; argument completion in the UI is a follow-up.

## Tests

- `test/slash_command_controller_test.dart` — 29 tests: trigger detection (`/`, `/mod`; mid-text `/` and `https://x` do not trigger), local filtering, fetch-once cache + refetch after invalidate, scope switch, gateway-failure fallback, executable-set parsing, wire shapes, plus 2 dropdown widget tests. Self-contained (fake gateway, no network).

## Summary

- Adds an explicit **Update now** action to the existing GitHub release prompt; the user can still choose Later, Skip or View release. No download starts without a tap.

The private download is streamed with progress/cancellation, strict HTTPS redirect hosts, and verified against the installed package, increasing versionCode and pinned production signing certificate before Android's installer is opened.

- This changes the intentionally browser-only update design and is proposed for the existing **GitHub APK** distribution. The installer permission and GitHub self-updater must not be shipped through Google Play; a separate Play-compliant build and update mechanism would be required before Play distribution. F-Droid or other differently signed builds retain the browser path and cannot update in place using the GitHub signer.
- Android still controls the permission and confirmation prompts. No silent install or automatic reopen is promised. A signing-key rotation fails closed until the pinned trust anchor is deliberately updated.
- The SHA-256 from GitHub confirms byte integrity, not independent publisher authenticity; the installed and pinned production signer checks provide a separate identity check. Android remains the final installer authority.
- No issue linked.

title: fix(nextgen): keep paging alive when a live turn grows the chat
body:
*** AI written. Old man reviewed..... ***

## What I found

I ran a deep audit of the 4.0.0 release line and one issue from it still ships in 4.0.0 stable. It is in the NextGen history path.

**Pagination dies after a live turn.** `loadOlder` sends `offset: _rowIds.length` to a server whose offset counts from the newest row. When a running turn persists a full page of rows while the reader is scrolled back, the newest end moves under that offset, the next page comes back entirely already shown, and `hasOlder = full && fresh.isNotEmpty` latches pagination off for good. The older history is then unreachable until a reconnect resyncs. I reproduced this in a test: open a 160 row chat, append 60 rows while scrolled back, and the next page is all known rows, so paging stops with most of the transcript still out of reach.

(The audit's companion finding, `getMessagesBytes` re-downloading stored images, already shipped its fix upstream in 4.0.1-rc.1 — `inline_images=false` is on `main`. The wire test here stays as a pin so it cannot silently regress.)

## What I changed

An all known full page no longer ends paging. It advances an `_olderFloor` past the shifted window instead, and any page that yields fresh rows resets the floor.

Known rows are filtered **before** `ngFromFirstTurn` trims the page start. On a partially-known page the unseen rows can be the tail of a long tool-heavy turn with no prompt among them; trimming first cut exactly those rows, and the floor then jumped a whole page past them, leaving silent holes and misplaced rows. Filtering first keeps every unseen row.

## How I verified it

- Three regression tests in `test/nextgen_long_chat_test.dart`: the growth test (fails on main with "an all-known page must not latch pagination off"), the tool-heavy-turn test from the review (fails on the first version of this PR with a hole in the long turn), and the wire-param pin.
- Mutation checked: reverting the lib changes turns the tests red again.
- `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean and the full suite passes on this branch, rebased onto current main (v4.0.4).

## One honest gap

Live-persisted rows that land inside an overlap window can be re-inserted as older items until the next resync. That duplication is transient and predates this change; this PR neither fixes nor worsens it.

## Known cost

Resetting the floor on a fresh page sends the next call back to `_rowIds.length`, so a growth burst costs one redundant fetch of already-shown rows per page. A running overlap shift would remove that and make the floor unnecessary; it was modelled on synthetic histories but not run against the controller, so it is deliberately left out of this PR and tracked in #280.

title: fix(nextgen): back closes the open sidebar instead of exiting the app
body:
## What

In NextGen mode the back gesture opened the sidebar, but a second back **exited the app** instead of closing the sidebar. This restores the expected toggle: back opens the sidebar, back again closes it.

## Root cause

`NgMainPage` wraps its `Scaffold` in `PopScope(canPop: false)`. When the drawer is open, Flutter's `DrawerController` adds a local-history entry to the route, but `ModalRoute.popDisposition` checks the `PopScope` veto **before** the local-history entry, so the pop is routed to `_onBack` with `isDrawerOpen == true`. That branch called `SystemNavigator.pop()`, leaving the app.

## Fix

`_onBack` now calls `scaffold.closeDrawer()` when the drawer is open (the close animation clears the local-history entry). Back with the drawer closed still opens it. Pushed pages (Settings, Scheduled, …) still pop normally first.

## Verification

- Updated regression test: back **opens → closes → reopens** the sidebar and asserts `SystemNavigator.pop` is never called.
- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos`: no issues.
- Full `flutter test`: **5793 passed**.

title: NextGen paging re-fetches already-shown rows after each growth burst (running-shift design)
body:
# NextGen paging re-fetches already-shown rows after each growth burst (running-shift design)

Found while fixing #275 (kept alive by the `_olderFloor` mechanism).

## The cost that remains

`loadOlder` re-anchors `_olderFloor = 0` on every page that yields fresh rows, so the next fetch goes back to `_rowIds.length`. When the chat grew by fewer rows than a page since the window was built, every page overlaps the shown rows by the same amount and each growth burst costs one redundant fetch of rows already on screen.

Concrete trace from the #275 review (60 rows appended to a 200-row history): fetch offsets come back as 60, 120, 120, 180, 180, 240 — every page of new rows costs a second fetch of rows already shown.

## Suggested direction: carry the overlap forward

Track the already-known rows each page returns in a running shift and fetch at `_rowIds.length + shift` instead of resetting. The floor becomes unnecessary: the offset never points back into the shown window, so an all-known page cannot occur from growth alone.

This design was modelled outside the app (20,000 random histories: no holes, no reordering of stored rows) but has **not** been run against `NgChatController`. Before implementing:

- Reproduce the offset trace above as a test pin on the current floor behavior.
- Re-run the shift model against the controller's fixtures (`test/nextgen_long_chat_test.dart`, `Paging across live growth` group) including the tool-heavy-turn regression test added in #275.
- Decide what happens to `_olderFloor` (likely deleted) and update the `_rowIds` doc comment accordingly.

Related known gap (also pre-existing, out of #275 scope): live-persisted rows landing inside an overlap window can re-insert as older items until the next resync. A correct shift shrinks that window and may make a clean regression fixture for it practical.


## Status: fix planned, waiting on #275

The fix for this will be implemented, but only after #275 merges into upstream `main`. The running shift *replaces* the `_olderFloor` mechanism that #275 introduces, so building it now would fork the same code path in two competing PRs. Once #275 is on `main`, the shift PR lands on top of it as a clean simplification: both of #275's growth regression tests carry over unchanged as acceptance criteria, plus an offset-trace test pinning that no offset is fetched twice.

Spike evidence (throwaway branch, discarded, nothing pushed): the shift was prototyped against the real `NgChatController` with the floor deleted. All of #275's paging tests passed, and the trace test showed the floor's redundant fetches `[0, 60, 120, 120, 180, 180, 240]` become strictly increasing offsets with zero re-fetches under the shift. So the design holds against the controller, not just the synthetic model.

title: Dashboard password login fails against gateway Webapp: suffixed session cookie name not matched
body:
## Summary

Dashboard password login against a **gateway-served Webapp** (`hermes webapp`, Hermes 0.23.1) always fails in Ares v4.0.4 with:

> Gateway connected, but the dashboard could not be reached or authenticated. Check the dashboard details or clear them to skip.

The login itself succeeds (`POST /auth/password-login` → 200), but the app cannot find the session cookie, because the Webapp suffixes every sign-in cookie name with a per-gateway id.

## Root cause

`DashboardClient._login()` (`lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart`, ~L2657) matches:

```dart
r'((?:__Host-|__Secure-)?hermes_session_at)=([^;,\s]+)'
```

The gateway Webapp sets (cookie names only, values redacted):

```
set-cookie: __Host-hermes_session_at_06bc9faebdfd8a6e=...
set-cookie: __Host-hermes_session_rt_06bc9faebdfd8a6e=...
set-cookie: __Host-hermes_session_provider_06bc9faebdfd8a6e=...
set-cookie: __Host-hermes_webapp_signin_06bc9faebdfd8a6e=...
```

This is intentional on the server side (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/cookies.py`): *"on the gateway's Webapp every one of these names is followed by `_<gateway>` (`<gateway>` from a digest of the gateway's home) … two gateways' Webapps on one hostname keep their own logins"*. The standalone `hermes dashboard` still uses the bare names, which is why it works there.

So the regex never matches → `Dashboard login succeeded but no session cookie found` → `getModelInfo()` throws → the generic error above.

## Repro

1. Hermes 0.23.1 with `webapp.enabled: true`, basic-auth provider, published over `tailscale serve` on `https://<host>.ts.net` (443).
2. In Ares, add a connection with dashboard port `443`, dashboard username/password, Desktop Gateway URL `https://<host>.ts.net`, profile set.
3. Save → the error above. `curl` with the same credentials against the same origin gets 200 on `/auth/password-login` and 200 on `/api/model/info`.

## Suggested fix

Accept the optional gateway suffix and send the cookie back under its real name, e.g.:

```dart
r'((?:__Host-|__Secure-)?hermes_session_at(?:_[0-9a-f]+)?)=([^;,\s]+)'
```

(group 1 is already reused as the cookie name, so the request side needs no other change). A unit test with a suffixed `Set-Cookie` alongside the existing bare/`__Host-`/`__Secure-` cases would cover it.

## Workaround

Point the Desktop Gateway URL at a standalone `hermes dashboard` instead of the gateway Webapp; it sets un-suffixed cookie names.

title: fix(dashboard): accept gateway-suffixed session cookie names
body:
## Problem

Ares could not use the dashboard served by the gateway Webapp, in two steps:

1. **Login returned 200, but no session cookie was found.** The Webapp suffixes every sign-in cookie
   name with `_<gateway>` (a digest of the gateway's home — `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/cookies.py`),
   so it sets `__Host-hermes_session_at_06bc9faebdfd8a6e` instead of `__Host-hermes_session_at`.
   `DashboardClient._login()` only accepted the bare name and its `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefixes, so
   it threw `Dashboard login succeeded but no session cookie found`.
2. **After that, every request was rejected as signed out.** Behind the Webapp's sign-in gate a
   cookie session is bound to the browser credential the gateway serves: the login also sets
   `hermes_webapp_signin_<gateway>`, and the gate treats a session cookie presented without a
   matching binding as signed out (`hermes_cli/webapp_sign_in.py`). The app sent only the access
   cookie, so `/api/sessions` and `/api/auth/ws-ticket` were rejected with
   `session_rejected reason=signed_out` while the login itself succeeded.

The standalone `hermes dashboard` keeps the bare names and sets no binding, which is why it worked.

## Fix

`lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart`, `DashboardClient._login()`:

- match each cookie under its **real** name: optional `__Host-`/`__Secure-` prefix, optional
  `_<gateway>` hex suffix;
- send the access cookie and, when the login set it, the `hermes_webapp_signin` binding in one
  `Cookie` header (`a=b; c=d`).

`_login()` is the only place the app builds that header, so every dashboard consumer inherits it:
`/api/` calls, the WebSocket ticket and delegated task history. Without the binding the header is
exactly what it was before.

## Tests

`test/connection_manager_test.dart`:

- `accepts a gateway-suffixed __Host- session cookie` — a suffixed access cookie is recognised and
  sent back verbatim.
- `sends the gateway sign-in binding beside the session cookie` — a login that sets suffixed `at`,
  `rt`, `provider` and `webapp_signin` cookies yields
  `Cookie: __Host-hermes_session_at_…=…; __Host-hermes_webapp_signin_…=…` on both the `/api/` request
  and `/api/auth/ws-ticket`.

Both are red against the previous pattern. Existing bare and `__Secure-` cases still pass.

Fixes #281

title: fix(nextgen): carry paging overlap forward instead of re-fetching shown rows
body:
*** AI created, old man reviewed ***

## The cost #275 left on the table

#275 kept paging alive across a live turn by latching a floor: when a page came back entirely already-shown, we skipped past that window. But the floor only handles the all-known case. Whenever a page *does* yield fresh rows, paging re-anchors on the shown rows (`_olderFloor = 0`, next offset `_rowIds.length`) — and if the chat grew since the window was built, that offset points back into the shown window again on *every* page. A 60-row burst on a 200-row history fetched offsets `0, 60, 120, 120, 180, 180, 240`: each page of new rows cost one redundant fetch of rows already on screen.

## Commit 1 — carry the overlap forward

Each page's already-known rows are exactly the ones a live turn appended after the window was built, so we accumulate them in a running shift and fetch at `_rowIds.length + shift`. The offset never points back into the shown window, so an all-known page cannot occur from growth alone — and `_olderFloor` becomes dead weight and is deleted. The burst above now fetches `0, 60, 120, 180, 240`: strictly increasing, zero re-fetches.

The subtlety that shaped #275 still holds: rows trimmed to the first turn boundary count as neither known nor shown, so the next page re-reads exactly them. The shift preserves that by construction — trimmed rows contribute to neither term of the offset.

## Commit 2 — a live turn's stored rows stop paging back in

The gap #280 called out beside it, now fixed rather than just shrunk. A live turn streams into one aggregate reply, but the gateway persists it as many stored rows whose ids the client never learned. When a burst outgrew the whole window, the next page re-served those rows, dedup missed them, and the turn re-inserted itself as older duplicate items until the next resync.

After `turn.end`/`message.complete`/`turn.error`, the controller walks the newest pages and adopts the unknown run at the tail — only rows above the last known one, since unknown rows below it are older history not yet shown. A window rebuild mid-fetch aborts the walk, and anything that persists between a fetch and its adopt stays covered by the shift, which remains the correctness backstop: worst case a duplicate survives until resync, never a lost row or a re-fetched offset.

## Tests

- New pin: `a growth burst never re-fetches an offset` reproduces the trace above and asserts offsets strictly increase across the whole session. Red on the floor code with the literal `[0, 60, 120, 120, 180, 180, 240]`, green here with `[0, 60, 120, 180, 240]`.
- New pin: `a live turn does not re-insert its stored rows as older items` drives a real WS `turn.end` over a 120-row burst on a 60-row window; without the adopt the burst's prompts page back in duplicated, with it none do.
- Both #275 growth regressions carry over **unchanged**, as promised in #280 — including the tool-heavy-turn case, which under the shift covers `[0, 200)` with no gap.
- Full suite 5800/5800 green; `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean.

Fixes #280

title: Sending a message fails with "Not sent: invalid_params" on Hermes 0.23.2: prompt.submit has no submission_id
body:
## Summary

In Ares v4.0.5, every message I send to a Hermes 0.23.2 gateway fails with:

> Not sent: invalid_params

It fails in existing chats and in brand-new chats, and Retry fails the same way.

## Cause

`GatewayTurnCoordinator` (`lib/core/services/gateway_turn_coordinator.dart`, around L674) sends:

```dart
client.send('prompt.submit', {
  'session_id': runtime.runtimeSessionId,
  'version': GatewayTurnRecoveryCapability.promptSubmitVersion,
  'client_turn_id': clientTurnId,
  'text': promptText,
  ...
});
```

There is no `submission_id` or `input_id`. Hermes issue NousResearch/hermes-agent#151715 documents that the gateway refuses `prompt.submit` without one of them, with a bare `invalid_params` (the check is in `AuthorityConnection.submission`, `gateway/session_controls.py`). Hermes logs nothing for the refusal, and my server logs show nothing for it either.

I read this from the source and have not captured the wire traffic, so I can't rule out another field also being involved.

## Suggested fix

Send a fresh UUID as `submission_id` with every `prompt.submit` (reusing it on a retry of the same turn). Hermes Desktop does this for sends that carry no identity.

## Environment

- Ares - formerly Hermes Android v4.0.5 (Android)
- Hermes Agent v0.23.2, gateway running as a system service
- Reached via `https://hermes.remotomatic.com` (reverse proxy) and via the Tailscale address

## Steps

1. Connect Ares to the gateway.
2. Open any chat (new or existing) and send a message.
3. The message shows "Not sent: invalid_params" with a Retry button; Retry fails the same way.

## Expected

The message is sent and the turn runs.

## Related

- NousResearch/hermes-agent#151715 (gateway refuses prompt.submit without submission_id/input_id)

title: NextGen: no Read aloud (TTS) action and code blocks are hard to copy (regression vs Classic)
body:
**Version:** Ares 4.0.5 (arm64), NextGen interface, Android.

**Problem:** NextGen has no Read aloud (TTS) action anywhere, and code blocks are hard to copy. Classic had both, so switching to NextGen is a regression.

**Read aloud**
- `lib/nextgen/` contains no TTS code at all (no `flutter_tts`, no "read aloud" string).
- The only `onReadAloud` / `_readAssistantText` wiring is in `lib/core/screens/chat_screen.dart` (Classic).
- NextGen's reply action row in `lib/nextgen/ui/chat_view.dart` (around line 1486) offers only Copy, Report AI output and Retry.
- The CHANGELOG entry for #271 (quick-action chips: Copy / Select text / Read aloud / Regenerate) and the README line "Copy/select text, Read aloud…" read as if they apply to both interfaces. They only apply to Classic.

**Code blocks**
- On a phone, copying a single fenced block in NextGen is awkward. I could not copy a block cleanly with the per-block control or by selecting it. The whole-reply Copy works, but it copies everything.
- Classic's message action sheet made this easy.

**Expected:** NextGen offers Read aloud (and Stop) on every assistant message, not only the latest one, and a code-block Copy button that is always visible and one tap.

**Workaround:** Settings → switch back to Classic.

Filed on behalf of a user by their Hermes agent; I checked the v4.0.5 source rather than a device, so the exact failure mode of the code-block copy needs confirming on the reporter's phone.

title: fix(nextgen): read aloud on every reply and one-tap code-block copy (#288)
body:
Fixes #288

NextGen had no TTS at all while Classic offered Read aloud on every assistant reply, and copying one fenced block meant discovering a small icon or dragging a selection across the fence. This restores parity.

## Read aloud
- New `NgReadAloud` controller (`lib/nextgen/data/read_aloud.dart`), one playback engine per chat view:
  - **Read aloud / Stop on every completed assistant reply's action row** (not only the latest); streaming replies get it once final.
  - Starting a reply stops whichever reply was being read; only one Stop is shown at a time. Claims are serialized so two quick taps cannot interleave.
  - Switching chats, or a retry/history reload that removes the reading reply, stops playback.
  - Voice selection mirrors Classic (`voice_name`/`voice_locale` prefs, speech rate 0.48), applied best-effort so a missing voice degrades to the engine default.
  - Android uses the same completion-correlated `FlutterVoiceReplySpeaker` as Classic hands-free: long replies are chunked to the engine's input limit and Stop is a real playback barrier. Other platforms use generation-guarded completion/cancel/error side channels, including a one-shot swallow for a stopped utterance's late cancel.
  - Playback failure surfaces the existing "Read aloud is unavailable on this device" toast.
  - Starting read aloud stops active dictation (Classic settles the mic before playback).

## Code blocks
- `MarkdownCodeBlock` gains an opt-in `showCopyLabel`: NextGen's fences render a labelled **Copy code** button (larger tap target, one obvious tap) wrapped in `Flexible` so long localized labels ellipsize instead of overflowing at narrow widths / large text scales. Classic keeps its icon-only header; the tooltip and exact-source copy behavior are unchanged.

## Localization
- `ng_read_aloud` added to all 12 ARB locales (reusing Classic's `read_aloud` translations); `app_localizations` regenerated. Stop reuses the existing `ng_stop`.

## Verification
- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos`: no issues.
- 21 new tests in `test/nextgen_read_aloud_test.dart`: claim/stop/switch races, failure and prepare-failure recovery, voice prefs, dispose, non-Android side channels (incl. late-cancel swallow), streaming gate, chat-switch stop, labelled copy clipboard exactness, 280dp + text scale 3.0 overflow guard, Classic unchanged.
- Full local suite + Play distribution tests: see latest run (posted before merge).
- Focused diff review: approve, no blocking findings; its three hardening suggestions are implemented in the second commit.

Note for the reporter: the per-block copy control already existed and copies the exact fence source (covered by tests); the labelled button makes it discoverable. The exact on-device failure mode in #288 was not reproducible from source alone — please confirm on a device after the next release.

title: v4.0.8 still fails on Hermes 0.23.2: session.create / session.resume send params the gateway rejects (invalid_params)
body:
## Summary

After #285 / v4.0.7 the `prompt.submit` params are fine, but sending still fails for me on Ares v4.0.8 against Hermes 0.23.2:

- Sending a message: "Not sent: invalid_params" (new chats and existing chats, Retry fails the same way)
- Opening a chat: "Live updates are unavailable: invalid_params"

I believe both come from two other gateway calls that send params the 0.23.x session authority refuses. I read this from source and have not captured the wire traffic.

## Cause

On the authority route the gateway's params models forbid unknown keys and enforce enums (`Params` has `extra="forbid"` in `tui_gateway/contracts/base.py`; canonical models are in `tui_gateway/contracts/canonical_sessions.py`).

1. `session.create` (`lib/nextgen/data/chat_controller.dart`, `_ensureSession`, ~L1727) sends `'source': 'desktop'`. `CanonicalCreateParams.source` is `Literal['cli', 'tui', 'gui', 'acp', 'tool', 'oneshot']`, so `desktop` is refused. A chat with no runtime session yet calls this before `prompt.submit`, so the send fails.
2. `session.resume` (same file, ~L709 and ~L1276; also `lib/core/services/ws_client.dart` ~L1382) sends `'inline_images': false`. `CanonicalResumeParams` has no `inline_images` field (it accepts `session_id`, `title`, `latest`, `workspace`, `source`, `editor`, `api_key`, `defer_history`, `omit_messages`, `cols`, `display_projection`, `profile`), so it is refused. This is the "Live updates are unavailable" banner, and it also leaves the chat without a bound runtime session, which then leads into the `session.create` call above.

`inline_images` is valid on the legacy `SessionResumeParams` in `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py`, so this looks like the legacy params being used on the canonical route.

## Suggested fix

- Use an allowed `source` value for `session.create` on the authority route (for example `gui`), keeping `desktop` for legacy gateways.
- Drop `inline_images` from `session.resume` when the gateway uses session authority (or retry once without it, like the `submission_id` fallback).

## Environment

- Ares v4.0.8 (Android)
- Hermes Agent v0.23.2, gateway running as a system service
- Reached via `https://hermes.remotomatic.com` (reverse proxy)

## Related

- #285 (prompt.submit missing submission_id, fixed in v4.0.7)
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#151715

title: fix(nextgen): select the profile that holds the chats on a multiplexed gateway
body:
## Problem

NextGen, connected to a multiplexed Hermes gateway with the profile left on **Server default**, shows an
empty session list ("no chats yet") even though the account has chats. Tapping a profile chip makes them
appear, which points at the profile, not at the connection or the login.

## Cause

`ConnectScreen._profile` stays `null` unless the user taps a chip (`lib/nextgen/ui/connect_screen.dart:68`;
the chooser is only rendered for a gateway with more than one profile, `:637`). A null profile means
`DashboardApiClient` sends `GET /api/sessions` with no `profile=` parameter
(`lib/core/services/dashboard_api_client.dart:226`). The gateway answers a profile-less request from its own
default store, so chats kept in another profile are not in that page: an empty list without any error, which
NextGen renders as "no chats yet".

## Fix

- `DashboardApiClient.profileSessionCounts()` reads `GET /api/profiles/sessions` (`profile_totals`), the
  all-profiles view.
- `profileOwningAllChats(counts)` returns the single non-default profile that holds chats, and `null` when the
  choice is ambiguous, so the server default stays.
- `ConnectScreen._save()` uses it when no profile was picked and the gateway exposes more than one profile: if
  exactly one profile owns all the chats, the connection is saved with that profile (the same row is updated,
  so no duplicate connection appears).
- Also folded in: `_test()` no longer clears an already saved profile when the gateway reports an empty
  `profiles` list.

Best effort throughout: any failure keeps the current behaviour and the server default. A connection saved
before this change keeps its stored profile until it is connected again.

## Tests

`test/nextgen_profile_preselect_test.dart` covers the selection rule (only owner, ambiguity, default-only),
the `profile_totals` parsing, an unexpected payload, and error propagation.

Locally: `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean, targeted test green, full `flutter test` suite passing (5836
tests) on Flutter 3.44.0.

title: fix(gateway): canonical session.create/resume params on session authority (#291)
body:
## Problem

Refs #291 — on Ares v4.0.8 against Hermes 0.23.2, sending fails with `Not sent: invalid_params` and opening a chat shows `Live updates are unavailable: invalid_params`.

The 0.23+ gateway routes session RPCs through the canonical session authority, whose params models are `extra="forbid"` (`tui_gateway/contracts/base.py`, `canonical_sessions.py`):

1. `session.create` sent `source: 'desktop'`, but `CanonicalCreateParams.source` is `Literal['cli','tui','gui','acp','tool','oneshot']`.
2. `session.resume` sent `inline_images: false`, which `CanonicalResumeParams` does not define (it is a legacy-only field in `contracts/sessions.py`).

## Root cause of the misroute

The app already had a `sessionAuthority` flag, but it read `session_authority` at the **top level** of the `gateway.ready` frame. The gateway nests it inside `params.payload` (`tui_gateway/ws.py`, since its introduction in NousResearch/hermes-agent 3187905d07), so the flag was never true on the real wire — the flat test fixtures masked this. The recovery coordinator already reads the nested shape correctly; only the authority flag was dead.

## Fix

- One wire-shape reader, `WsClient.readyFrameHasSessionAuthority`, used by both `WsClient.sessionAuthority` and `NextGenGateway.sessionAuthority`.
- `session.create`: `source: 'gui'` on the authority route (NextGen `_ensureSession` and Classic `createSession`); `desktop` kept for legacy gateways.
- `session.resume`: omit `inline_images` on the authority route (NextGen `_attach` / `_reloadForCatchUp`, Classic `resumeSessionDetails` — also covers `desktop_gateway_client` recovery, which calls these helpers). `source: 'desktop'` stays: `CanonicalResumeParams.source` is a free string and the desktop surface hint is intended.
- Side effect (intended design, previously dead code): with the flag now live, authority gateways get `reasoning` instead of `reasoning_effort` on create, and model switches use `session.mutate` (a registered canonical method) instead of `config.set`.
- REST history `inline_images=false` query params are unchanged: the canonical stored-reads contract accepts them.
- Flat `session_authority` fixtures in `nextgen_model_switch_test.dart` updated to the real nested wire shape so tests exercise the production path.

## Tests

New `test/canonical_session_params_test.dart` (9 tests):
- wire-shape unit tests (nested matches; flat top-level must not match; legacy/absent frames),
- loopback WebSocket gateway enforcing the real canonical contract for `WsClient.createSession` / `resumeSessionDetails`,
- NextGen controller send/open paths against a strict fake gateway,
- legacy behaviour pinned unchanged on both surfaces.

On the unfixed code the tests reproduce both reported symptoms exactly (`Invalid params: source…`, `Live updates are unavailable: Invalid params: inline_images…`).

Local gates (Flutter 3.44.x, worktree at `0d38d1d` = v4.0.8 main):
- `dart format` on all changed Dart files
- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos` — No issues found
- `flutter test --no-pub` — **All tests passed (5840)**

## Compatibility / risk

Legacy gateways (no `session_authority` in the ready payload) keep the exact previous params. Authority gateways get the canonical shapes they require. No protocol, storage or UI changes.

## Known limitation (pre-existing, not introduced here)

The Classic desktop path's fire-and-forget `_rebindStoredSessions` runs one microtask hop after the transport handshake and does not await `gateway.ready`; on a gateway whose ready frame is delayed (slow skin resolve) that pre-bind can still send the legacy shape once and fail silently. Explicit user actions retry after the frame is pinned and succeed. Awaiting the ready frame inside `createSession`/`resumeSessionDetails` was prototyped and reverted: 30 existing lifecycle tests use fakes that never emit `gateway.ready`, so that hardening needs its own harness work. NextGen (the reported surface) awaits the ready frame before any call and is race-free.

## Review follow-up (test-only, head dd37007)

- Authority catch-up resync (`_reloadForCatchUp`) now pinned through a live loopback socket — all three resume sites covered.
- Loopback fake enforces full `extra="forbid"` parity on `session.create` keys, not just the source enum.
- Full suite at dd37007: **5841 passed**, analyze clean. Lib code byte-identical to the independently reviewed head 93e54a2.

title: fix(nextgen): replay open requests after the catch-up resume
body:
## Symptom
A chat that is waiting on a `clarify` question shows the question card in Hermes Desktop, but NextGen shows nothing when the app comes back to that chat.

## Cause
`NgChatController._reloadForCatchUp` (`lib/nextgen/data/chat_controller.dart`) calls `session.resume` and reads only `session_id` and `running`. It ignores `open_requests`, unlike the other two resume sites (`_attach`, `_catchUp`). A client that attaches after the question was asked gets no live `clarify` frame, so the replay in `open_requests` is the only way to see it. `_reloadForCatchUp` runs from `resync()` on foreground and whenever the `session.events.since` ring cannot be used (no `last_seq`, new epoch, truncated, or an error). In those cases the question was lost. If the turn was no longer shown as running, `_finishTurn` also cleared `request`.

## Fix
Deliver `open_requests` from that resume and bind them to the chat, as `_attach` does. The socket handler is extracted to `NextGenGateway.acceptServerRequest` (no behaviour change) so a test can wire a real `WsClient` to it.

## Tests
`test/nextgen_replayed_clarify_test.dart` uses a loopback gateway and an anonymised copy of a real Hermes 0.23 `session.resume` reply (`test/fixtures/nextgen_resume_with_clarify.json`: running chat, five-question `clarify`, session authority).
- Resync after a quiet resume: fails before the fix (`request` stays null), passes after.
- Cold `open()` with the same reply: passes before and after; kept as a regression guard.

`flutter analyze` is clean. `nextgen_replayed_clarify_test`, `nextgen_test`, `nextgen_catch_up_test` and `canonical_session_params_test` pass.

Note: the cold-open path already worked with this payload, so this fixes the resume/resync path. I could not reproduce a cold-open failure statically.

title: fix(nextgen): offer the profile after sign-in on a gated gateway
body:
Completes #292.

**Symptom:** on a gated multiplexed gateway NextGen shows an empty chat list and offers no profile chooser.

**Cause:** the unauthenticated `/api/status` probe has no `profiles`, and `lib/nextgen/ui/connect_screen.dart` only read them from it (chooser gated on `status.profiles.length > 1`, #292 preselect gated on `profiles.length > 1`). Also `profileOwningAllChats` (`dashboard_api_client.dart`) counts cron runs from `/api/profiles/sessions`, so it found no single owner.

**Fix:**
- After sign-in, read profiles from the authenticated `GET /api/profiles` when the probe had none, and show the chooser as a step before connecting (sign-in again from an existing connection goes through the same step).
- Preselect: count the chats NextGen lists per profile (page 1 of `/api/sessions`, minus cron rows). If default has none and exactly one other profile has some, choose it.

**Tests:** `test/nextgen_profile_preselect_test.dart` (`listProfiles`, `visibleChatCounts`, `profileHoldingVisibleChats` with the reported counts → `delta`). `flutter analyze` clean.

title: NextGen chats list shows one or two conversations: the first page is cron rows
body:
## Environment

Ares 4.0.x (NextGen), stock Hermes Agent gateway 0.23.x, ~1.4k sessions in `state.db`, ~750 of them `source='cron'`.

## What happens

The "All" list shows one or two chats. Typing any term in the search field returns plenty of others, including ones the list never shows. Scrolling does nothing: there is no scroll extent.

## Cause

1. `NgSessionsModel._refreshOnce` reads a single 60-row page (`lib/nextgen/ui/sessions_sidebar.dart:195`, request shape at `lib/core/services/dashboard_api_client.dart:297`): `limit=60&offset=0&order=recent&archived=exclude`, where `order=recent` is the gateway's activity order across every source.
2. Cron rows are dropped after the page arrives: `:200` removes `isUntitledCronShell` (`lib/core/models/session.dart:92`) and `:456` removes every `source='cron'` row from the chats list.
3. Pagination is scroll-only (`:326`, `extentAfter < 400`), so a one-row list never requests page two.

Every cron run leaves its own row, and a 15-minute job alone produces four empty rows per hour, ~75 per day. Those are exactly the rows the drawer hides, so they fill the page with nothing.

## Measured on a real gateway

`GET /api/sessions?limit=60&offset=0&order=recent&archived=exclude`:

| rows | kind |
|---|---|
| 55 | `source='cron'`, 0 messages, no title |
| 3 | `source='cron'` with content |
| 2 | desktop chats |

Two conversations rendered out of 60 rows, with 920 non-shell sessions behind them (1367 listable rows, 447 of them shells; the first real rows sit at positions 1, 25, 26, 58, 59, 61, 68...).

## Why search finds the others

Search does not page the list: it calls `GET /api/sessions/search` (`lib/core/services/dashboard_api_client.dart:281`), FTS5 over message content, with no recency order and no cron/archived/child filtering. The data is there; the list just never reaches it.

## Suggested fix

1. **Read until the list is usable:** loop bounded pages until there are enough non-cron rows or the store ends, and keep the server offset separate from `sessions.length` (`:229` reuses the row count, which the shell filter has already shrunk). No server change, crons section keeps the same scan.
2. **Ask the gateway for chats only:** `exclude_sources=cron` plus a separate `source=cron` read. Cheaper, but `session_browser_loader.dart` scans unfiltered on purpose to keep legacy cron ids, so that path needs care.

Either way, an explicit "load more" row would help: scroll-only pagination cannot grow a short list.

title: fix(nextgen): fill the chat list past cron-only pages
body:
Fixes #297

## Symptom
On a cron-heavy gateway (~750 cron rows among ~1.4k sessions) the NextGen "All" list shows one or two conversations, search finds the rest, and scrolling does nothing.

## Cause
`NgSessionsModel._refreshOnce` read a single 60-row activity-ordered page. Cron runs fill those pages, and the chat list hides them (`isUntitledCronShell` after the read, `isCronSession` in the chats projection), leaving one or two rows and no scroll extent — so the scroll-only `loadMore` never fired. `loadMore` also used `sessions.length` as the server offset, which the shell filter had already shrunk, so it re-read hidden rows instead of advancing.

## Fix (no server change)
- Refresh reads bounded pages (max 10 × 60) until at least 20 chat rows are collected or the store ends; cron rows with content are kept for the Crons section. Generation is re-checked after every page.
- The raw server offset is tracked separately from the filtered list length; `loadMore` pages from it and applies the same shell filter, deduping by id.
- An explicit **Load more** row appears whenever more rows exist and the list is not loading/searching — a short list has no scroll extent, so scroll-only paging cannot grow it.
- Search stays a single server-side read.

## Tests
`test/nextgen_cron_page_fill_test.dart`: cron-only first pages read on; bounded scan with load-more continuation from the raw offset; load-more offset counts raw rows (40 shells + 20 chats → offset 60, not 20) with dedupe and shell filtering; search single-read; widget regression proving the Load more row grows a two-chat list. The existing load-more invalidation test now seeds through a real refresh. All new tests fail on the pre-fix tree. `flutter analyze` clean; focused suites pass; full suite run on the combined tree before merge.
