title: fix(chat): scroll the transcript to the end when the keyboard opens
body:
*** AI created, old man reviewed ***

When I opened the keyboard mid conversation, the transcript just sat there. The composer moved up, the last message ended up behind the keyboard, and I had to scroll down by hand every single time I wanted to reply. This is the classic chat; NextGen was not touched.

I fixed it by watching for the keyboard opening on the composer's own focus. When the keyboard rises and the composer is the thing holding focus, the chat marks itself as near the end and rides the transcript down to the bottom, using the same scroll machinery that already follows a streaming reply. A dialog or bottom sheet that steals focus gets its own keyboard, and a parked chat stays parked while it is up. If the keyboard is already open and I tap into the composer afterward, the jump still happens, once. Scrolling away while the keyboard stays open is respected, the chat does not yank me back on every keystroke, and a fresh stream re arms auto follow.

I wrote the failing widget test first and watched it fail for the right reason, then made it green. Four new tests pin the behavior: the jump on keyboard open, a held open keyboard not re jumping after I scroll away, a dialog keyboard leaving a parked chat alone, and auto follow coming back when a stream starts with the keyboard up. I also mutation checked the fix, reverting each piece of it in turn takes a test down, so the tests are load bearing and not decoration.

No gateway changes, this is all client side on the stock RPC surface. Full test suite green and flutter analyze --fatal-infos clean at this head.

title: fix(chat): handle /new locally like the desktop instead of slash.exec
body:
*** AI created, old man reviewed ***

When I typed /new and hit send, nothing happened. The app was sending the command to the gateway's slash worker, which is a headless process with no screen. That command wants a "this starts a fresh session, are you sure?" confirmation first, the worker has nowhere to show one, so it always answered "cancelled, no input" and my chat never moved. I reproduced it directly against a live gateway by piping the command into the worker.

The desktop app never had this problem because it owns /new locally and never asks the worker. I made the phone do the same thing. Typing /new, or its alias /reset, now opens a fresh draft chat right away, carrying over the model and project of the chat I was in, and an optional title works too: /new My next chat. The command is consumed from the composer and never reaches the gateway, so there is nothing left to cancel. The name is canonicalized the same way the command catalog does it, so //new lands on the local handler too. Gateway owned commands like /status still run through slash.exec exactly as before, and this works on plain REST transports too since the local path needs no socket.

I wrote the widget tests first and watched them fail for the right reason. Five tests pin it: /new never hits the gateway and never leaks to the model as prose, the title argument, the /reset alias, //new, and a regression check that /status still goes through the gateway. A seven mutant battery (drop the intercept, ignore the title, skip consuming the composer, drop model inheritance, leak as prose, drop canonicalization, drop the title fallback) all died, so the suite genuinely binds the behavior. Two rounds of fresh context review: the first asked for full test hook and archive callback forwarding plus the prose leak test, the second approved with no blocking findings.

No gateway changes, client side only, classic mode. Full test suite green and flutter analyze --fatal-infos clean at this head.

title: docs: audit of slash dropdown entries the gateway refuses to run
body:
Following up on the `/new` work in #301: we ran a full audit of the slash-command dropdown against a live stock Hermes gateway (v0.23.3), driving the exact RPC path the app uses (`session.create source=gui` → `slash.exec`) and executing every stock command bare in a throwaway session.

The dropdown shows all 243 rows the gateway's `commands.catalog` advertises, but only 45 of the 98 stock commands actually execute. The other 52 come back as `unsupported_command` — and because the app treats that like any other send-path error, the typed text falls through and is delivered to the agent as a plain chat message. So picking `/redraw`, `/model`, `/sessions` and friends from the dropdown and sending it just posts the literal text into the conversation. This is the same failure family that broke `/new` (a command the shared gateway surface can't run); #301 fixed `/new` by handling it client-side, and `/new` is now the only one of the 52 with an answer today.

The full breakdown is in `docs/SLASH_COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED_AUDIT.md`: the accepted set matches the gateway's reviewed allow-list in `gateway/session_commands.py` exactly, and the refused entries split into terminal/client-machine commands, session-runtime commands the app already covers through other RPCs or screens (`model`, `steer`, `branch`, `sessions`), and host-state commands where the gateway even attaches a "run this in a terminal instead" hint that we currently discard.

We're working on the client-side fix — filtering the dropdown so refused entries aren't offered, driven by catalog data rather than a hardcoded list (the `{'new','reset'}` mirror in #301 already showed how those drift), surfacing the refusal hints instead of silently converting the text to prose, and wiring the commands that have RPC equivalents to them. But the simpler alternative belongs upstream: if `commands.catalog` simply stopped advertising these rows for non-terminal surfaces — or published an `executable` set, which the app's catalog parser already tolerates — the dropdown would be honest with no client change at all.

Marked draft deliberately: this is a docs-only audit for now, and we'd like maintainer input on which direction to take before the code lands. Happy to align either way; the client-side filter can land regardless.

title: fix(chat): stop refused slash commands leaking into chat as prose
body:
Follows up on the audit in #302. **Jon is actively working on these fixes right now** — this PR is being built task-by-task and each step is reported in the comments as it lands.

The audit found 51 stock slash commands the `/` dropdown advertises but the gateway refuses with `unsupported_command` — and today a refusal silently falls through, delivering the literal text (e.g. `/redraw`) to the agent as a chat message. This PR fixes that in three client-side steps plus one upstream ask:

1. **No prose leak** — a refused *catalogued* command renders a local notice card carrying the gateway's own "run this in a terminal" hint (`data.detail`) when present, else a generic unavailable line. Unknown `/`-lines keep the plain-send fallback.
2. **Learned refusals** — the first refusal marks the command for the life of the connection and the dropdown stops offering it. No hardcoded mirror list (the `{'new','reset'}` lesson from #301): it self-corrects on reconnect if a server update starts accepting a command.
3. **Wire the equivalents** — `/model` opens the existing model picker; `/sessions` and `/resume` open the session browser; same local-intercept pattern as `/new`, canonicalized so `//model` can't slip past.
4. **Upstream ask** — tracked as a comment on #302: stock `commands.catalog` publishing an `executable` set (which this app's parser already tolerates) would make the learned set unnecessary.

Every code step follows the usual gates: watched red loop first, mutation check on each fix, full suite + analyzer, and an independent fresh-context review before this leaves draft.

title: chore(deps): enable Dependabot version updates
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/dependabot.yml` so Dependabot opens routine version-update PRs for Ares.

Until now only Dependabot **security** updates were enabled. Without this file a dependency was only bumped when an advisory existed, and none of the last 100 PRs came from Dependabot.

## What it covers

| Ecosystem | Directory | Manifests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pub` | `/` | `pubspec.yaml`, `pubspec.lock` |
| `gradle` | `/android` | Gradle plugins, libraries, wrapper |
| `gradle` | `/tools/embedded-push-rebuild` | Build adapter plugins |
| `github-actions` | `/` | `.github/workflows/*.yml` |
| `pip` | `/server/mobile-push` | `pyproject.toml` |
| `pip` | `/tools/fake_gateway` | `requirements.txt` |

Each entry runs weekly at 06:00 UTC, keeps at most 10 PRs open and labels them `pr: dependency-update`. These are the same settings as the other rusty4444 repositories. The label now exists in this repository, so it is applied.

## Notes

- Configuration only: no app, build or workflow change.
- Validated against the SchemaStore `dependabot-2.0` schema.
- Once this is on `main`, Dependabot checks every entry straight away, so expect a first batch of PRs.
- Security updates are unchanged and are not limited by the weekly schedule.

title: chore(deps): bump org.robolectric:robolectric from 4.16 to 4.18.1 in /android
body:
Bumps [org.robolectric:robolectric](https://github.com/robolectric/robolectric) from 4.16 to 4.18.1.
Release notes

Sourced from org.robolectric:robolectric's releases.

Robolectric 4.18.1 is a minor release that fixes several issues and improves the Robolectric simulator.

It fixes data races that ThreadSanitizer reported when several threads link calls to the same shadow method at once (#11784, #11786). It also fixes ShadowServiceManager.waitForService, which never blocked and could throw IllegalMonitorStateException (#11758), and scheduled task time queries on ShadowPausedLooper, which returned wrong times on newer SDKs and could race when called off the Looper thread (#11780, thanks to Brett Chabot). Content providers are now installed for lazily created applications (#11775), and Choreographer display receivers are disposed, which fixes a CloseGuard leak and stale clock callbacks (#11688, thanks to @​utzcoz).

For the simulator, it handles mouse and keyboard input when running headless (#11750) and advances the system clock by the time spent rendering (#11783). It also adds two opt-in system properties, which the simulator Gradle plugin turns on: robolectric.bindRealServices=true binds to the app's own services the way the system does (#11748), and robolectric.installDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler=true installs an uncaught exception handler that logs crashes the way Android does (#11734).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/robolectric/robolectric/compare/robolectric-4.18...robolectric-4.18.1

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed (#11625, #11633). As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

Other Highlights

  • Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36 (#11578).
  • Robolectric no longer prints the "restricted method in java.lang.System has been called" warnings on JDK 24+ (#11482).
  • The shadow annotation processor now supports KSP (#10996).
  • Lots of performance improvements:
    • Resource values are shared between bags and themes instead of copied (#11726, #11595)
    • Faster shadow method lookups (#11723, #11593)
    • Cached resource reference resolution (#11586)
    • Cached service and plugin lookups (#11451, #11594, #11631)
    • Native runtime assets are extracted once and shared (#11453, #11522)
    • Faster class loading checks in the sandbox (#11662)
    • Regexes compiled once instead of on every use (#11399, #11400, #11401)
  • Conscrypt is now enabled by default on Mac arm64 (#11352).

What's Changed

  • Sign all .module metadata files. by @​brettchabot in robolectric/robolectric#11327
  • Fix Robolectric fontScale config being reset on SDK 24+. by @​copybara-service[bot] in robolectric/robolectric#11336
  • Add device-specific permission support to Robolectric shadows. by @​copybara-service[bot] in robolectric/robolectric#11342
  • Bump version to 4.18-SNAPSHOT. by @​brettchabot in robolectric/robolectric#11340
  • Fix aggregateDocs gradle task. by @​brettchabot in robolectric/robolectric#11341
  • Add missing @Deprecated annotation in SQLiteMode by @​MGaetan89 in robolectric/robolectric#11329
  • Update AGP internals copies by @​MGaetan89 in robolectric/robolectric#11328
  • Make :shadows:framework:compileJava compatible with Gradle's configuration cache by @​MGaetan89 in robolectric/robolectric#11314
  • Let shadows for the SafetyCenterManager check permissions correctly. by @​copybara-service[bot] in robolectric/robolectric#11332
  • Remove Conscrypt's XDH KeyPairGenerator to fix TLS issues by @​copybara-service[bot] in robolectric/robolectric#11349
  • Update tests to run on API 24+ by @​copybara-service[bot] in robolectric/robolectric#11350

body:

Release notes

Sourced from org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm's releases.

1.11.0

Various

  • Kotlin was updated to 2.2.20 (#4545).
  • Improved the published jar files (#3842, #4599).
  • Various documentation improvements, including complete rewrites of structured concurrency and error handling-related KDoc (#4433, #4596).

Breaking changes and deprecations

  • Moved Promise-related functions from JS and Wasm/JS to the new web target. On Wasm/JS, this is a breaking change. Before the change, Promise on Wasm/JS could work with arbitrary Kotlin types, but now, only JsAny subtypes are accepted (#4563).
  • Changed handling of coroutine exceptions that can't be propagated on JS and Wasm/JS. B efore, exceptions were logged, but now, they are reported to the JS runtime (#4451, #4631).
  • Deprecated using CoroutineDispatcher as the coroutine context key; now, ContinuationInterceptor has to be used instead (#4333).
  • Advanced the deprecation levels on kotlinx-coroutines-test APIs (#4604).
  • Added lint functions that mark passing a Job to coroutine builders as deprecated (#4435).

Bug fixes and improvements

  • Added a callsInPlace(EXACTLY_ONCE) contract to runBlocking in code shared between JVM and Native (#4368).
  • Added a callsInPlace(EXACTLY_ONCE) contract to suspendCancellableCoroutine (#4574).
  • Fixed flowOn incorrectly handling ThreadContextElement updates (#4403).
  • Fixed exceptions in user-supplied Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler instances causing the internal coroutines machinery to fail (#4516).
  • Fixed CoroutineDispatcher.asScheduler in the RxJava integration not cancelling outstanding work when a Worker gets cancelled, which led to memory leaks in some scenarios (#4615).
  • Fixed SharedFlow entering an invalid state when a subscriber and an emitter are cancelled simultaneously (#4583).
  • Fixed an R8 optimization leading to shareIn/stateIn coroutines getting garbage-collected (#4646). Thanks, @​solevic!

Small additions

  • Added CompletableDeferred.asDeferred for obtaining a read-only Deferred view (#4408).
  • Added SharedFlow.asFlow for obtaining a Flow view with hidden hot flow semantics (#4530). Thanks, @​g000sha256!

body:
Updates the requirements on [uvicorn](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from uvicorn's releases.

Version 0.54.0

📨 Send metadata after the response body

uvicorn 0.54.0 adds response trailers and 103 Early Hints to its experimental HTTP/2 implementation through zttp.

uv add uvicorn==0.54.0 "zttp>=0.0.34"
  • Send HTTP/2 response trailers (#3146). The ASGI http.response.trailers extension lets applications send metadata, such as checksums, after the response body. Clients must send TE: trailers to receive them. Multiple trailer messages are combined before completing the response.
  • HTTP/2 remains experimental and opt-in. Enable it with --http zttp --http2. Upgrade-based h2c and WebSockets over HTTP/2 remain unsupported.

💡 Hint at resources before the final response

  • Send 103 Early Hints over HTTP/2 (#3137). Applications can use the ASGI http.response.early_hint extension to send resource hints before the final response. Each supplied link becomes a separate Link header.

Full changelog: 0.53.0...0.54.0

Changelog

Sourced from uvicorn's changelog.

0.54.0 (September 24, 2026)

HTTP/2 support remains experimental. Install zttp>=0.0.34 and enable it with --http zttp --http2.

Added

  • Add HTTP/2 103 Early Hints through the ASGI http.response.early_hint extension (#3137)

This release adds experimental HTTP/2 support through zttp. Enable it with --http zttp --http2. Upgrade-based h2c and WebSockets over HTTP/2 are not supported.

body:
Updates the requirements on [dnspython](https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from dnspython's releases.

dnspython 2.9.2

A malicious WKS record in text format can consume excessive memory and CPU when parsed, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.2

  • A maliciously crafted zone file could use a WKS record to consume excessive memory and CPU, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

2.9.1

  • LOC text parsing now converts the altitude, size, horizontal precision, and vertical precision fields to centimeters exactly, and requires them to be decimal numbers of meters with at most two fractional digits, as RFC 1876 section 3 specifies. They were converted with float(), so 9.29m became 928 cm rather than 929 cm and the text and wire forms of the record disagreed, forms such as 1e3m, 1_000m, +10m, nanm, and infm were accepted, extra fractional digits were silently dropped, and an altitude outside the representable range was accepted and then failed in to_wire() with a non-DNS exception. dns.exception.SyntaxError is now raised for all of these.

  • The resolver now assigns a new random query id to every query.

  • For transports that require a 0 query id, set it in a way that does not break TSIG.

  • dns.message.QueryMessage.resolve_chaining() now caps the minimum TTL of a negative response with no SOA record at 300 seconds (dns.message.NEGATIVE_TTL_WITHOUT_SOA). Previously the TTL was left at its initial value of 2^32 - 1, so a single NXDOMAIN or NODATA response with no SOA, e.g. a spoofed one, stayed in the resolver cache for the life of the process.

  • DNSSEC validation now rejects an RRSIG whose type covered or class does not match the RRset, as RFC 4035 section 5.3.1 requires. This was not checked, so a revoked DNSKEY, which may only validate the DNSKEY RRset, still validated any RRset signed with its private key if the RRSIG claimed to cover DNSKEY.

  • dns.tokenizer.Tokenizer now ends a line at a carriage return, or at a carriage return followed by a line feed, unless the carriage return is in a quoted string. The carriage return of CRLF line ends used to stay in the last token of each line and in the text of a comment, so e.g. dns.zone.from_text() rejected a zone with CRLF line ends.

  • DNSSEC validation no longer uses a DNSKEY with the REVOKE flag set to validate anything other than the DNSKEY RRset. RFC 5011 section 2.1 says a revoked key must not be used for any other purpose, but it was a candidate key like any other, so as long as the revoked key was still published, data signed with its private key, e.g. by whoever compromised it, validated.

body:
Updates the requirements on [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.2.0

pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14716: -c now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled FileNotFoundError.

  • #8593: The indirect, ids and scope arguments of Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> -- and therefore of @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> -- are now keyword-only.

    Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)]) made the argvalues land in indirect and failed with indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist; such mistakes now fail with an understandable TypeError. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.

  • #993: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code 1:

    • a plugin that cannot be found -- via -p, pytest_plugins or PYTEST_PLUGINS -- exits with pytest.ExitCode USAGE_ERROR (4), like a conftest.py that fails to import;
    • a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken pytest11 entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with pytest.ExitCode INTERNAL_ERROR (3), with the traceback preserved.

    pytest.main now returns these codes instead of raising ImportError. Also fixed an IndexError from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #14742: The private _pytest.python.CallSpec2 name has been renamed to CallSpec. The old CallSpec2 alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14755: Schedule yield_fixture decorator for removal in pytest 10 or 11.

  • #14774: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1, all higher-scoped fixtures (module, package, and session) defined as instance methods are now deprecated.

    They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for class-scoped fixtures, see 10819 and 14011.

  • #14808: Passing a non-string value to a string-typed ini option now emits a pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning. This affects [tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml. In pytest 10 this will raise a TypeError, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.

  • #7323: Passing bytes to TerminalReporter.write_line() is now deprecated, pass a str instead.

New features

  • #14743: Full diff: now contains a legend explaining the + & - symbols in diff output.
  • #2781: When strict_markers is enabled, marker names used in -m expressions are now validated against registered markers.
  • #6881: Added the parametrize_long_str_id_strategy configuration option to control how long str/bytes parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ids=[...] or pytest.param(..., id=...) are not affected. Available strategies: short (default, values over 100 chars fall back to argname+index), sha256 (SHA-256 hex digest), legacy (keep full value), and disallow (error requesting explicit IDs).

Improvements in existing functionality

  • #10745: A RecursionError whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and unreadable. Pass --full-trace to see every frame.

title: chore(deps): bump xml from 6.6.1 to 7.1.0
body:
Bumps [xml](https://github.com/renggli/dart-xml) from 6.6.1 to 7.1.0.
Changelog

Sourced from xml's changelog.

7.1.0

  • Dart 3.13 and PetitParser 7.1.0 requirement.
  • Standard-compliant DOM position comparison:
    • Introduced XmlNode.compareDocumentPosition returning XmlDocumentPosition bitmask flags (isSame, isDisconnected, isPreceding, isFollowing, isContains, isContainedBy, isImplementationSpecific), matching W3C DOM Level 3 / DOM 4.
    • Deprecated XmlNode.compareNodePosition in favor of compareDocumentPosition.
  • XML attribute and namespace separation:
    • Added XmlAttribute.isNamespaceDeclaration to distinguish namespace declarations (xmlns or xmlns:*) from regular attributes.
    • Added elementAttributes getter on XmlAttributesBase and XmlHasAttributes to iterate over attributes excluding namespace declarations.
  • XPath 3.1 enhancements and W3C compliance:
    • Excluded namespace declarations from the attribute axis (@*), aligning with XPath 3.1 specification.
    • Restored document order for reverse-indexed axes with predicates.
    • Implemented canonical EQName path generation in fn:path (/Q{uri}name[idx], @Q{uri}name, text()[idx]).
    • Improved ID and IDREF resolution in fn:id, fn:idref, and fn:element-with-id with xml:id and DTD <!ATTLIST ... ID/IDREF> attribute declarations.
    • Introduced XPathConfiguration to configure evaluation contexts (custom variables, functions, namespaces, documents, environment variables, base URI, unparsed text loader, and trace callback). Deprecated passing variables and functions directly to xpath and xpathEvaluate.
    • Added XML serialization (fn:serialize) supporting XML, HTML, XHTML, text, JSON, and adaptive output methods with serialization parameters.
    • Added PetitParser-based regular expression transformer for XML Schema regex syntax supporting fn:matches, fn:replace, fn:tokenize, and fn:analyze-string.
    • Added fn:parse-ietf-date.
    • Standardized error handling with XPathErrorCode and W3C error codes.
    • Redesigned date, time, and duration types (xs:duration, xs:dayTimeDuration, xs:yearMonthDuration, xs:dateTime, xs:date, xs:time, and Gregorian date types) for strict W3C compliance.
    • Added support for xs:anyAtomicType, xs:error, and string-derived XML Schema constructors.
    • Added support for unparsed text and JSON document retrieval (fn:unparsed-text, fn:unparsed-text-lines, fn:unparsed-text-available, fn:json-doc) via unparsedTextLoader.
    • Added context-aware document lookup (fn:doc, fn:doc-available) and cross-platform environment variable resolution (fn:environment-variable, fn:available-environment-variables).
    • Added support for key sequences and native Dart Map and List structures in lookup expressions (?).
    • Integrated maps and arrays into dynamic function calls.
    • Added duration support in aggregation functions (fn:avg, fn:sum).
    • Protected arithmetic and math functions (fn:ceiling, fn:floor, duration operations) against Infinity and NaN.
    • Significant XPath evaluation performance optimizations:
      • Preserved document order on absolute paths (/, //), avoiding redundant sorting and deduplication fallbacks. Yields up to 775x speedup on large documents (e.g., at $N=10,000$, //* is ~775x faster dropping from 3.75s to 4.8ms; /root/item/name is ~609x faster dropping from 840ms to 1.38ms; //item is ~307x faster dropping from 870ms to 2.84ms).
      • Introduced two-tier node sorting with direct sibling indexing in DOM position comparisons for queries requiring deduplication.
      • Collapsed DescendantOrSelfAxis + ChildAxis into DescendantAxis for steps with non-positional predicates (e.g., //item[@id=100] is ~5.75x faster).
      • Cached small XPathInteger instances (0..128) and unboxed integer comparisons for zero-allocation positional predicate matching with early-exit loop termination.
      • Optimized sequence atomization with zero-allocation fast paths for empty and single-item sequences, along with primitive 1-vs-1 comparison fast paths.
    • Fix short-circuit evaluation for != general comparisons (#207).
    • Removed @experimental annotation from XPath API.
  • Add command-line XPath evaluation example tool (example/xml_xpath.dart).

7.0.1

  • Better namespace support across all parts of the library:
    • Namespaces of XmlDocument.parse and XmlDocumentFragment.parse are now resolved at parse-time and constant when manipulating the DOM (this aligns with other XML libraries and removes surprising behavior when moving nodes around).
    • Deprecate all namespace arguments and replace them with the more intention revealing namespaceUri and namespacePrefix.
    • Lower-level parser and event APIs can now enable and disable the validation and resolution of namespaces with validateNamespaces and withNamespaces. This is a BREAKING CHANGE to existing code using these lower-level APIs, as namespaces are no longer available by default.
    • Introduced XmlNamespaceException for error reporting of invalid namespaces.
    • XmlName is now immutable and the complexity with different states is gone.
    • Added XmlNamespace node type and XmlHasNamespaces mixin to support reading in-scope namespaces on nodes.
  • Correctly move nodes from their previous parent when inserting them into a new location, rather than throwing an XmlParentException. This aligns with standard DOM behavior and improves usability and performance. XmlDocumentFragment nodes are automatically expanded and their children are moved as well.
  • Improved performance and usability of XmlBuilder:
    • Significantly improve the performance of XmlBuilder as all namespace lookups are now in constant time.
    • Deprecated namespace(String uri, String? prefix) and namespaces(Map<String, String?> uriToPrefix) accessors that have an unusually awkward API. Replaced with namespaceUri(String? prefix, String? uri) and namespaceUris(Map<String, String> prefixToUri) with a clear prefix-uri order.

title: chore(deps): bump com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android from 1.23.0 to 1.24.0 in /android
body:
Bumps [com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android](https://github.com/tink-crypto/tink-java) from 1.23.0 to 1.24.0.
Release notes

Sourced from com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android's releases.

Tink Java v1.24.0

Tink is a multi-language, cross-platform library that provides simple and misuse-proof APIs for common cryptographic tasks.

This is Tink Java 1.24.0

The complete list of changes since 1.23.0 can be found here.

New Features

  • APIs which depend on what algorithms are registered now have an overload taking a configuration argument. Using these overloads allows to ensure that behavior is independent of what else is linked in the binary. For example, instead of keysetHandle.getPrimitive(Aead.class), users can now write keysetHandle.getPrimitive(TinkConfig2026.get(), Aead.class). Similary for key generation and serialization of keysets.

    The following configs are available: AeadConfig2026 (which does not contain the KMS algorithms; use KmsAeadConfig2026 for those), DeterministicAeadConfig2026, HybridConfig2026, JwtConfig2026, KeyDerivationConfig2026, MacConfig2026, PrfConfig2026, SignatureConfig2026, StreamingAeadConfig2026. In addition, TinkConfig2026 contains all of the above algorithms (except the KMS algorithms). Finally, RegistryConfiguration.java is available to make previous behavior (examining the registered algorithms) explicit.

    Finally, the Configuration interface needed to implement new behavior is completely public, and users can implement it themselves.

  • Added support for JWT ML-DSA signatures.

  • Added support for MLDSA44-Ed25519-SHA512 and MLDSA65-Ed25519-SHA512 Composite ML-DSA algorithms.

  • X-Wing HPKE is now also available on Android. In particular, it is available natively on Android 17 (or above), or otherwise on Android 12 (or above) with SDK Extensions version 22 or later.

  • Added predefined HPKE parameters.

  • Added the Prehash primitive interface for computing prehashes of messages, to support the prehash-and-sign paradigm (such as ML-DSA External Mu).

  • Updated 'org.conscrypt:conscrypt-openjdk-uber' to version 2.7.0.

Changes

  • Changed the named parameter name for SLH-DSA-SHA2-128S with Tink output prefix type from SLH_DSA_SHA2_128S_TINK to SLH_DSA_SHA2_128S for consistency with the other Tink languages.
  • In SignaturePemKeysetReader, treat Base64 decoding failures like other PEM key parsing errors.
  • In SignaturePemKeysetReader, continue parsing multi-key PEM bundles after encountering an unparsable key.
  • In SignaturePemKeysetReader, preserve the parsed RSA public exponent when importing RSA public keys instead of hardcoding 65537 (F4).
  • Fixed unchecked runtime exceptions in JwkSetConverter.toPublicKeysetHandle and SignatureJwkSetConverter.toPublicKeysetHandle when importing malformed JWK sets, ensuring they consistently throw a GeneralSecurityException.
  • Validate coordinate lengths against curve field size in JwkSetConverter and SignatureJwkSetConverter.
  • Fixed unchecked runtime exceptions in JsonKeysetReader.read and JsonKeysetReader.readEncrypted when reading malformed keysets, ensuring they consistently throw an IOException.
  • AesGcmSiv now uses Conscrypt if it's available on the class path, even if it is not installed. Previously, a Conscrypt provider needed to be installed for it to work.
  • Enforce canonical Base64url encoding in JwtFormat.strictUrlSafeDecode, preventing signature/MAC malleability from unused trailing bits.
  • Fixed StreamingAeadSeekableDecryptingChannel.read to always authenticate the final ciphertext segment when reaching the end of the plaintext, ensuring valid empty plaintexts return -1 (EOF) and rejecting truncated or unauthenticated empty trailing segments with an IOException.

Release notes

Sourced from org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm's releases.

1.11.0

Various

  • Kotlin was updated to 2.2.20 (#4545).
  • Improved the published jar files (#3842, #4599).
  • Various documentation improvements, including complete rewrites of structured concurrency and error handling-related KDoc (#4433, #4596).

Breaking changes and deprecations

  • Moved Promise-related functions from JS and Wasm/JS to the new web target. On Wasm/JS, this is a breaking change. Before the change, Promise on Wasm/JS could work with arbitrary Kotlin types, but now, only JsAny subtypes are accepted (#4563).
  • Changed handling of coroutine exceptions that can't be propagated on JS and Wasm/JS. B efore, exceptions were logged, but now, they are reported to the JS runtime (#4451, #4631).
  • Deprecated using CoroutineDispatcher as the coroutine context key; now, ContinuationInterceptor has to be used instead (#4333).
  • Advanced the deprecation levels on kotlinx-coroutines-test APIs (#4604).
  • Added lint functions that mark passing a Job to coroutine builders as deprecated (#4435).

Bug fixes and improvements

  • Added a callsInPlace(EXACTLY_ONCE) contract to runBlocking in code shared between JVM and Native (#4368).
  • Added a callsInPlace(EXACTLY_ONCE) contract to suspendCancellableCoroutine (#4574).
  • Fixed flowOn incorrectly handling ThreadContextElement updates (#4403).
  • Fixed exceptions in user-supplied Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler instances causing the internal coroutines machinery to fail (#4516).
  • Fixed CoroutineDispatcher.asScheduler in the RxJava integration not cancelling outstanding work when a Worker gets cancelled, which led to memory leaks in some scenarios (#4615).
  • Fixed SharedFlow entering an invalid state when a subscriber and an emitter are cancelled simultaneously (#4583).
  • Fixed an R8 optimization leading to shareIn/stateIn coroutines getting garbage-collected (#4646). Thanks, @​solevic!

Small additions

  • Added CompletableDeferred.asDeferred for obtaining a read-only Deferred view (#4408).
  • Added SharedFlow.asFlow for obtaining a Flow view with hidden hot flow semantics (#4530). Thanks, @​g000sha256!
  • Added a StateFlow.collectLatest overload returning Nothing to assist with finding unreachable code (#4454).
  • Added ReceiveChannel.consumeTo for consuming a ReceiveChannel into a MutableCollection (#4520).

title: feat(nextgen): add a Models page for model settings
body:
## Summary

Adds a **Models** page to the NextGen interface so model settings are readable in one place: the default model with what the gateway reports about it, the ordered fallback list, every helper-task model, and the providers with their allowance and rate limits.

It opens from NextGen **Settings → Model management**, **More → Model management** and the top of a chat's model picker. The classic model screen is unchanged.

## What changed

- `lib/nextgen/ui/models_page.dart`: the page (default model, fallback models, auxiliary models, providers).
- `lib/nextgen/ui/model_choice_sheet.dart`: searchable model picker with prices, used by every assignment on the page.
- `lib/nextgen/data/model_catalog.dart`: parses `model/options`, `model/info` and the auxiliary list. Endpoint addresses and key names are reduced to a boolean while parsing and never stored.
- `lib/nextgen/data/model_settings_controller.dart`: loads and saves. One write at a time, read-back before a save is reported, per-section loading and error state, and a dirty fallback draft survives a refresh.
- `lib/core/services/connection_manager.dart`: new `assignAuxiliaryModel` (existing method signatures are untouched, so test fakes still compile).
- 12 locale files and generated localisations for the new strings.
- `docs/model-management.md` and the README describe the page.

## Behaviour worth reviewing

- A `confirm_required` answer from the gateway shows the gateway's own warning and resends with `confirm_expensive_model: true` only if the user agrees.
- `reasoning_effort` is sent only for an explicit thinking-level change, and the control is offered only when the task row carries that key.
- Providers on a custom endpoint are listed but cannot be assigned, because an assignment without `base_url` would drop the endpoint on the gateway.
- Fallback rows are added, moved and removed, never edited in place. Nothing is sent until **Save fallback list**.

## Testing

- New tests: `test/nextgen_model_catalog_test.dart`, `test/nextgen_models_controller_test.dart`, `test/nextgen_models_page_test.dart`, `test/nextgen_models_l10n_test.dart`.
- Local at `67dd0ff`: `flutter analyze` reported no issues and the test suite passed, with `certificate_file_ownership_test.dart` left out of the local run. CI on this PR is the reference run.
- The page has been seen rendering in a Windows build of the same change against a loopback demo gateway (reads only).

## Not verified

- No save has been exercised against a real Hermes gateway. Every write path is covered by tests against fakes only.
- Not run on an Android or Apple device.
- The translations have not been reviewed by native speakers.

title: fix(nextgen): change the default model and fallback rows on any listed provider
body:
## Problem

On 4.0.12 the NextGen Models page would not change the default model for many setups, and fallback rows could be added, moved or removed but not given another model.

- The default was read-only whenever its provider had an address saved with it that is not on the app's short reviewed list. A provider plugin (for example `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`, address `process://…`) always has one.
- Every named endpoint (`providers:` entries such as `gemini1`, `qwencloud-token-plan`) was unassignable everywhere on the page.

## Change

- Any provider the gateway lists under a `providers:` name can be chosen as the default, a fallback or a helper-task model. Only provider and model are sent; the gateway applies that provider's address and key.
- Tapping a fallback row gives it another model. Rows with routing details (`base_url`, `key_env`, `api_key`…) keep their model and can still be moved or removed.
- The default stays read-only unless its address is known to come back when its provider is chosen again (`DashboardClient.getMainModelEndpointOwnership`, fail-closed). Changeable: no saved address; a `providers:` entry at its own address; a legacy `custom_providers` entry at its address; a reviewed standard address (any case, spaces or trailing slash); the `process://<provider>` address a provider plugin registers. Read-only: unnamed endpoints (`custom`, `local`, `ollama`, `vllm`, `llama.cpp`… in any case), the host's `direct-config` row, a named endpoint at another address, and any address on a provider the app has no reviewed address for.
- Not offered anywhere: unnamed endpoints and the `custom:` rows the picker makes up for legacy entries (the fallback and helper-task resolvers do not accept every such slug).
- The classic model screen and `getMainModelRoute` are unchanged.

## Checks

- Host contract, run against the installed Hermes host's real routes (`caafe5389a`) in-process over disposable homes, network refused except loopback: named→named default switches write the target's own address and key pointer and drop the old ones; named→standard and back; legacy `custom:` rows; a bare `custom` default at a `providers:` entry's address is reported as `direct-config`; unknown models refused with nothing written; helper tasks and fallback rows on named providers save by name, and fallback rows resolve to their own address and key. The standard-provider leg used a validation seam (it needs the provider's network).
- The ownership check was fed the host's custom-endpoints answer for a real config with a `process://` plugin default: changeable.
- One code review of the first commit found a blocker (local-server names and capitalised `Custom` became changeable and would lose their address) and several should-fix items; all are addressed in the second commit with tests.
- `flutter analyze --no-pub --fatal-infos` clean; focused suites (catalogue, controller, page, l10n, classic model screen, theme guard) 139 passed; full suite run locally on the first commit (5,956 passed).
- Not run on a phone.

title: CI: flutter_tts native test fails intermittently downloading Robolectric's runtime jar
body:
## Description

`Native Android and Push Server` → **Android native regressions** fails intermittently in `:flutter_tts:testDebugUnitTest`, before any test logic runs:

```
FlutterTtsCorrelationTest > classMethod FAILED
    java.lang.AssertionError at MavenArtifactFetcher.java:129
        Caused by: java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException at AbstractFuture.java:292
            Caused by: java.io.IOException at HttpURLConnection.java:2059
```

`MavenArtifactFetcher` is Robolectric downloading the `android-all` runtime jar at test time. `HttpURLConnection.java:2059` is the HTTP-error path, so the download is being refused or dropped. A re-run of the failed job has passed every time.

## Occurrences

| Run | Trigger | Commit | Re-run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45391220311 | PR #347 | `67dd0ff` | passed |
| 45426276999 | push to `main` | `323f14b` | — |
| 45427855612 | push to `main` | `26a5eaa` | — |
| 45473301428 | push to `main` | `a3cbd08` | passed |
| 45476154458 | push to `main` | `215c4d4` | passed |

The last four were consecutive pushes to `main` (25 Nov). PR runs on the same trees passed.

## Likely cause

- The workflow caches Gradle (`setup-java` `cache: true`) and `~/.cache/hermes-voice`, but not Robolectric's runtime jars. Those are fetched by `MavenArtifactFetcher` into the local Maven repository at test time, so every run downloads them from Maven Central.
- #351 moved the app to Robolectric **4.18.1** (`android/app/build.gradle.kts`). `android/flutter-tts-patch.gradle` still adds **4.16** to the flutter_tts plugin. The two versions want different instrumented `android-all` jars, so each run now downloads two of them. That would explain the failure becoming frequent after #351 rather than occasional, as on #347 before it. Not proven.

## Fix options (smallest first)

1. Align `flutter-tts-patch.gradle` with the app's Robolectric version, so only one runtime jar is fetched.
2. Cache Robolectric's downloaded jars in `native-server.yml` (the local Maven repository path for `org/robolectric`), keyed on the Robolectric version.
3. Make the runtime jar a Gradle test dependency and run Robolectric offline (`robolectric.offline=true` with `robolectric.dependency.dir`), so Gradle's own cache covers it.

## Impact

CI noise only: release builds do not run this Gradle task, and no test has failed on its own logic. But a red `main` hides real native failures, and each occurrence costs a manual re-run.

title: Flaky: 'old push finalizer cannot clear newer ordinary single-flight' found no ChatScreen once in the v4.0.12 tag build
body:
## Description

`test/application_root_navigation_authority_test.dart` → **"old push finalizer cannot clear newer ordinary single-flight"** failed once, in the v4.0.12 tag build:

```
Expected: exactly one matching candidate
  Actual: _TypeWidgetFinder:<Found 0 widgets with type "ChatScreen": []>
#4  _Root.expectChat (test/application_root_navigation_authority_test.dart:299:7)
#5  main.<anonymous closure> (test/application_root_navigation_authority_test.dart:480:9)
```

So the final `f.expectChat(tester, 'shared')` found no chat after the newer ordinary tap's held list reply was released.

- Failed: Release run 45403593251, attempt 1, commit `2c9287b` (5,967 passed, 1 failed).
- Passed on the identical tree: PR Quality Checks 45398562144 and 45400802278, and the tag run's attempt 2.
- Passed 12 times out of 12 locally, run alone (`--plain-name`), on that commit.
- The test file has not changed since before v4.0.11, and nothing in v4.0.12 touched notification navigation.

## Two readings

1. **Test timing.** After `newer.complete()` the test waits for `listReplies == 2` (`_until`: 400 × 5 ms real time), then `_drain` (one 1 s pump plus 20 microtask rounds). On a slow runner the route push that follows the second list reply may land after the fixed drain. If so, the fix is to wait for the outcome, for example `_until(() => find.byType(ChatScreen, skipOffstage: false).evaluate().isNotEmpty)` with its own bound, before `expectChat`.
2. **A real race.** The test exists to prove that the old push tap's finalizer cannot clear the newer ordinary tap's single-flight. If, under some interleaving, the finalizer does clear it, the newer tap's navigation is dropped: in the app, a notification or chat tap that does nothing. One failure in many runs fits a race as well as slow timing.

## Suggested next step

Run the test in a loop under load (CPU-throttled, or with the rest of the suite running in parallel) and log, on failure, whether the second list reply arrived and whether a route push was requested after it. That tells the two readings apart before choosing a fix.

title: NextGen chat list shows oneshot/subagent runs as 'Untitled' chats; request exclude_sources like the Hermes desktop app
body:
## Summary

NextGen shows every automated run as an "Untitled" chat when the gateway has headless callers (`hermes chat --oneshot`, delegate subagents). They are always the most recently used rows, so they sit at the top of the chat list and push real conversations down. Ares already hides cron shells client-side, but not these sources.

## Setup

Ares 4.0.11 (Play Store), NextGen, Hermes dashboard over Tailscale. State DB had 2,154 sessions with `source='oneshot'` and ~600 with `source='subagent'` (an automation that calls `hermes chat -Q --oneshot` once per item), all with empty titles.

## Cause

`DashboardApiClient` requests `/api/sessions?limit=60&offset=0&order=recent&archived=exclude` and filters only cron on the client (`sources.isCronSession`, `Session.isUntitledCronShell`). It never sends `exclude_sources`, so `oneshot` and `subagent` rows are returned and shown. Hermes itself hides them: the server defines `INTERNAL_LISTING_SOURCES = ("kanban", "tool", "oneshot")` and `GET /api/sessions` accepts `exclude_sources` (comma-separated), which the official Hermes desktop app uses for its recents list (the route's own comment says the desktop splits recents `exclude=cron` from the cron section). In my setup the sessions do not appear in the official desktop app or in a third-party iOS Hermes client, only in Ares.

## Suggested fix

For the chat list (not the Crons section, not search), send `exclude_sources=oneshot,subagent,kanban,tool` (cron is already handled separately). Optionally add a toggle next to the existing "Show subagents" switch, default off. This avoids client-side filtering after the page arrives, so the page size issue from #297 does not come back.

## Workaround for now

A script archives `oneshot`/`subagent` sessions every few minutes (`hermes sessions archive --source oneshot --include-open --older-than 2m --yes`), which works but leaves a short window where they are visible.

Thanks, and thanks for the quick German fix in #359.

title: fix(nextgen): keep composer mic and send flush right on wide windows
body:
## What

On wide windows the NextGen composer's mic and send buttons sat in the middle of the bottom row instead of at the right edge. Reported on Windows; it also happens on macOS, Android tablets, and Android phones when the model label is short.

## Why

The row was `[attach, Flexible(model pill), Spacer, mic, send]`. A loose `Flexible` and a `Spacer` each get half the free width. When the pill's label is narrower than its half, the unused part ends up after the send button.

Measured on `main` (v4.0.14) at 1280×800, on both Windows and macOS: the send button's right edge was at 894dp against a composer edge of 1261dp. That is a 367dp gap with the default model label, 462dp with `gpt-5`, and 216dp with the 300dp docked sidebar.

## Fix

The pill is now `Expanded` wrapped in `Align(centerStart)`, and the `Spacer` is kept. The pill keeps the same size limit and position. Mic and send end at the composer's edge. Keys, tooltips, semantics and the `TextField` are unchanged, so the desktop ports' `SendOnEnter` wrapper still fits.

The Classic composer measured flush right with no overlap in every tested state, so it is not changed. It is covered by the new test.

## Tests

- New `test/desktop_composer_layout_test.dart` (40 cases). It pumps the real NextGen and Classic chat screens on Windows, macOS and Android, at phone/tablet/desktop sizes, at text scale 1.0 and 1.3, while idle, drafting, running and listening. It checks that send is flush right and that no control overlaps the text.
- Red on `main`: 19 failures, all "send not flush right". Green with this change.
- `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean. The 17 existing composer/NextGen test files (204 tests) pass.

Not verified on a real Windows or macOS build; the measurements are widget-test layout only.

title: fix(nextgen): hide one-shot, subagent, kanban and tool runs from the chat list
body:
Fixes #362.

## What

NextGen's chat list showed one-shot, subagent, kanban and tool runs as "Untitled" chats. It now asks the server to leave them out, the same way the Hermes desktop app does.

## How

- Every NextGen browse page, including Load more, sends `exclude_sources=oneshot,subagent,kanban,tool`. The server applies this before paging.
- **Show subagents is respected.** The stock backend re-admits subagents when the selected profile has `sessions.show_subagents` on (`hermes_cli/session_listing.py`). The app reads that setting with the same authenticated dashboard client (GET only, 3-second timeout).
  - **Setting off or missing:** subagents are hidden.
  - **Setting on:** they stay.
  - **Read fails or is unsupported:** whatever the server returned is kept, so the app never overrides a choice it couldn't read.
- **Older servers that ignore the filter:** the list still hides these runs, and its server cursor advances by raw rows. A page full of hidden runs can't stop real chats from loading (#297).
- **Crons:** switches to its own unfiltered read, and reopening the drawer keeps the Crons view.
- **Search** keeps its existing scope.

## Tests

- New `test/nextgen_machine_sources_test.dart` (14 tests). It uses the real NextGen model/sidebar and the production dashboard client, including a real loopback mTLS exchange.
- Red on `main`: 5 of 5 targeted cases fail.
- Targeted NextGen, paging and dashboard batch: 116 passed. `flutter analyze` is clean.
- The real backend list router was run against disposable stores. Show subagents off gives `[cron, human]`; on gives `[child, cron, human]`.

One extra profile config GET per browse refresh (not per page).

title: fix(ci): share one Robolectric version, cache its runtimes, and wait for real navigation in the root test
body:
Fixes #360 and #361. Two independent commits.

## #360: Robolectric runtime downloads in native CI

- The app used Robolectric 4.18.1, but the patched `flutter_tts` tests pulled 4.16. Both now read one `robolectricVersion` from `android/gradle.properties`, and dependency insight resolves 4.18.1 for both.
- Robolectric downloads its instrumented Android runtimes into `~/.m2`, outside Gradle's cache, so every CI run fetched them again. The native workflow now caches `~/.m2/repository/org/robolectric/android-all-instrumented`. The cache key covers the shared version and the test trees' SDK annotations.
- **Evidence:** I forced the native TTS task against a local origin returning HTTP 503.
  - With an empty repository it fails.
  - With only the cached subtree restored, all 10 tests pass and it makes zero requests.
- **Not proven:** the original CI failure's HTTP status was never retrieved. This reduces how often runs depend on the network; it isn't a diagnosis of that specific failure.
- `scripts/test_native_ci_config.py` guards the shared version and the cache step's placement.

## #361: notification navigation test

- No production change. The finalizer's exact-intent guard was already correct.
- The test asserted right after the second lookup reply arrived. Arriving doesn't mean the body was read, the continuation page fetched and the route pushed.
- With a held HTTP body, the old assertion fails deterministically with exactly the reported `Found 0 widgets with type "ChatScreen"`.
- The test now waits on the real client closure and the continuation, and keeps every existing assertion: 2 lookup clients, offsets `[0, 0, 50]`, and no `prompt.submit`.
- **Mutant check:** a production mutant that drops the finalizer's identity check still fails the strengthened test (3 lookup clients instead of 2).
- **Results:** 8 of 8 passes under CPU load. 72 passes across the three root-routing test files.

title: fix(gateway): fence Stop/Steer on the run's generation and replay canonical sessions by their own epoch (#84)
body:
Part of #84 (items 1–3 of the current-contract audit). Full durable recovery stays open in #84.

Against a current Hermes gateway (one that sends `session_authority`), three app bugs:

## 1. Stop and Steer name the run they target (NextGen and Classic)

Canonical `session.interrupt` / `session.steer` require `execution_generation`. Without it the gateway answers `stale_generation` / `invalid_params`.

- **Generation source:** the app tracks the newest generation per session from the resume/create snapshot, the submit receipt and event stamps.
- **When it's sent:** captured at the tap, and sent only on canonical connections. Legacy shapes are unchanged: the legacy dispatcher rejects the extra key with `4000 Extra inputs are not permitted`, which the captured fixture shows.
- **Failure handling:**
  - `stale_generation` says "the turn changed" and never retries against a newer run.
  - An unknown generation refuses locally without sending.
  - A steer that isn't `queued` shows as rejected and is never re-sent.

## 2. NextGen catch-up uses the session's own replay epoch

The app was sending the gateway's process epoch, so canonical replay always answered `snapshot_required` and incremental catch-up never worked.

- **Separate cursor:** a canonical cursor is now taken from the snapshot's `replay_epoch`/`last_sequence` and each frame's `replay_epoch`/`seq`, apart from the legacy cursor.
- **Exact request:** `session.events.since` sends `{session_id, replay_epoch, last_sequence}`. Only an exact, contiguous reply in the same epoch is accepted.
- **Bounded reload:** `snapshot_required`, truncation, a restart or a new stream does one bounded reload. The accepted watermark fences held frames.
- **Overflow and reconnect:** a `session.replay_gap` replays and then re-attaches, and a canonical reconnect replays before it resumes.

## 3. Foreground fallback reconciles

When replay failed while the chat looked busy, the app skipped the only repair, so a reply that finished in the background could stay missing. It now always reads the snapshot and keeps the live reply only while the *same* generation is still running. Nothing is ever re-sent.

## Tests

- **Fixture from the real backend:** `test/fixtures/canonical_replay_contract.json` is generated by `tools/capture_canonical_replay_fixture.py`. It runs the backend's own `SessionEvents`, `events_since`, interrupt/steer controls and legacy dispatcher in memory, with no services and sockets blocked.
- **New test files:**
  - `nextgen_canonical_controls`
  - `classic_canonical_controls` (real loopback WebSocket)
  - `nextgen_canonical_replay` and its parser test
  - `nextgen_foreground_catch_up` (real `NgMainPage` lifecycle)
- **Red on `main`:**

  | Area | Fail | Pass |
  |---|---|---|
  | Controls | 8 | 3 |
  | Replay | 7 | 0 |
  | Foreground | 3 | 0 |
  | Classic | 4 | 1 |

  The parser test doesn't compile on `main`, because the function didn't exist.
- **Green:** 23 targeted files, 385 tests. `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean.

## Server versions

These fields appear together from backend `v0.22.1`. Servers without `session_authority` take the unchanged legacy path.

## Still open in #84

- `durable-admission-v1` negotiation;
- a local receipt journal;
- `prompt.receipt`;
- unknown-state UI with user-confirmed `prompt.resolve_unknown`;
- consuming snapshot `pending`;
- keeping `session.create.request_id`.

title: feat(nextgen): Projects browser and a project picker on new chats (#304)
body:
Fixes #304, and adds a project picker when starting a new NextGen chat (Kyllene-style).

## NextGen Projects (#304)

- **More → Projects** reuses Classic's `ProjectsPane`, `ProjectDetailScreen` and `ProjectsRepository`, scoped to the selected connection and Hermes profile. It uses the same authenticated dashboard/socket, prefix and mTLS, with no new RPC.
- **Existing project chats** open in the normal NextGen chat. **New chats in a project** start in its folder; projects without a folder are refused. Server-folder settings stay a separate More row.

## Choosing the project when starting a chat

- **Where:** an empty, not-yet-created chat shows the project in the greeting as an accent pill with a chevron, like Kyllene's "What are we building in **herald** ⌄?". The menu lists Home plus the non-archived projects that have a folder.
- **Picking:** keeps the draft. Home clears the folder. Loading or having no projects never blocks typing.
- **Locking:** the pick locks before the first create, is disabled once the chat exists, and is fenced against profile or connection switches and late reads.
- **What's sent:** a deliberate pick sends `cwd` with `cwd_explicit: true`. Without that flag, current gateways let a named profile's `terminal.cwd` override the client folder (`tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`). Home sends neither.
- **Mismatch:** if the gateway runs the chat elsewhere (its `info.cwd`), the chat says so.
- **Uncertain creates** (timeout or malformed acknowledgement) are never retried automatically.

## Tests

- **New:** `test/nextgen_projects_test.dart`.
  - **Browse:** browsing and refreshing counts; opening an existing chat; a new chat starting in the project folder; projects with no folder; profile/connection switches while reads are held; cache isolation.
  - **Picker:** shown, hidden, Home, create races, uncertain create, a folder mismatch, and 320dp layouts in EN/DE/JA/RU.
  - **Transport:** a real loopback mTLS test.
- **Red:** red on `main` for the browser, and red on the browser commit for the picker.
- **Green:** 333 targeted tests pass, including `desktop_composer_layout_test`. `flutter analyze` is clean, and the new strings are in all 12 locales.

title: feat(composer): highlight slash commands and show their usage on tap
body:
## What

Typing a slash command in either compose box now highlights it straight away. Tapping the highlighted command shows a small card with its description and usage.

- **Classic** highlights exactly what its send path would run: `/new` and `/reset` (handled in the app), plus whatever the loaded `commands.catalog` makes executable. Before the catalogue loads, it uses the same `kSlashExecutableCommands` fallback as the send path, and the card shows "Loading commands…".
- **NextGen** gets a cached `commands.catalog` read, scoped per connection, profile and live session, used only for display. It's marked stale when the gateway reconnects, so newly added commands show up. If the read fails, the compose box works normally with no highlight.
- **Not highlighted:** paths like `/Users/sam`, slashes mid-sentence and unknown names.
- **The card:**
  - **Content:** the canonical name, an "alias of" line when an alias was typed, and the gateway's localised description. That description already includes "(usage: /name args)", so the separate argument hint only shows when no usage clause is present.
  - **Position and size:** at most 280dp wide, 6dp above the compose box, left-aligned to the command. It never covers the field or any control.
  - **Focus:** it never takes focus or closes the keyboard, and doesn't show while the command dropdown is open.
  - **Closing:** it closes on a tap anywhere, any edit, the caret leaving the command, focus loss, Esc, send, a chat switch, or after 8 seconds (no timeout with a screen reader on).
  - **Keyboard and screen reader:** moving the caret into the command opens it.
- **The text sent is unchanged.** `SlashCommandHighlightController` is a drop-in `TextEditingController` that only overrides `buildTextSpan`: value, selection, undo, input formatters, the IME composing underline and the desktop ports' `SendOnEnter` all behave as before.

NextGen still sends `/command` drafts as ordinary prompts in this PR, and the card says so. A follow-up PR makes NextGen run commands through `slash.exec`/`command.dispatch`, like Classic and Kyllene, and removes that note (`NgSlashCommandInfo.showsSentAsMessageNote`).

## Tests

- **New test files:**
  - `test/slash_command_highlight_test.dart`: spans for known, alias, unknown, path and mid-sentence commands; composing region kept; value unchanged; usage-clause detection.
  - `test/chat_composer_slash_highlight_test.dart`
  - `test/nextgen_slash_highlight_test.dart`
- **Widget tests:** highlight on typing, tap to show, each dismissal, dropdown open, catalogue not loaded, scoped NextGen fetch and fetch failure.
- **Placement tests:** 12 cases at phone 412×760 (Android) and 1280×800 (Windows, macOS), with one- and three-line drafts. They check with `getRect` that the card clears the field and every control and is at most 280dp wide.
- **Red on `main`:** 12 of 14 widget tests fail. The 2 that pass are the negative cases.
- **Red on the first revision:** all 12 placement tests fail (360dp wide; it covered the controls).
- **Green:** 188 slash and compose box tests (including `desktop_composer_layout_test`), 263 NextGen tests, and 56 in the new files. `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean, and the new strings are in every locale.

Not run on a device; this is widget-test evidence.

title: feat(nextgen): run slash commands through the gateway like Classic and Kyllene
body:
**Merge after #303 and #369.** This branch contains both, so its diff shrinks once they land.

## What

NextGen now runs slash commands through the gateway, the way Classic and Kyllene do. Before, NextGen sent `/help` to the model as ordinary text: `prompt.submit` has no slash handling, and commands only run through `slash.exec` / `command.dispatch`.

## Behaviour

- **Which drafts run:** the same rule the highlight (#369) uses, from the connection and profile's `commands.catalog` (aliases via `canon`, skills, plugin commands). If the catalogue hasn't loaded, a send waits up to 2 seconds, then uses Classic's `kSlashExecutableCommands` fallback. Unknown `/words`, paths, mid-sentence slashes and drafts with attachments still go out as normal prompts.
- **Handled in the app:** `/new` and `/reset` start a new chat, `/stop` stops the running turn, and a bare `/model` opens the model sheet.
- **Everything else** runs on the gateway:
  - **Calls:** `slash.exec {session_id, command}` with NextGen's profile scoping. It falls back to `command.dispatch {session_id, name, arg}` only after a definite refusal: #303's `unsupported_command` rules, plus the gateway's explicit pre-execution 4018 "use command.dispatch for /x" for skills and `/snapshot restore` (`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`).
  - **Results:**
    - Output and warnings show on a collapsible command card in the chat.
    - An alias is followed once.
    - `send`/`skill` results go out as a normal prompt showing the gateway's `display`, never `message`.
    - `prefill` fills the compose box only if you haven't typed since, then the transcript reloads.
- **A lost reply** (timeout or dropped socket) never falls back or resends, because both methods reach the same executor and the first may already have run. The card says the command may still be running, and the draft comes back.
- **Older gateways without `slash.exec`:** the line goes out as a prompt, and that connection stops trying until it reconnects.
- **During a running turn**, commands still go to the gateway, and its answer or refusal is shown.
- The highlight card's "sent as a normal message" note is now off.

## Tests

- New: `test/nextgen_slash_exec_test.dart` (20 widget), `nextgen_slash_exec_unit_test.dart` (12) and `nextgen_slash_exec_wire_test.dart` (4 real-socket tests checking the profile scope on each call). They cover:
  - `/help` output;
  - refusal falling back to dispatch, and the 4018 redirect;
  - skill send with display text, and prefill;
  - alias;
  - the local commands;
  - unknown words and paths staying prompts;
  - timeout with no fallback or resend;
  - method-not-found falling back to a prompt;
  - a command during a running turn.
- Red on the highlight base: 19 failures, 1 expected pass (the unknown-word control).
- Classic's refusal checks moved into a shared file unchanged; Classic's slash tests still pass.
- 523 targeted tests pass, and `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean.

## Limits

- Not run against a live gateway or on a device.
- `/new <title>` ignores the title, as Kyllene does.
- Command cards live only in the open chat view, so a full transcript reload drops older ones.

title: fix(notifications): stop re-alerting questions and approvals answered on another device
body:
## What

When Hermes asked a question or needed a command approved and it was answered on another device (for example Ares on Windows), the Android app kept notifying "Hermes has a question" and the yellow "needs you" highlight kept coming back.

## Causes

- **NextGen:** a cancelled request was cleared only from the chat that was open on this device, and a request missing from the server's list of open requests was never removed. The yellow highlight therefore stuck, and every trip to the background re-posted every cached request.
- **Classic:** "Input needed" / "Approval needed" notifications were never taken down, and each reconnect posted a new one for the same request.
- **Android push:** the phone treated the server's "question answered" hint (`input_resolved`) as new activity. It posted a second notification and left the original up. The server hint also didn't say which question it answered.

## Fix

- **Server list is authoritative:** the gateway's `open_requests` (from `session.resume` / `session.events.since`) now decides what's still open. A request it no longer lists, or one the server cancels, is removed and its notification taken down, whichever chat is open.
- **One notification per open request:** going to the background posts nothing new for requests already notified or already settled.
- **Classic:** takes down its own input/approval notifications when the request settles.
- **Socket drop:** the notification stays up. When the same request comes back after the reconnect it is updated in place, silently, so its Approve/Deny buttons still work. It is taken down only when the server cancels it, it's answered here, the turn ends, or a read that started after the drop no longer lists it.
- **Android push:** `input_resolved` cancels the matching `input` notification and posts nothing, including on older servers whose hint lacks the request fields. The push companion now includes the session and request in the resolved hint.
- **Nothing is answered or resent** on the user's behalf.

## Platforms

The highlight fix applies everywhere, since the Dart code is shared. Only Android (local and push) and iOS (local, until iOS suspends the app) post these notifications. Windows, macOS and Linux post none.

## Backend findings (read-only)

The older gateway doesn't send a cancel to other devices when one answers; its list of open requests is the only signal. The newer session-authority gateway does send one to every attached device. `on_human_input_resolved` fires whoever answered.

## Tests

- **New:**
  - `test/nextgen_remote_answered_request_test.dart`
  - `test/nextgen_remote_answered_catch_up_test.dart`
  - `test/desktop_gateway_remote_answered_request_test.dart`
  - `test/normal_gateway_remote_answered_request_test.dart`
  - `MobilePushInputResolvedTest.kt`
  - a push companion outbox test
- **Red on `main` before the fix.** The kept-across-drop behaviour was also checked by breaking the code and watching the tests fail.
- **Green on the merged head:**
  - `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean.
  - 246 targeted tests pass (the new files plus notification, push, root-routing, NextGen and desktop-gateway).
  - 49/49 native `MobilePush*` tests and 217 push-companion pytest pass.

## Limits

- No real two-device test.
- On the newer gateway, a request answered while this phone was offline stays as a silent notification for chats that aren't open, until the app returns to the foreground. It never alerts again.
- Classic's older chat-screen prompt path still doesn't take down its own notifications.

feat(nextgen): suggest slash commands in a box above the composer
body:
## What

Typing `/` in the NextGen compose box now opens a box of suggested commands above it, narrowing as you type, like Hermes desktop, Kyllene and Ares Classic.

## Behaviour

- **The box:** sits above the composer and never covers the field or its buttons. About 6 rows, scrollable, at most 420 dp wide, NextGen styling, skills marked "Skill".
- **Sources:**
  - **Bare `/`:** the cached `commands.catalog`.
  - **Typing more:** `complete.slash` (debounced 120 ms, scoped to the chat's session or profile). Stale replies to older typing are ignored.
  - **Fallback:** if `complete.slash` fails or is missing, the catalogue is filtered instead, and an old gateway is remembered per connection.
  - **Always offered:** the local `/new` `/reset` `/stop` `/model` when they match. Only commands a send would actually run are listed.
  - **Arguments:** argument completions (`replace_from`) are supported, e.g. `/personality al` → `alice`.
- **Accepting:** tap or click, or Up/Down then Enter or Tab. Fills the composer with a trailing space, keeps focus and the keyboard open, and never sends.
- **Enter on a fully typed command** (e.g. `/help`) closes the box and lets Enter send it.
- **Closing:** Esc, Back, tapping elsewhere, deleting the slash, or a space after the name. Android Back closes the box before it can open the sidebar (`main_page.dart` asks the box first).
- **Info card:** the slash info card (#369) stays hidden while the box is open. A tap or caret move never opens the box, so tapping a command token still shows its card.
- **Desktop ports:** the box handles keys on the field itself, before the Windows/Apple `SendOnEnter` wrapper, and swallows the key-up and repeats of an Enter it uses. A test with a SendOnEnter-style wrapper covers this.

## Tests

- **New:**
  - `test/nextgen_slash_suggestions_test.dart`: 18 widget tests, all failing on `main` before the change.
  - `test/nextgen_slash_suggestions_wire_test.dart`: 5 tests over a real local socket, checking the profile on `complete.slash` and that an old gateway is remembered per connection.
- **Gates:**
  - 566 across all `nextgen_*`, `slash_command_*` and `desktop_composer_layout`. The existing highlight tests are unchanged.
  - After merging `main` with #373: 172 targeted tests pass and `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` is clean.

## Limits

- An unsent new chat's picked project folder isn't passed to `complete.slash`, so its project-local skills follow the profile.
- The backend completer's reply shape was read from source rather than run locally.

title: Add parked Android Automotive support on the existing Ares Play listing
body:
## One listing; separate Automotive and phone releases

The mobile and parked Android Automotive OS (AAOS) bundles use `com.hermesagent.hermes_android`. The car bundle alone requires Automotive hardware and API 33+, enforces parked-only UI, and uses `1_000_000_000 + pubspec base` for a distinct version code. The sideloadable debug preview retains its separate `.automotive.preview` ID. Android Auto notifications and replies remain in the phone build.

## Verified

- [Build-only run for the final head](https://github.com/rusty4444/ares/actions/runs/45556746745): the car job passed, mobile publishing job skipped. The downloaded Actions ZIP checksum, source SHA, AAB checksum, base manifest, signing integrity and pinned upload certificate were checked independently. The same-listing AAB is **4.0.16 / 1000003072**. SHA-256 `7195c81658faf0137c6e88fc0565cba79be3e355e9437e98d3a88122adf4e66b`.
- On `00655838`, 6,312 phone tests, 10 parked-mode tests and 2 Play distribution tests passed, zero failed or skipped. The final follow-up (`71238585`) changes only the verifiers/tests, build workflow and local build instructions; the Android/Flutter app and Flutter test sources are byte-identical. Cross-track, expired/future certificate and wrong-signer rejections now run before signing. Local car builds use a separate worktree to avoid overwriting staged phone artifacts.
- The debug preview was exercised on an API 35 Automotive emulator: a typed chat and streamed local-fixture reply, system driving lockout, blocked relaunch and restoration after parking. No physical vehicle or Google Play installation is claimed.
- The certificate ownership regression waits for the real account mutation queue, checks the physical identity directories and staging state, then verifies fresh mTLS and unrelated-key removal.

## Publication boundary

The build workflow has no Play upload or release operation. Google Play did not have `automotive:production` on the last successful read; the mobile release was separately in review. **Do not upload the car AAB to mobile production, restart a phone review or create a second listing.** Confirm a supported car category or an applicable Google partner approval before enrolling the existing listing for AAOS and submitting. See `docs/parked-automotive.md`.

title: NextGen: dock the sessions sidebar on wide windows (tablet landscape, car)
body:
## What this changes

NextGen now docks the sessions sidebar beside the chat on expanded windows, instead of always using a modal drawer:

- **Expanded (840 dp and wider, at least 480 dp tall):** the sidebar stays visible on the left. This covers tablet landscape, unfolded foldables and Android Automotive in both car profiles: 1024×768 landscape and 800×1280 portrait at about 1067 dp. The chat header's sidebar button collapses and restores it.
- **Compact and medium:** unchanged. Phones, short landscape phones and small tablets keep the drawer.
- Search, filter and scroll survive crossing the breakpoint, because the same sidebar `State` moves between drawer and dock through a `GlobalKey`.

The breakpoints and layout follow the Apple port (`feat/apple-port`, `abc94121`). `lib/core/utils/adaptive_layout.dart` is byte-identical to that branch, and the `main_page.dart` build logic matches it apart from the desktop keyboard shortcuts, so merging the port later stays straightforward. No other port changes are included.

## Verification

- `test/nextgen_docked_sidebar_test.dart`: breakpoints, drawer on compact windows, docking at car-landscape size, collapse and restore, and search state across the breakpoint.
- The parked Automotive debug build ran on the generic AAOS emulator against the loopback demo gateway. The 1024×768 landscape and 800×1280 portrait profiles both docked the sidebar, with no clipping. Collapse and restore worked.
- Full phone, parked and Play test runs are reported in the comments.

title: NextGen: handle car replies for missing/new sessions (4.0.16)
body:
Upstream 4.0.16 handles Android Auto replies for **existing sessions** only. A reply on the "new chat" entry, or on a session that no longer exists, is dropped.

This branch adds a small, additive hook:

- `AutoMessagingService` gets an optional `onNewChatReply(connection, text)` callback, invoked when `_lookup` finds no session and the action is a `reply`.
- `HermesAppState` wires it to a `pendingNextGenVoiceReply` notifier.
- `MainPage` opens a fresh NextGen chat and sends the text via `NgChatController.send()`.
- `ChatScreen` keeps an `initialVoiceReply` path for the Classic interface.

No changes to the native Auto architecture (`AutoMessagingPlugin`, `HermesAutoNotifications`, `AutoMessageReceiver`) — the token-based flow is untouched.

Full technical notes: https://wiki.kooreman.local/procedures/ares-fork-technisch (internal wiki; happy to paste the relevant parts here).

Build used locally: 4.0.16+3070028 (arm64 30700282), signed with our own release key.
